item.title: [TSN] Dodgers' Ohtani admits he won't be fully healthy in playoffs
item.dc:creator: Alden Gonzalez
item.description: LOS ANGELES -- Dodgers’ two-way star Shohei Ohtani called the past few days “very productive” and believes his swing is “in a better place” heading into a National League Division Series showdown against the Braves that begins Saturday. But Ohtani won’t be fully healthy then and perhaps at any point this postseason. The left knee and right biceps ailments that compromised him throughout the summer will linger into the fall, Ohtani and Dodgers manager Dave Roberts indicated Friday. “As of now, it
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES -- Dodgers’ two-way star Shohei Ohtani called the past few days “very productive” and believes his swing is “in a better place” heading into a National League Division Series showdown against the Braves that begins Saturday.
But Ohtani won’t be fully healthy then and perhaps at any point this postseason. The left knee and right biceps ailments that compromised him throughout the summer will linger into the fall, Ohtani and Dodgers manager Dave Roberts indicated Friday.
“As of now, it’s something I’m just going to have to manage,” Ohtani said through an interpreter.
Knee and biceps injuries finally sent Ohtani to the injured list in early September after a 14-game stretch during which he compiled seven hits and 22 strikeouts. Ohtani returned with five regular-season games left and was inconsistent, putting together an encouraging stretch against the San Diego Padres and an overwhelming one against the San Francisco Giants.
Ohtani took batting practice on the field during workouts Tuesday and Wednesday, a rarity for him, and Dodgers hitting coach Aaron Bates said those sessions were “as good as we’ve seen it this year as far as the way the ball was coming off and the way he was getting his move off.”
Bates provided some proof of that.
“He did hit a couple balls up off the scoreboard,” he said.
Ohtani also had three plate appearances against Yoshinobu Yamamoto in a prolonged simulated game Wednesday, worked out inside Thursday and came onto the field for three rounds of outdoor batting practice around 6 p.m. PT Friday. Moments later, he had two at-bats against right-hander Emmet Sheehan, striking out before hitting a line drive to right field.
“Shohei’s not 100%, but he’s going to be in the lineup,” Roberts said, adding that veteran first baseman Freddie Freeman also isn’t fully healthy, among others. “I think that most players that are performing now are not 100%. Obviously with Shohei, it’s a bigger deal because of the player, but there’s a lot of players that are not 100%, and they’ve just got to manage it.”
Despite being compromised for much of the past three months, Ohtani finished the year batting .275/.377/.512 with 30 home runs and 11 stolen bases and is likely to finish second to Chicago Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong in NL MVP voting. Ohtani also went 8-2 with a 1.79 ERA in 14 starts, but he didn’t pitch after July 3 and had essentially been ruled out of pitching by Labor Day. Ohtani went on the IL thereafter.
“During the IL, I pretty much knew I wasn’t going to pitch the rest of the season,” Ohtani said. “So I did focus on just the hitting aspect of the game and coming to understanding and wanting to execute and try new things when I came back. So those were the things that I really took the IL time to think through what I wanted to try when I was back in action.”
Ohtani had several hard-hit balls upon returning from the injured list, notably an opposite-field double off a 103 mph fastball from star Padres closer Mason Miller. But Ohtani ultimately went 5-for-21 with eight strikeouts in his last five regular-season games, and by the end, Roberts noticed him being overanxious, trying too hard to get acclimated to major league pitching with limited time.
The 32-year-old Ohtani said he still has to make “little tweaks here and there” with his swing before feeling ready for Game 1.
He downplayed having limited playing time before then.
“Whether I have a lot of at-bats or not, I can figure out how I feel, especially in my setup,” Ohtani said. “So that’s something I was able to kind of see. But I do want to get into the postseason, feel the atmosphere and again kind of recalibrate what I have to.”

item.content:encoded:
Por problemas de lesión
Shohei Ohtani sigue siendo cuestionante para los Dodgers
**Ohtani llega a los playoffs con molestias y Dodgers abren ante Braves**
LOS ÁNGELES.— Shohei Ohtani llega a la postemporada todavía tratando de convivir con las molestias que lo alejaron del montículo después del Juego de Estrellas y que lo llevaron por primera vez a la lista de lesionados de los Dodgers de Los Ángeles.
El japonés no tiene claro todavía el origen de las molestias en el bíceps derecho, la rodilla izquierda y el cuello, situación que deberá ser evaluada con mayor profundidad durante la temporada muerta.
“Hasta ahora no he podido comprender bien la causa fundamental de todo esto, así que creo que ese proceso tendrá lugar durante la temporada baja, cuando tenga un poco más de tiempo para abordarlo. Por ahora, es algo que simplemente tendré que manejar”, explicó Ohtani el viernes a través de un intérprete.
El estelar jugador de dos vías regresó de la lista de lesionados cuando restaban apenas cinco partidos de la serie regular y bateó de 21-5, con ocho ponches, una base por bolas y un doble.
Ohtani, sin embargo, aseguró que se siente mejor y que su swing está recuperando su ritmo.
“Mi cuerpo se siente muy bien en general. Siento que mi swing está en un mejor lugar, se siente fluido. Solo algunos pequeños ajustes aquí y allá y estaré listo”, manifestó.
Los Dodgers comenzarán este sábado la Serie Divisional de la Liga Nacional contra los Bravos de Atlanta, en el primer paso en busca de su tercer campeonato consecutivo de la Serie Mundial.
El dirigente Dave Roberts no quiso adelantar qué versión de Ohtani podrá ofrecer en la postemporada, aunque confía en que pueda responder cuando llegue el momento.
“Espero cosas buenas. Realmente lo hago. Simplemente no lo hemos visto lo suficiente como para pronosticarlo”, señaló Roberts.
### Braves llegan con rotación golpeada
Mientras los Dodgers han tenido cinco días para descansar y preparar la Serie Divisional, Atlanta llega a Los Ángeles después de eliminar a los Filis de Filadelfia en tres partidos de la Serie de Comodines.
La situación de su rotación es uno de los principales temas antes del inicio de la serie.
Chris Sale, su as, lanzó los últimos cuatro outs del tercer partido ante Filadelfia con apenas un día de descanso. Había realizado 95 lanzamientos en el primer encuentro de esa serie, por lo que todavía no está definido si podrá abrir el segundo partido ante los Dodgers.
Además, los Bravos descartaron para esta serie a los abridores Martín Pérez, por molestias en la espalda, y Bryce Elder, por un problema en la rodilla.
El dirigente Walt Weiss reconoció que el bullpen podría asumir una carga importante, especialmente durante los primeros partidos.
“Hay una posibilidad de que tengamos que lanzar muchas entradas con nuestro bullpen, especialmente en los primeros dos partidos”, dijo Weiss.
### El calor también juega
A la exigencia del playoff se suma el intenso calor que afecta a Los Ángeles.
Para el primer partido, programado para la tarde del sábado, se pronostica una temperatura máxima de 100 grados Fahrenheit, unos 38 grados Celsius, muy por encima del promedio de 81 grados para esta época del año.
El domingo tampoco habrá mucho alivio, con una temperatura proyectada de 99 grados Fahrenheit.
Tarik Skubal será el abridor de los Dodgers en el primer partido, mientras que los lanzadores de ambos equipos deberán lidiar con unas condiciones poco habituales para un partido de octubre.
El récord de temperatura durante un partido en el Dodger Stadium es de 103 grados Fahrenheit, registrado en dos ocasiones: durante el primer partido de la Serie Mundial de 2017 contra Houston y en un encuentro de temporada regular ante Cleveland en 2024.

item.title: [The Sporting Tribune] Tarik Skubal named Game 1 starter as Shohei Ohtani provides health update

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — With less than 24 hours before the first pitch of Game 1 of the NLDS, Dodgers manager Dave Roberts made his decision: Tarik Skubal will take the ball Saturday afternoon against the Braves.
The choice came from a rotation that gives the Dodgers perhaps as much depth as any team could ask for. Skubal earned the assignment over reigning World Series MVP Yoshinobu Yamamoto, fellow two-time Cy Young Award winner Blake Snell and All-Star right-hander Tyler Glasnow.
“With the four guys, it doesn't really matter who, but I think that we feel good about Tarik taking the baseball tomorrow afternoon,” Roberts said.
As it turns out, Skubal knew his assignment before the regular season was even over.
When Roberts pulled him after just 75 pitches in his final start in San Francisco, Skubal initially wondered why. He approached his manager, expecting there might be another reason for the early exit.
Instead, Roberts gave him a message that changed the rest of his week.
“He came and shook my hand. I was at kind of a low pitch count, I thought in the moment I was going to be able to finish the game. And he was like, ‘Get ready for Game 1,’” Skubal said.
Skubal said he was “obviously excited and fired up and ready to go.”
Now comes a new experience for the reigning back-to-back unanimous Cy Young winner.
For everything Skubal has accomplished, he has never had the opportunity to pitch at home in October. That changes Saturday, when he takes the mound in front of a Dodgers crowd for the opening game of the NLDS.
“I’m excited for the opportunity to throw in front of the fans,” Skubal said.
The left-hander also knows exactly what the atmosphere can feel like when he pitched for the Tigers.
“Usually when I walk out onto the field in a playoff game, it's usually received with a lot of boos,” Skubal said. “So I'm excited to get some cheers in there for us. And to pitch at home, I think it's going to be a ton of fun in front of this atmosphere.”
His approach for the biggest start of his Dodgers career?
Keep it simple.
“I have to be really good at what makes me good,” Skubal said.
The weather will provide another challenge, with triple-digit temperatures expected Saturday. Skubal, however, doesn't appear particularly concerned.
“We probably won't have to go to the bathroom. Just sweat it out,” he joked.
The extra time between starts has also been welcomed by the left-hander.
“I think for a starter, it's easiest to take time off,” Skubal said.
He also credited Dodgers fans for the reception he has received since arriving in Los Angeles and said he is looking forward to finally pitching in front of them in October.
“I’m excited to throw in front of them tomorrow.”
Ohtani Says His Swing Is Trending in the Right Direction
While Skubal prepares for his first postseason start at Dodger Stadium, Shohei Ohtani is preparing to return to October action after recently being activated from the 15-day injured list.
Ohtani said he feels really good overall and believes his swing has benefited from the extended break.
“I do feel like my swing is in a better place,” Ohtani said. “Just little tweaks here and there, and I’ll be ready for tomorrow.”
The time away from games, he said, has given him an opportunity to make adjustments while managing the ailments that surfaced during the second half.
“Being on the IL has taught me a lot,” Ohtani said.
But the Dodgers' star acknowledged that his lingering biceps and knee issues remain something he will have to manage throughout the postseason.
Asked whether those injuries could require attention during the offseason, Ohtani said he has not yet identified the root cause of everything he has been dealing with.
“I haven't been able to get a good grasp of the root cause of all this,” Ohtani said. “I think that process is going to happen during the off-season when I'm going to have a little bit more time to be able to address it. But as of now, it's something I'm just going to have to manage.”
That reality isn't unique to Ohtani.
Roberts said most of the players currently preparing for the postseason are dealing with some level of physical issue.
“Most players that are performing now are not at 100%,” Roberts said.
Still, Roberts expects Ohtani to perform well when the Dodgers open their series Saturday. He also expressed confidence in Freddie Freeman, whose own lingering injuries have been a storyline heading into October, particularly after seeing Freeman in Thursday's intrasquad game.
The Dodgers will enter the NLDS with a roster expected to feature 14 position players and 12 pitchers, according to Roberts. He was not yet ready to announce the starters for Games 2 and 3.
For now, the focus belongs to Skubal.
The Dodgers acquired him to pitch in moments exactly like this one. On Saturday, in front of a home crowd and with the season entering its most important stretch, he gets the opportunity to show what he can do.
And unlike his previous playoff outings in opposing ballparks, this time, the cheers will be for him.

item.content:encoded:
Shohei Ohtani Gives Injury Update Before Dodgers vs. Braves MLB Playoff Series Amid Arm, Knee Issues
Los Angeles Dodgers superstar Shohei Ohtani provided a positive update to reporters regarding ailments in his left knee (inflammation, soreness, lingering pain) and right biceps (discomfort, pain) on Friday, one day before L.A. will host the Atlanta Braves for Game 1 of the National League Division Series.
Ohtani hasn't pitched since July 3 due to the issues, but he's largely remained in the batting lineup, hitting .275 (.889 OPS) with 30 home runs and 81 RBI in 135 games.
TOP NEWS
Stanton Ready to Pinch Hit
Report: Judge's Status 'Up in the Air'
Braves-Dodgers NLDS Preview 📖
Ohtani was placed on the injured list in September due to knee and biceps issues. He was out from Sept. 8-22 but returned for his team's final five regular-season games.
A big question remains about whether Ohtani, who has managed these ailments for months, will need further medical attention this offseason.
The knee issue first arose on June 11, when he left a game against the Pittsburgh Pirates. Ohtani was removed from his July 3 start against the San Diego Padres due to the right biceps issue.
In the meantime, Ohtani may have benefited from five days of rest this week after the Dodgers, the National League's No. 2 playoff seed, bypassed the Wild Card Round.
Ohtani clearly feels good right now based on his comments, and we'll see how he fares soon enough when L.A. faces Atlanta for its 4 p.m. ET matchup.

item.title: [New York Post] Dodgers hope Shohei Ohtani is better –– but are ‘not so sure’ what to expect in playoffs
item.dc:creator: Jack Harris
item.description: When it comes to Shohei Ohtani’s health, the Dodgers have plenty of hope — but few precise expectations. That, at least, was the way manager Dave Roberts framed his superstar’s status on the eve of the National League Division Series on Friday, saying he was hopeful Ohtani would play well after battling right arm and left knee injuries during the second half of the season, but also acknowledging that he was “not so sure” about exactly what the slugger would be able to provide. “I know that once
item.content:encoded:
When it comes to Shohei Ohtani’s health, the Dodgers have plenty of hope — but few precise expectations.
That, at least, was the way manager Dave Roberts framed his superstar’s status on the eve of the National League Division Series on Friday, saying he was hopeful Ohtani would play well after battling right arm and left knee injuries during the second half of the season, but also acknowledging that he was “not so sure” about exactly what the slugger would be able to provide.
“I know that once the lights turn on, the postseason starts, [his] focus will be heightened,” Roberts said. “I expect good things. I really do. We just haven’t seen it enough really for me to forecast it.”
While addressing reporters on Friday for the first time since before going on the injured list in mid-September — when his injuries had become so bad he was showing visible signs of pain at the plate — Ohtani insisted his ailments had “gotten much better” and that the past few days had been “productive” for his previously slumping swing.
“I think my swing has gotten better,” he said in Japanese. “If I can make solid adjustments today, I think I can go into tomorrow in sufficient condition.”
However, Roberts also reiterated that the four-time MVP is “not 100%” following an 11-for-70 slump in his final 18 games of the regular season (the last five of which came after he returned from the IL last week).
Ohtani, meanwhile, described his injuries as something he will have to continue to manage during the playoffs, unsure if further treatment will be needed in the offseason.
During the Japanese portion of his news conference, he even revealed that, during his stint on the injured list, he avoided holding his young daughter with his aching right arm.
“I was able to hold my daughter using my left arm,” he said.
“The physical part, I think, he’s kind of moving past that,” hitting coach Aaron Bates said. “Now it’s just gaining the timing of different speeds and when he wants to get his move off, that sort of thing. Kind of the usual stuff that hitters go through, as opposed to trying to cheat [to pitches] because the physical components are limiting them.”
During the club’s bye week workouts, Ohtani took batting practice on the field multiple times — typically a rarity for him — and even sent a couple balls nearly to the outfield scoreboards, according to Bates.
“It was as good as I’ve seen it this year,” Bates said, “as far as just the way the ball was coming off [the bat].”
He also got live at-bats in the team’s intrasquad scrimmages, including a couple matchups against Yoshinobu Yamamoto on Wednesday.
“Yoshi won the matchup,” Roberts joked, but Ohtani at the very least didn’t strike out.
Whether that will be enough for Ohtani to truly turn the corner, however, remains to be seen.
For the one intrasquad scrimmage reporters were allowed to observe on Thursday, Ohtani was nowhere to be seen (staying back in the clubhouse and indoor batting cages to get his work in instead).
Ohtani himself also failed to offer much of an expectation for how he might perform this October, saying only: “I think I can get closer to the results I want if I can adjust to the atmosphere of the postseason.”
For now, such hopes will have to suffice.
Only when Game 1 of the NLDS begins on Saturday afternoon will Ohtani and the Dodgers know exactly where he is at.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Shohei Ohtani Breaks Silence on Injury, Andrew Friedman's Comments and More Before NLDS vs Braves
item.dc:creator: Noah Camras; Unknown

Since last speaking to reporters, Ohtani had his first stint on the injured list as a Dodger. He also returned for five games before the end of the regular season, going 5-for-21 with eight strikeouts. Ohtani is dealing with lingering injuries to his knee, biceps and neck. Here's what he
item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers superstar Shohei Ohtani spoke to reporters for the first time since Sept. 7 on Friday, one day before the start of the team's National League Division Series matchup with the Atlanta Braves.
Since last speaking to reporters, Ohtani had his first stint on the injured list as a Dodger. He also returned for five games before the end of the regular season, going 5-for-21 with eight strikeouts.
Ohtani is dealing with lingering injuries to his knee, biceps and neck. Here's what he had to say about his various ailments, through interpreter Will Ireton.
"It feels really good overall," Ohtani said. "I do feel like my swing is in a better place, feels smooth and just a little tweaks here and there, and I'll be ready for tomorrow."
Ohtani said he had a "very productive time" during the five-day layoff, "getting live at-bats, live [batting practice] and simulated games, and having a good amount of time to recover."
Ohtani was also asked if he'd have to address the injuries in the offseason, potentially in the form of surgery.
“I haven't been able to get a good grasp of the root cause of all this," he said. "I think that process is going to happen during the offseason when I'm going to have a little bit more time to be able to address it. But as of now, it's something I'm just going to have to manage."
Overall, Ohtani appeared in 135 games as a batter this season, hitting .275 with 30 home runs, 80 RBIs and an OPS of .889. In the second half of the season, he hit .245 with an OPS of .772 across 47 games.
Ohtani's last pitching appearance came on July 3. He attempted to return to pitching in August, but was ultimately shut down before going on the IL.
"During the IL I pretty much knew I wasn't going to pitch the rest of the season. So I did focus on just the hitting aspect of the game and coming to understanding and wanting to execute and try new things when I came back," Ohtani said. "So those were the things that I really took the IL time to think through what I wanted to try when I was back in action."
Shohei Ohtani Addresses Andrew Friedman's Comments About Lack of Communication
Finally, Ohtani was asked about comments from president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman, who said the organization's communication with the two-way star was "not as awesome" at times this year in terms of "fully sharing exactly how he’s feeling."
"I think the discussion became more about like what's best for the team," Ohtani said. "Is it something that I can play through, and if that's best for the team, sure. But I think we both came to an understanding where the decision to be on the IL came from the fact that it's probably best for the team for me to recover and be able to focus on the postseason."
As for why he wants to play through his injuries?
"Just overall, I do pride myself on playing every day. I do see it as an obligation as a professional to be on the field every single day. Just being on the IL has taught me a lot, and that's something that I'm just take it as I go."

item.title: [Field Level Media] Dodgers not talking 3-peat yet as Braves enter NLDS with confidence
item.description: LOS ANGELES — The potential road to history for the Los Angeles Dodgers begins with a reunion as the National League Division Series starts Saturday afternoon with a visit from the Atlanta Braves. Freddie Freeman has been a major postseason contributor during the Dodgers’ consecutive World Series titles, and the veteran will be in the heart of the order again in a matchup against his former team. Freeman also was invaluable in the 2021 World Series when the Braves won their most recent title. Fr
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — The potential road to history for the Los Angeles Dodgers begins with a reunion as the National League Division Series starts Saturday afternoon with a visit from the Atlanta Braves.
Freddie Freeman has been a major postseason contributor during the Dodgers’ consecutive World Series titles, and the veteran will be in the heart of the order again in a matchup against his former team.
Freeman also was invaluable in the 2021 World Series when the Braves won their most recent title. Freeman joined the Dodgers as a free agent in 2022 after Atlanta moved on to Matt Olson as their first baseman.
While Freeman has won three rings in five seasons, the Dodgers are trying to become the first National League club to win championships in three consecutive years. Only two American League franchises have ever done it: the New York Yankees and Oakland Athletics.
The Yankees were the last to accomplish the feat when they won championships in 1998, 1999 and 2000.
“We don’t need to be adding any extra pressure onto ourselves,” Dodgers third baseman Max Muncy said. “We’ve been saying that for a long time. When you talk about three-peating, you’re putting that extra pressure on it that doesn’t need to be there. Winning a World Series is already hard enough as it is.”
After returning from a biceps injury during the final week of the regular season, Shohei Ohtani will be back atop the Los Angeles order when the club’s postseason run begins.
Left-hander Tarik Skubal was named the Dodgers’ Game 1 starter over right-hander Yoshinobu Yamamoto. Skubal arrived just before the trade deadline in a deal with the Detroit Tigers and went 5-2 with a 2.61 ERA in 10 starts for his new club.
Skubal is 0-1 with a 4.91 ERA in two career starts against Atlanta, including an outing in April when he gave up two runs over seven innings in a no-decision.
The Braves opened their postseason by getting past the Philadelphia Phillies in the wild-card round. Atlanta won a winner-take-all Game 3 on Thursday behind a three-run home run from Michael Harris II and a dominating day on the mound. Six pitchers kept Philadelphia in check, including staff ace Chris Sale, who recorded the final four outs.
The Braves face the Dodgers after going 5-1 against them in the regular season, including a three-game home sweep in late August.
“Everyone knows the Dodgers have a juggernaut, but we played well against them this year,” Atlanta manager Walt Weiss said. “I know that doesn’t carry a whole lot of stock. Once the playoffs begin, everybody starts at zero. The Dodgers are healthier now than they were when we saw them.”
Weiss has yet to name his Game 1 starter, with a left-handed opener a possibility to line up against early left-handed bats like Ohtani and Freeman.
The Braves will continue to be without a pair of starters in right-hander Bryce Elder (knee) and left-hander Martin Perez (back).
Like Freeman before him, Olson has emerged as a Braves leader, along with Ronald Acuna Jr. Olson hit a team-best 41 home runs in the regular season and added another in the wild-card round. Harris hit 26 home runs in the regular season and Acuna added 20 homers and 21 steals.
“I think it’s just kind of going out there and playing our game and knowing that … we can compete with them and beat them,” said Braves catcher Drake Baldwin, an All-Star and 2025 NL Rookie of the Year who contributed 25 home runs.
–Doug Padilla, Field Level Media

item.dc:creator: Julian Castillo

item.content:encoded:
Ohtani busca recuperar su mejor versión ante Atlanta tras una campaña con lesiones que frenaron su impacto en los Dodgers.
Los Angeles Dodgers ya conoce a su rival en la Serie Divisional de la Liga Nacional. Atlanta Braves superó la ronda de comodines y visitará Dodger Stadium este sábado 3 de octubre, en una serie al mejor de cinco juegos que abrirá a la 1:00 p.m. del Pacífico. Ahora, la atención de los fanáticos angelinos apunta a Shohei Ohtani y al nivel que podrá ofrecer después de un cierre de campaña marcado por molestias físicas.
El japonés completó una temporada productiva en términos generales, con promedio de .275, OPS de .889 y 30 jonrones, la cifra más alta del roster de los Dodgers. Sin embargo, su rendimiento quedó lejos de la continuidad que mostró en otros años, sobre todo durante el tramo final del calendario. Una lesión en el bíceps derecho y problemas en la rodilla izquierda afectaron su ritmo, limitaron su trabajo como lanzador y lo llevaron a la lista de lesionados.
Ohtani volvió para los últimos cinco juegos de la campaña regular, aunque sus números dejaron dudas. Bateó de 5-21, con un extrabase, una base por bolas y ocho ponches. Ese panorama pone el foco sobre su estado físico y su capacidad para convertirse de inmediato en un bate determinante frente a Atlanta.
MÁS INFORMACIÓN: Dodgers inician la defensa del bicampeonato: Braves o Phillies será su primer obstáculo
¿Cómo llega Shohei Ohtani a la Serie Divisional ante Braves?
La principal incógnita no tiene que ver con el talento de Ohtani, sino con su condición física después de un año exigente. El japonés arrastró molestias desde junio, cuando la rodilla izquierda comenzó a afectar su disponibilidad. Más tarde apareció el problema en el bíceps derecho, una lesión que tuvo impacto en su ofensiva y en su preparación para abrir juegos desde la lomita.
Los Dodgers decidieron actuar con cautela. Ohtani ingresó a la lista de lesionados de 15 días en septiembre y dejó de trabajar como pitcher. Su última apertura llegó el 3 de julio ante los San Diego Padres, partido en el que lanzó seis innings, permitió tres carreras y ponchó a nueve rivales antes de salir por tensión en el bíceps derecho.
La organización ya asumió que Ohtani no lanzará durante esta postemporada. Su aporte dependerá por completo de su trabajo como bateador designado, un rol que permite concentrar su recuperación en el ajuste ofensivo y reducir el desgaste físico. El propio jugador indicó durante septiembre que su prioridad sería el bateo, mientras los Dodgers proyectan que retome su faceta de dos vías en 2027.
Ese contexto eleva la importancia de cada turno. Los Dodgers necesitan a un Ohtani capaz de impactar el juego desde el primer lugar de la alineación, sobre todo ante una serie corta donde un mal inicio puede cambiar el rumbo de la eliminatoria.
¿Qué números tuvo Ohtani contra Atlanta en 2026?
Atlanta representa un reto incómodo para el japonés. Ohtani enfrentó a los Braves en seis juegos durante la temporada regular y conectó apenas cinco hits en 26 turnos, para un promedio de .192. Esa producción contrasta con sus números globales y refleja la dificultad que tuvo el lineup de Los Ángeles frente al pitcheo rival.
El problema tampoco quedó limitado a Ohtani. Los Braves dominaron la serie particular ante los Dodgers con cinco victorias en seis enfrentamientos y una diferencia de carreras de 26-15. Atlanta llega con la confianza de haber encontrado una fórmula efectiva contra el campeón defensor, aunque los playoffs representan un escenario distinto y Dodger Stadium recibirá los dos primeros juegos.
El bajo promedio del japonés ante Atlanta no define lo que puede ocurrir en octubre, pero sí señala un punto de atención. Ohtani deberá mejorar la calidad de sus turnos, siendo más selectivo en los lanzamiento que ataca para poder hacer daño. En una ofensiva con figuras como Freddie Freeman, Mookie Betts y Will Smith, su presencia en circulación puede abrir oportunidades para el resto del orden.
Los Dodgers tampoco requieren que cargue solo con el ataque. Su tarea inmediata pasa por recuperar consistencia, seleccionar mejor los pitcheos y ofrecer una amenaza constante en cada aparición al plato.
¿Cuándo juegan Dodgers vs. Atlanta Braves en la Serie Divisional?
Los Angeles Dodgers abrirá la Serie Divisional de la Liga Nacional ante los Atlanta Braves este sábado 3 de octubre en Dodger Stadium. El Juego 1 comenzará a las 4:00 p.m., hora del Este, con los angelinos como locales tras asegurar la ventaja de localía.
- Juego 2: domingo 4 de octubre, Braves vs. Dodgers, 8:00 p.m. hora del Este, Dodger Stadium
- Juego 3: martes 6 de octubre, Dodgers vs. Braves, 6:00 p.m. hora del Este, Truist Park
- Juego 4: miércoles 7 de octubre, Dodgers vs. Braves, 6:00 p.m. hora del Este, Truist Park, si es necesario
- Juego 5: viernes 9 de octubre, Braves vs. Dodgers, 8:00 p.m. hora del Este, Dodger Stadium, si es necesario
¿El descanso puede ayudar a Ohtani con Dodgers?
La mejor noticia para Los Ángeles llegó con el calendario. El equipo aseguró el primer sembrado de la Liga Nacional y obtuvo cinco días de descanso antes del inicio de la Serie Divisional. Ese margen le permitió a Ohtani descansar después de volver de la lista de lesionados y trabajar en su swing sin la presión diaria de la temporada regular.
Dave Roberts espera una versión más saludable de su estrella para el sábado. La pausa no elimina por completo las dudas sobre el bíceps y la rodilla, aunque sí ofrece una ventana útil para que el japonés llegue con mayor frescura. El club también tiene margen para administrar su carga física durante una serie que contempla días de descanso entre los primeros compromisos.
La serie comienza el sábado en Los Ángeles con un duelo que marcará el tono de la eliminatoria. Ohtani no tendrá responsabilidad desde el montículo, pero su presencia en el primer turno de la alineación será una de las claves ofensivas del equipo. El descanso abre una oportunidad para que el japonés deje atrás un cierre irregular y responda en el momento que más importa para los Dodgers.

item.title: [Primera Hora] Dodgers se lo toman con calma: van por el histórico “three-peat” en la MLB
item.dc:creator: Por The Associated Press

item.content:encoded:
Dodgers se lo toman con calma: van por el histórico “three-peat” en la MLB
Los Ángeles busca convertirse en el primer equipo desde los Yankees de 1998-2000 en ganar tres Series Mundiales consecutivas.
PUBLICIDAD
Los Ángeles. Freddie Freeman y Emmet Sheehan bostezaron. El mánager Dave Roberts usó pantalones cortos para la práctica de bateo.
Los Dodgers de Los Ángeles se lo toman con calma mientras se encaminan a una postemporada potencialmente histórica.
Intentan convertirse en el primer equipo desde los Yankees de Nueva York de 1998-2000 en ganar tres Series Mundiales consecutivas. Serían el primer club de la Liga Nacional en lograrlo.
Y dejarían las expectativas altísimas para todos los demás.
“No es algo en lo que realmente estemos enfocados. Cuando hablas de ganar tres seguidas, le estás poniendo esa presión extra que no tiene por qué estar ahí“, comentó el antesalista Max Muncy. ”Ganar una Serie Mundial ya es lo suficientemente difícil”.
Los Dodgers disputaron un juego simulado el jueves, mientras se proyectaba el duelo decisivo de la serie de comodines de la Liga Nacional entre Filadelfia y Atlanta en las pantallas de video del estadio. Los Bravos vencieron a los Filis por 6-2 y jugarán en Los Ángeles el primer duelo de la serie divisional de la Liga Nacional, al mejor en un máximo de cinco encuentros, el sábado, cuando se pronostica que la temperatura alcance los 100 grados Fahrenheit (38 Celsius) para el juego diurno.
“Te enfrentas a un equipo que ya pasó por el fuego y ya vivió la emoción”, comentó Muncy.
Los Dodgers han pasado la semana de descanso recuperándose, mientras alternaban práctica de bateo en vivo y en la jaula con juegos simulados en un estadio mayormente silencioso. Aparte de las canciones de entrada al plato, los únicos sonidos eran el chasquido del bate, los gritos de los jugadores desde las bancas y los jardineros avisando a sus compañeros que ellos se encargarían de un elevado.
Freeman aprovechó el tiempo para concentrarse en ajustar la mecánica de su swing mientras lidiaba una molestia en la rodilla derecha. El plan del primera base de 37 años incluía hacer 400 swings “con la esperanza de quitarme los malos hábitos”, explicó.
En el inicio del juego simulado del jueves, conectó un doble ante Tyler Glasnow.
“De verdad me siento bien físicamente ahora mismo y depende de mí resolver la mecánica del swing”, comentó. ”No tengo dolor en la rodilla en este momento”.
Shohei Ohtani, cuatro veces nombrado el Jugador Más Valioso, ha lidiado durante semanas con molestias persistentes en el bíceps derecho y la rodilla izquierda. La rodilla lo frenó para lanzar y el brazo lo llevó recientemente a la lista de lesionados por primera vez con los Dodgers.
Regresó a tiempo para jugar en cinco partidos al final de la temporada.
Aún está por verse qué versión de Ohtani tendrán los Dodgers en la serie divisional de la Liga Nacional. Sin embargo, Roberts dijo que “se siente muy bien físicamente. Sus swings, en general, están en un gran punto”.
La alineación de jugadores de posición de los Dodgers es la de mayor edad en las Grandes Ligas, encabezada por el infielder venezolano Miguel Rojas, de 37 años, Freeman y Muncy, de 35. Ohtani tiene 32. El relevista Blake Treinen tiene 38, pero se perderá la postemporada tras lesionarse el fin de semana pasado.
“Creo que la experiencia va a ser enorme. Sabemos lo que se necesita”, aseveró Freeman
Al mismo tiempo, advirtió que los Dodgers no deben adelantarse.
“Si en este momento piensas en el panorama general, vas a perder de vista las cosas”.

item.content:encoded:
【ロサンゼルス1日（日本時間2日）＝横山尚杜】米大リーグ、ドジャースの大谷翔平投手（32）が9月30日（同10月1日）の全体練習で、山本由伸投手（28）と対戦したとベイツ打撃コーチが明かした。紅白戦や実戦形式を含めても移籍後初対決で3打席の勝負だったという。また、同日まで2日連続で屋外フリー打撃も実施し、150メートル級の特大弾をマーク。同コーチは「今年1番と言っていいくらい」と状態に太鼓判を押した。
非公開練習で、大谷が衝撃の打棒を披露していた。ドジャースが戦う地区シリーズの対戦相手が東地区優勝のブレーブスに決定。報道陣に公開されたこの日の練習で、大谷はグラウンドに現れなかったが、前夜は山本との予行演習を実施し、フリー打撃では特大弾を連発したという。
「昨日はヨシと3打席対戦したよ。紅白戦に近い形だったので最終的な結果は分からない。ただ、昨日のフリー打撃は今年見た中で一番いいと言える状態だった」
9月29、30日に本拠地で開催した全体練習は非公開。30日は紅白戦が実施され、大谷は山本と3打席対戦。ドジャースではキャンプ中の実戦形式などを含めて初の実現。超一線級の球筋で実戦勘を養い、2日連続で実施した屋外フリーでは「スコアボードのすぐ下まで飛んだ打球が何本かあった」と150メートル級の放物線を放ったと証言した。
「右上腕二頭筋の炎症」による負傷者リスト（IL）から復帰後、シーズンは5試合で22打席21打数5安打8三振。実戦感覚の鈍りを感じさせる場面もあり、ロバーツ監督は地区シリーズまでに実戦形式の練習実施を要望していた。大谷にとって追い風となる可能性があるのはポストシーズンの日程。地区シリーズは最大2連戦でリーグ優勝決定シリーズ以降も最大3連戦。移動回数は増えるが、連戦が少なくコンディションを整えやすい面もある。ワールドシリーズ2連覇に貢献してきた大谷と山本。最高峰の予行演習で、戦線離脱した分の空白を埋めた。

item.title: [Orange County Register] Dodgers anticipate Shohei Ohtani being in ‘a great spot’ for NLDS after dealing with injuries

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — He is the elephant in the lineup.
Shohei Ohtani’s presence looms large as the Dodgers prepare to open their postseason run with Game 1 of their National League Division Series on Saturday afternoon against the Atlanta Braves.
But what version of the four-time league MVP will be in the lineup on Saturday is a mystery. He has played just eight games in the past month and spoken to the media just once in the past six weeks, so assurances about his health have only come second hand.
But they have come.
“Everything is feeling great physically,” Dodgers general manager Brandon Gomes said this week. “The swings, once he came back, overall were in a good place. And using these five days to continue to get reps and feeling good into this series is really important. But feels like he’s in a great spot.”
Ohtani returned for the final five games of the regular season and went 5 for 21 (.238) with just one extra-base hit (a double), one RBI, no runs scored, eight strikeouts and only one walk. But that was enough for Dodgers manager Dave Roberts.
“I feel confident that you’re going to see the best version of Shohei of the last two months,” Roberts said, referencing a stretch that saw Ohtani hit .232 with a .745 OPS while compromised by knee and arm injuries.
“I know that’s sort of a low bar given his injury, but I do think that he’s as healthy as he’s been in quite some time, and every day from the training staff, it keeps getting better. So yeah, No. 1 he’ll be a threat being in the lineup, but I do think that the performance piece will be what we’re hoping for.”
Media were not allowed into the Dodgers’ workouts on Tuesday and Wednesday. Ohtani took batting practice on the field each day and also took three at-bats against Yoshinobu Yamamoto during Wednesday’s intrasquad game.
Thursday’s workout was open to the media and Ohtani was nowhere to be seen during batting practice or the intrasquad game that followed.
“His BP outside the last two days was really good,” Dodgers hitting coach Aaron Bates said during Thursday’s workout. “It was as good as we’ve seen it this year as far as the way the ball was coming off and the way he was getting his move off.
“He looked really good in his BP, in his work. He looks as good as he has as far as that goes. … The ball always comes off his bat hard, but the last two days in particular he was swinging very well.”
Bates said there have been no signs of any physical limitations in Ohtani’s work.
“The physical part he’s kind of moving past that,” Bates said. “Now it’s just getting the timing against different speeds, when he wants to get his move off, that sort of thing – kind of the usual stuff hitters go through as opposed to him navigating trying to achieve the physical components (while injured).”
The expectation is not to have Ohtani – or anyone else in the lineup – at 100% full strength, Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman said.
“I don’t think anyone is going to be at 100% in October,” Friedman said. “It’s a long, grueling season, and everyone’s on fumes. Our group, the team we’re playing against, everyone is on fumes. And it’s so adrenaline-based that, for me, it’s about each guy just drawing from their experience and having calmness in what they do. And I would bet on our talent to shine through.
“We don’t need anyone to try to do more.”
But they do need “a lot” from Ohtani, Roberts said, in a lineup that has underperformed at times and struggled against the better pitching staffs of the National League.
“We need him to be full strength and do what he does – take good at-bats, take what they give you,” Roberts said. “If they’re going to pitch around you to pitch to Mookie, so be it. And if they make mistakes, then hit it hard.
“Yeah, we need him to be healthy and strong. It certainly helps our offense.”

item.content:encoded:
ロサンゼルス・ドジャースの大谷翔平が、2026年のMLBポストシーズンに臨む。
本記事では、大谷翔平の2026年MLBポストシーズン出場見通しをはじめ、二刀流の可能性、ドジャースの試合日程を紹介する。
大谷翔平は2026年MLBポストシーズンに出場する？
ロサンゼルス・ドジャースの大谷翔平は、2026年のMLBポストシーズンに出場する見通しとなっている。
大谷は右上腕の炎症により9月8日付で15日間の負傷者リスト(IL)に入っていたが、9月23日(現地時間)に戦列へ復帰。復帰後も指名打者(DH)として出場を続けている。
デーブ・ロバーツ監督も「一番大事なのは健康な状態でプレーできたこと。いい状態で迎えられる」と語っており、ポストシーズンでも打者として主力出場する見通しだ。
大谷翔平はポストシーズンで二刀流出場する？
大谷の2026年シーズンにおける投手登板はすでに終了しているため、ポストシーズンでは指名打者(DH)に専念する予定となっている。
そのため、10月のポストシーズンで投手として登板する予定はなく、打者としてドジャース打線を牽引することになる。
ドジャースに所属する日本人選手
2026年のドジャースには、大谷翔平、山本由伸、佐々木朗希の日本人選手3名が所属している。
| 選手 | ポジション |
|---|---|
| 大谷翔平 | 指名打者(DH) |
| 山本由伸 | 投手 |
| 佐々木朗希 | 投手 |
ドジャースのMLBポストシーズン試合日程
ドジャースはナショナル・リーグ西地区で優勝し、第2シードを獲得したため、ワイルドカードシリーズが免除される。
ポストシーズンはナ・リーグ地区シリーズ(NLDS)から登場し、ブレーブスvsフィリーズのワイルドカードシリーズ勝者と対戦する。
ナ・リーグ地区シリーズ(NLDS)
| 試合 | 日程(日本時間) | 開催 |
|---|---|---|
| 第1戦 | 2026年10月4日(日) | ホーム |
| 第2戦 | 2026年10月5日(月) | ホーム |
| 第3戦 | 2026年10月7日(水) | アウェー |
| 第4戦 ※必要な場合 | 2026年10月8日(木) | アウェー |
| 第5戦 ※必要な場合 | 2026年10月10日(土) | ホーム |
ドジャースが地区シリーズを突破した場合の日程
ドジャースが地区シリーズを勝ち抜いた場合は、ナ・リーグ優勝決定シリーズ(NLCS)へ進出する。
NLCSは7戦4勝制で、日本時間10月12日(月)から10月20日(火)まで開催予定となっている。
さらにNLCSを突破した場合はワールドシリーズへ進出。ワールドシリーズは日本時間10月24日(土)に開幕し、最長で11月1日(日)まで行われる予定だ。
| ラウンド | 日程(日本時間) | 方式 |
|---|---|---|
| ナ・リーグ優勝決定シリーズ(NLCS) | 2026年10月12日(月)～10月20日(火) | 7戦4勝制 |
| ワールドシリーズ(WS) | 2026年10月24日(土)～11月1日(日) | 7戦4勝制 |
MLBポストシーズン2026のテレビ放送・ネット配信予定
MLBポストシーズン2026は、Amazonプライムビデオ『SPOTVチャンネル』、『SPOTV NOW』『MLB.tv(Amazonあり)』『Lemino(SPOTVパック)』でネット配信されるほか、衛星放送『J SPORTS』でも中継が予定されている。
『NHK』でもポストシーズンの注目試合が放送される予定だ。

|---|---|---|

| NHK BS | 衛星放送 | 注目試合を生中継 10/1(木)10:59 カブスvsパドレス |

※各チャンネルの中継対象試合は各ラウンド対戦カード決定後に発表。

【Amazonプライムビデオ】30日間無料体験あり

プライム会員は追加料金なしで視聴でき、初めて登録する場合は30日間無料体験の利用が可能だ。

- 「ライブを観る 30日間の無料体験を始める」をタップ

※無料体験終了後は月額600円(税込)で自動更新。
【SPOTV NOW】MLBポストシーズンもライブ配信
SPOTV NOW
『SPOTV NOW』では、2026シーズンもポストシーズンまでMLBを視聴できる。ポストシーズンの試合は全試合をライブ配信予定となっている。SPOTV NOW登録方法

- 各種情報を入力し、登録完了後すぐに視聴可能！

Amazon
まずはAmazonのMLB.tvチャンネルページにアクセス

item.title: [DodgersBeat] Josue De Paula’s Potentially Limited NLDS Role

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES, CA—While the Dodgers await the conclusion of the three-game Wild Card Series between the Philadelphia Phillies and Atlanta Braves, they’ll have plenty of time to look over their 26-man roster before Game One of the NLDS on Saturday.
Among those players on the bubble is top prospect rookie outfielder Josue De Paual, who, after a scorching two-week stretch while Shohei Ohtani was on the injured list, saw his chances of joining Los Angeles in October skyrocket.
Much of the discussion surrounding the Dodgers’ final NLDS roster spot has centered around Josue De Paula and Dalton Rushing potentially battling it out for the final left-handed bat off the bench.
While De Paula has shown plenty during his brief time in the majors and remains a major part of the Dodgers’ future, his potential inclusion on the NLDS roster would come with a clearly defined role. Rather than expecting the top prospect to become an everyday contributor in October suddenly, Los Angeles would primarily be looking to his bat in specific situations.
“I would say if he were to make it, it would just be as a bat,” manager Dave Roberts said.
That distinction is important because De Paula’s other tools are unlikely to get much use in a postseason series. He impressed during his September stint with the Dodgers after Shohei Ohtani was placed on the 15-day injured list, receiving most of his opportunities at designated hitter and showing the elite offensive potential that initially made him one of the organization’s most intriguing prospects.
Defensively, De Paula has acknowledged he wants to improve, but that could limit his opportunities in the field against a team the Dodgers expect to contend deep into October. His speed is another tool that could theoretically give Los Angeles an advantage, but Roberts doesn’t appear interested in using him as a pinch-runner.
“For me, that’s just really not his calling card,” Roberts explained. “So as far as on the bases, I just haven’t seen enough to supplant somebody else. But I’ve seen enough with the bat.”
That leaves De Paula’s bat as the primary reason for carrying him, and there is certainly an argument for it. The Dodgers have seen enough offensively to believe he can change a game with one swing, and limiting his responsibilities would let him focus on the one area where Roberts has already expressed confidence.
Still, that doesn’t necessarily mean De Paula would see significant playing time.
The Dodgers are also considering Dalton Rushing, who returned for their final regular-season series against the San Francisco Giants and went 0-for-3 with a strikeout. Rushing’s ability to provide more versatility could factor into how Los Angeles ultimately constructs the bench, making the final decision about more than which player has the better bat.
Roberts has also indicated that the Dodgers could consider adding Hyeseong Kim to the NLDS roster, though his inclusion would likely center on his speed and defense rather than his offense.
For De Paula, then, making the roster would be a significant accomplishment in itself. But don’t confuse a roster spot with a major October role. If the Dodgers carry him into the NLDS, the plan appears to be using him selectively as a dangerous left-handed bat rather than asking the 20-year-old to take on a regular role.
Still, a lot can happen, and things rarely go according to plan, and that could very well bode in De Paula’s favor. Whether it’s an injury or a double-switch situation, De Paula could play more than a small pinch-hit appearance, but for now, that appears to be his role moving forward this season.

item.title: [Dodgers Nation] Mookie Betts Makes Feelings Clear on Dodgers vs. Red Sox Legacy
item.dc:creator: Nelson Espinal
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers star Mookie Betts has a storied career with both the Dodgers and the Boston Red Sox, but he identifies more with one of those teams. Dodgers or the Red Sox? After multiple postseason runs and a legacy with the Dodgers, Betts made it clear he identifies more with the current Dodgers core than with any other team he has played for. “Going through the losses, going through all the ups and downs is why we are where we are today,” Betts said to The Athletic’s Katie Woo. “When I’m
item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers star Mookie Betts has a storied career with both the Dodgers and the Boston Red Sox, but he identifies more with one of those teams.
Dodgers or the Red Sox?
After multiple postseason runs and a legacy with the Dodgers, Betts made it clear he identifies more with the current Dodgers core than with any other team he has played for.
“Going through the losses, going through all the ups and downs is why we are where we are today,” Betts said to The Athletic’s Katie Woo.
“When I’m done playing, I’ll remember Boston, of course. But what I’ll really remember is if somebody said, ‘Oh, you played baseball, like who did you play with?’ These are the guys I’m going to say I played with. That’s my team.”
For Betts, it must be hard to choose between the two franchises since he did well in both places and surely has fond memories of both, but he is known far more as a Dodger and a member of the current dynasty.
Mookie Betts’ History with the Dodgers and Red Sox
Betts has spent more time with the Dodgers, seven seasons, while playing only six years with the Red Sox, though arguably his best baseball came with the Red Sox, and that is where he ascended into superstardom.
In fact, in a statistical comparison, Betts earned 42.5 bWAR in Boston, while he got just 36.5 bWAR for the Dodgers.
He won an MVP with Boston, with a second-place finish, a sixth-place finish, and an eighth-place finish. He also got four Gold Glove awards and three Silver Slugger awards.
He has won three titles with the Dodgers, while he won only one with the Red Sox. Betts has four Silver Slugger awards and two Gold Glove awards.
Additionally, Betts moved from right field to shortstop as a Dodger, making a great transition that few players make in the latter half of their careers.
Given how things ended with the Red Sox, via a trade that was sudden and unexpected, the Dodgers have been a welcoming home for Betts.
He inked a 10-year contract and became the face of the franchise until Shohei Ohtani arrived, helping bring a title to an organization in a drought that struggled to get over the hump.
Betts is a certified Hall of Famer at this point with his resume, and it seems that when he makes it to Cooperstown, he will enter as a Dodger.

item.title: [mlb.com] Could this top prospect be a postseason weapon for Dodgers?
item.dc:creator: Theo DeRosa

item.content:encoded:
On Sept. 13 at loanDepot park in Miami, the Dodgers rookie turned on a 98 mph fastball from Marlins righty Eury Pérez for a massive three-run home run: 108.2 mph off the bat and 416 feet into the right-field seats. In a game in which De Paula first walked and later roped a 101.9 mph double off the wall in right-center, it was the titanic homer that put Dodgers fans on notice.
Manager Dave Roberts seemed to think it was possible, saying the sweet-swinging lefty had earned the right to be “a part of the conversation” for the club’s NLDS roster when De Paula was optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City on Sept. 23.
Here’s a look at how De Paula fared during his time in the Majors and what he could bring to the Dodgers during the 2026 postseason.
Power and plate discipline
In his 42 plate appearances with the Dodgers, De Paula put up some eye-popping offensive numbers: He posted a .323 batting average, a .500 on-base percentage and a .581 slugging percentage, scored seven runs and had seven RBIs. Most notable, though? De Paula drew 11 walks and struck out only five times.
Those 11 free passes rank as the third most in any Dodgers hitter’s first 11 career games, trailing only Andy LaRoche (2007) and Jim Gilliam (1953), who both had 12 walks.
Not only were opposing pitchers evidently cautious when pitching to De Paula -- who slashed .303/.401/.547 with 27 home runs this season for Double-A Tulsa -- but the lefty steadfastly refused to expand the zone. He swung at just 18 of the 97 out-of-zone pitches he saw for an excellent 18.6% chase rate, fitting right in on a Dodgers team whose 27.5% chase rate in 2026 ranked third best in the Majors. That’s not a fluke for De Paula, either: He drew 81 walks and struck out just 87 times this season in Double-A.
As good as his plate discipline is, De Paula can flat out mash, too. Twelve of the 26 balls he put in play in the big leagues were hard hit (95+ mph exit velocity), including five above 100 mph. Nine of those 26 (34.6%) registered as pulled-air contact; while De Paula’s Major League sample size is admittedly quite small, National League MVP favorite Pete Crow-Armstrong led MLB with a 34.0% pulled-air rate in 2026.
"He's just a special hitter," Roberts said. "Hitters don't see the ball that quickly out of hand; it's a gift. Just the ability to [limit] chase, I think that lines up in the postseason. And no moment is going to be too big for that kid."
Where does he fit in?
Evidently, De Paula’s offensive skill set could serve the Dodgers well in October. But what is his pathway to playing time?
That’s where things get a little difficult.
The rookie, who split his time with Tulsa between left and right field, made just two appearances in the field for the Dodgers, playing six total innings in left. Not willing to compromise what ranks as an average defensive outfield, the Dodgers plan to use De Paula as a designated hitter. There’s just one problem: Some guy wearing No. 17 currently occupies that spot.
Yes, Shohei Ohtani's presence will make De Paula’s path to postseason at-bats harder, although the Dodgers are certainly happy their superstar is back in the lineup. When De Paula was optioned to the Minors, it was as the corresponding move for Ohtani’s return from the injured list. Dalton Rushing's return from the IL two days later might also make it harder for De Paula to find postseason at-bats.
But there’s a reason De Paula became the first Dodger to bypass Triple-A and head right to the Majors since 2014. Used correctly -- presumably to face right-handed pitchers, against whom De Paula hit .314 with a 1.016 OPS in Double-A -- he can be a postseason weapon as a pinch-hitter or, if Ohtani is out of the lineup, at DH. The 6-foot-3, 185-pound De Paula has below-average sprint speed but still managed to steal 31 bases in 41 tries in the Minors this season, so he can be a threat on the basepaths as well.
While October baseball might prove to be overwhelming for the 21-year-old, De Paula could be a big piece of the Dodgers' success this postseason, whether it's in the NLDS or potentially further down the line.

item.title: [Dodger Blue] Freddie Freeman and Shohei Ohtani change routine ahead of NLDS
item.dc:creator: Matt Borelli
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers are getting a much-needed breather this week as they wait to see which team they will face in the National League Division Series, which begins Saturday with Game 1 at Dodger Stadium. The Dodgers will have their answer by the end of Thursday night as the Philadelphia Phillies and Atlanta Braves meet at Truist Park — the only Wild Card Series that reached a decisive Game 3. In the meantime, the Dodgers are using the time off to rest and prepare for their next opponent. The
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are getting a much-needed breather this week as they wait to see which team they will face in the National League Division Series, which begins Saturday with Game 1 at Dodger Stadium.
The Dodgers will have their answer by the end of Thursday night as the Philadelphia Phillies and Atlanta Braves meet at Truist Park — the only Wild Card Series that reached a decisive Game 3.
In the meantime, the Dodgers are using the time off to rest and prepare for their next opponent. The team has been going through workouts and simulated games at Dodger Stadium to stay sharp for when they resume play later this weekend.
As part of their on-field workouts, several Dodgers players got some swings in during batting practice. In a video shared by the team on X, the group of players who participated includes Shohei Ohtani, Freddie Freeman and Mookie Betts, among others.
Locked in for October. pic.twitter.com/RT5twoW3ED
— Los Angeles Dodgers (@Dodgers) September 30, 2026
Ohtani taking swings during the bye week is an encouraging sign after he recently returned to the Dodgers following a stint on the 15-day injured list. He typically does not hit on the field, but has done it a few times throughout his tenure with the club, usually following a slump he’s trying to break out of.
For Freeman, the extra work could be pivotal in helping him get his swing back on track.
“Today is going to be a big day to see how BP goes,” Freeman said earlier this week. “Like I kind of told you guys a couple days ago, I feel like BP’s not going to go well today, just because of how my swing is right now. And then I’ll be able to start working on if I am blocking balls to left field in BP, then I can make those adjustments coming down.
“It’s hard to explain what’s going on in this head a lot of times, but it’s going to be big because I’m going to hit BP every single day on the field. I think that will help seeing balls velocity-wise, to be able to start moving it lower and lower and down toward the shortstop, and hopefully that will get my body in line with how I want it to work going into Saturday.”
The Dodgers had to manage Freeman down the stretch as he dealt with a right knee injury that affected both his offense and defense. He was kept out of the lineup for multiple games, but the Dodgers declined to place him on the injured list.
The time off did help Freeman improve, but the results didn’t follow. He closed out the season by batting just .226/.300/.278 over his final 30 games, and he hit just one home run in the final two months of the year.
The Dodgers are hopeful that the brief layoff will help Freeman reset mechanically and rediscover his rhythm at the plate just in time for the postseason.
Freddie Freeman incorporating 2024 World Series approach
Freeman has been exploring unorthodox ways to get back on track and recalled a key adjustment he made that led to his historic showing in the 2024 World Series.
“Just doing different work. I’m trying to find something that gets me results. We’re at the time where we’re just trying to get hot for five weeks here,” Freeman noted earlier this month.
“Kind of like I did in the World Series a couple years ago, I did the step-out move. That’s not sustainable over six months. (But) I’m not trying to find something that’s sustainable. I’m trying to find something that works for four weeks.”

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Dodgers Injury Updates Before NLDS: Shohei Ohtani, Freddie Freeman, Edgardo Henriquez

item.content:encoded:
As the Los Angeles Dodgers prepare to embark on another October with sky-high expectations, there are a few stars who did not end the regular season at 100% health.
Superstars Shohei Ohtani and Freddie Freeman, and flame-throwing relief pitcher Edgardo Henriquez, have perhaps the biggest question marks surrounding them heading into the National League Division Series.
Here's the latest updates on all three players.
Shohei Ohtani Injury Update
Ohtani has dealt with nagging knee and biceps injuries for the majority of the season. His knee eventually shut him down from pitching ahead of the All-Star break, and his biceps injury resulted in the minimum stay on the 15-day IL, returning for a lackluster (5-for-21) final five regular season games.
General manager Brandon Gomes spoke on a Tuesday Zoom call with the media and had an update on the four-time MVP, and how his swing has been looking amid a much-needed break while the wild-card round finishes up.
“Everything is feeling great physically," Gomes said of Ohtani. "The swings, once he came back, overall were in a good place. And using these five days to continue to get reps and feeling good into this series is really important. But feels like he's in a great spot."
Manager Dave Roberts appeared to feel the same about Ohtani, and even went as far as saying that the man who hit just .245 during the second half of the season will still have a stellar postseason.
"I feel confident that you're going to see the best version of Shohei of the last two months," Roberts said. "I know that's sort of a low bar given his injury, but I do think that he's as healthy as he's been in quite some time. And every day from the training staff, it keeps getting better. So yeah, No. 1, he'll be a threat being in the lineup, but I do think that the performance piece will be what we're hoping for."
Freddie Freeman Injury Update
Freeman is no stranger to playing through injury, and has recently been dealing with right knee tendinitis that manifested itself in the form of a .184 batting average in the final 20 games he played of 2026.
"My body feels good,” Freeman said Tuesday. “I think that’s the main thing. I feel like it’s in a good spot to be able to do the work and hopefully fix my swing and everything that’s been going on the last couple months.”
Freeman was asked to compare his current pain level to past postseasons. Fans remember his heroics in the 2024 World Series —where he would later take home MVP honors — thriving through the Fall Classic despite a sprained ankle and broken rib cartilage.
“A couple of Octobers ago was probably 100 times worse, ailment-wise,” Freeman said. “I truly feel good right now, physically. So it’s on me now to figure out the mechanics of the swing in the next five days, and I have all the confidence in myself that I will figure that out by Saturday.”
Edgardo Henriquez Injury Update
Henriquez put up a 2.85 ERA across 60 innings of work this season, averaging a 100.8 mph fastball (in the 100th percentile among active pitchers), until lower back discomfort landed him on the injured list last month. He was activated off the IL this week.
“He’s trending really well at this point,” Gomes said. “His last live BP went well. He’s responding positively after he throws and isn’t feeling any lingering discomfort. We’ve still got a few steps to go. But if that all goes well, then yeah, the expectation is he’ll be on the roster.”
Roberts also made sure to acknowledge how pivotal the off-week was for his fireballer. Due to an excellent track record (a career 2.73 ERA in 86 regular season appearances), he could prove to be a crucial piece this October.
“I think he’s one of those guys that getting the bye has really benefited,” Roberts said. “He’ll throw another live or sim game to some hitters. ... Then he should be ready to go. And given the body of work, what he’s done, the unique skill set could be huge for us, will be huge for us.”

He graduated from San Francisco State University in 2020 and received his Masters of Science at the University of Southern California in 2025.

item.title: [yardbarker.com] Dodgers NLDS Notes: Edwin Díaz, Edgardo Henriquez & Starting Rotation
item.dc:creator: Matthew Moreno
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers earned the benefit of a postseason bye and now are reaping the full benefit as the Philadelphia Phillies staved off elimination to force the Atlanta Braves to a winner-take-all Game 3 in their Wild Card Series matchup. The winner advances to face the Dodgers in the National League Division Series, which begins Saturday at Dodger Stadium. The start for time for Game 1 has not yet been decided as it hinges on whether or not the San Diego Padres or Chicago Cubs reach the NLD
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers earned the benefit of a postseason bye and now are reaping the full benefit as the Philadelphia Phillies staved off elimination to force the Atlanta Braves to a winner-take-all Game 3 in their Wild Card Series matchup.
The winner advances to face the Dodgers in the National League Division Series, which begins Saturday at Dodger Stadium. The start for time for Game 1 has not yet been decided as it hinges on whether or not the San Diego Padres or Chicago Cubs reach the NLDS to play the Milwaukee Brewers.
In the meantime, the Dodgers are spending the rest of the week going through workouts and simulated games, much like their approach in 2024 that proved beneficial.
The Dodgers avoiding the Wild Card Series this year has proven beneficial for multiple players dealing with an injury, including Edgardo Henriquez.
He missed the final two weeks because of lower back discomfort but has made steady progress in his recovery and is on track for the NLDS.
“We’ll get him some work this week. He’s trending really well at this point,” Dodgers general manager Brandon Gomes said on Tuesday. “His last live BP went well, he’s responding positively after he throws and isn’t feeling any lingering discomfort.
“We’ve still got a few steps to go, but if that all goes well, then yeah, the expectation is he’ll be on the roster.”
Elsewhere in the Dodgers bullpen, Edwin Díaz finished the regular season on a high note after returning from a stint on the 15-day injured list because of a neck issue.
“I don’t know if we could have asked much more out of Edwin. I think it was, like, a 50-plus percent strikeout rate when he came back,” Gomes noted. “Felt like each outing was more and more sharp, and looking more like himself.
“Feels like he’s in a great place right now, stuff out of hand is as good as it’s been all year, and we know that he has pitched in the hottest of hot games in the past, and in any role, especially in the postseason. He’s looked great and glad that he’s in the position that he’s in and was able to bounce back after the IL stint.”
Díaz threw five scoreless innings, allowed just one hit and one walk while collecting nine strikeouts across five appearances upon getting activated Sept. 18. While Gomes projected confidence, what may still be different for Díaz is he’s not relied upon as the primary closer.
Even without Shohei Ohtani pitching, the Dodgers are heading into the playoffs with a formidable starting rotation that consists of Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow. What order they will pitch in has not yet been decided.
Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said the team would not set their NLDS rotation until Thursday, at which point they would know whether the Braves or Phillies advanced.
“I say that because just trying to figure out opponent and the schedule going forward, not sure about game times and things like that. We’re having conversations but we’re not definitive yet,” Roberts explained.
“I think opponent certainly should matter, could matter. Talking to Mark Prior about where guys are at. To be honest, we could really put all four guys in a hat and run them out there. But I think there is going to be more thought behind it. We don’t need to make a decision right now, so really just trying to be clear and talk through it.”
Last year the Dodgers almost exclusively used Snell (Wild Card, NL Championship Series and World Series) as their Game 1 starter. Ohtani started against the Phillies in the opener of the NLDS.
One change from the 2025 postseason is Glasnow’s first appearance likely won’t come out of the bullpen during the NLDS due in part to a different schedule.

item.title: [heavy.com] Why David Stearns’ Pitching Philosophy Stands Between the Mets and Tarik Skubal
item.dc:creator: Terrance Biggs

However, his money did nothing but return misery and hopelessness. Unlike his predecessors, the Wilpons, Cohen is more than eager to open his wallet and continue trying to bring talent to Flushing. Meanwhile, David Stearns, the president of baseball operations, faces criticism from both media and fans for free agent signings that have not be
item.content:encoded:
New York Mets owner Steve Cohen is the richest in the MLB. He’s spent at least a billion dollars in contracts to bring a World Series trophy back to Queens. However, his money did nothing but return misery and hopelessness. Unlike his predecessors, the Wilpons, Cohen is more than eager to open his wallet and continue trying to bring talent to Flushing.
Meanwhile, David Stearns, the president of baseball operations, faces criticism from both media and fans for free agent signings that have not been successful. With the exception of Juan Soto, who continues to excel, Stearns’ eye for talent seems to have suffered from astigmatism, where he cannot judge the proximity of the roster to becoming a winning one.
Yet, some believe that lefthander Tarik Skubal, in the estimation of many, could be the one to lead the Mets back to the playoffs. However, considering Stearns’ approach, the deal looks like a long shot. Stearns, in his season postmortem, discussed the need for starting pitching.
“I do think it is necessary for us to add to our rotation,” Stearns said. “We can do that in a variety of different ways. We’ve talked about this plenty before—you’d always love to add to the top of your rotation; any team would love to do that. Over the long term, what we need to do is develop pitchers at the top of our rotation, and I think we are proving we can do that, and we’ll continue to do that.”
On Baseball Night in New York, @chelsea_janes says “call me crazy” but she’d rather have two good starters opposed to getting just Tarik Skubal pic.twitter.com/STB6i2PTe2
— SNY Mets (@SNY_Mets) September 28, 2026
Making the Case
First, Skubal is a southpaw that the Mets need to break up their righty-dominant rotation. More importantly, his 2.72 ERA & 0.96 WHIP suggest that he continues to dominate pitchers, even after changing leads and settling into the Los Angeles Dodgers pressure cooker.
It makes sense to bring in an elite lefty to minimize the impact of Bryce Harper, Pete Crow-Armstrong, Kyle Schwarber, and Shohei Ohtani. Additionally, Skubal’s presence would also take the pressure off a bullpen that sorely needs a frontline starter to pitch into the seventh inning. Freddy Peralta was supposed to be the one, but he often struggled to escape the fifth.
Tarik Skubal has 10 Ks through 6 scoreless innings! pic.twitter.com/LOWMtaLuIf
— MLB (@MLB) September 26, 2026
Against the Grain
Stearns, during his time with Milwaukee, built his rosters on a mix of young talent, under-contract control, and not paying pitchers long-term. As a result, when news of Peralta sought a nine-year extension, his days in New York became shorter. Stearns, to his credit, continues to build a farm system that produces young talent.
Skubal presents a departure from all of that. First, he will command at least $300 million in a long-term contract. Next, Stesarns wants the rotation to still have room for the younger pitchers like Christian Scott, Nolan McLean, Zac Thornton, and eventually Jonah Tong. To sign Skubal, Stearns would need to completely change how he fundamentally views pitching, and that does not seem to be the case at all.
Danny Abriano of SNY outlined the perils of signing a veteran pitcher long-term.
“For every long-term, big-money deal to a pitcher 29 or older that works out (Max Scherzer’s seven-year deal with the Nationals looks incredible in retrospect, and the Yankees‘ deal for Max Fried is aging well), you can point to a whole bunch that didn’t or currently aren’t (Patrick Corbin, Jacob deGrom, Jordan Zimmermann, Felix Hernandez, and Corbin Burnes).”
Scherzer and Fried appear to be the few exceptions to the rule. Otherwise, it’s a dice roll on what type of arm you will get. On top of that, Skubal already underwent a medical procedure this season.
Mets fans see Skubal as their ticket to the playoffs. Similarly, some media do. However, the Mets, despite their abundant supply of cash, could look to other avenues.

item.title: [Dodgers Way] Projecting the Dodgers' NLDS roster with Josue De Paula, bench shuffle
item.dc:creator: Katrina Stebbins
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers get to kick back and watch as eight teams duke it out to move on to their respective League Division Series this week. The Atlanta Braves and Philadelphia Phillies will go head-to-head in the NL Wild Card Series before one of them moves on to try and topple LA. One would think that this Dodgers team would have everything buttoned up well ahead of the NLDS, but there are still a couple of key questions to be answered. Projecting the Dodgers' NLDS roster with Josue De Paula
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers get to kick back and watch as eight teams duke it out to move on to their respective League Division Series this week. The Atlanta Braves and Philadelphia Phillies will go head-to-head in the NL Wild Card Series before one of them moves on to try and topple LA.
One would think that this Dodgers team would have everything buttoned up well ahead of the NLDS, but there are still a couple of key questions to be answered.
Projecting the Dodgers' NLDS roster with Josue De Paula called upon
Catchers (2): Will Smith, Hunter Feduccia
For some reason, the Dodgers decided to carry three catchers on their Wild Card and NLDS rosters last year — Smith, Dalton Rushing, and Ben Rortvedt — but adjusted ahead of the NLCS by shedding Rushing, who received just one at-bat in the NLDS but otherwise rode the bench.
Rortvedt didn't get a start or even substitution after Game 2 of the NLDS with Smith slowly coming back from injury at the beginning of the postseason. Feduccia figures to play a similar break-glass-in-case-of-emergency role. As a lefty, he could get a start and then an early pull depending on matchups but, barring disaster, it's mostly going to be Smith's show.
Designated hitters (2): Shohei Ohtani, Josue De Paula
The Dodgers clearly want to find a way to bring De Paula with them in October, even if only as a lingering threat on their bench. They're reportedly not entertaining putting him in the outfield at all, and it's not hard to see why. Even if they're confident they'll be able to fix his defense in time, they can't afford any leakage in the postseason.
Ohtani is still shaking off the cobwebs from his 15-day IL stint. He picked up a few hits with promising exit velocity in his return against the San Diego Padres and later against the San Francisco Giants, but there are still question marks around what version of him we might see this postseason.
Infielders (6): Freddie Freeman, Mookie Betts, Tommy Edman, Max Muncy, Miguel Rojas, Kiké Hernández
A notable exclusion here is Hyeseong Kim. Although he's in the running to get a spot on the bench and exclusively come into games to pinch-run or for reassurances on defense, there's still a chance he doesn't make the roster if the Dodgers are set on carrying 13 pitchers. Edman and Hernández, though lacking the same speed as Kim, can still offer the same defensive versatility.
Outfielders (3): Andy Pages, Kyle Tucker, Teoscar Hernández
Pages might've found himself in the same boat as Ohtani, but he announced his return to the Dodgers after a month-long IL stint in a big way, hitting .333 with a 1.180 OPS, two homers, and five RBI against the Padres and Giants. No doubt Dave Roberts and Andrew Friedman breathed a massive sigh of relief.
Alex Call will be the odd man out. He was on all four of LA's playoff rosters last year and received sporadic appearances throughout the month, but that was when Michael Conforto was still on the payroll. Tucker and Hernández have certainly had their ups-and-downs this season, but the Dodgers would never seriously consider leaving them out.
Starters (4): Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Blake Snell, Tarik Skubal, Tyler Glasnow
There's not much to say about what's probably the best rotation going into the postseason. Snell and Glasnow have both battled injury this season but came back when the Dodgers needed them most. It might be too much to ask that any of Yamamoto, Snell, or Glasnow replicate their dominance from last year, but they'll certainly try.
Relievers: (9): Tanner Scott, Roki Sasaki, Alex Vesia, Evan Phillips, Brock Stewart, Justin Wrobleski, Edwin Díaz, Kris Bubic, Edgardo Henriquez
Just like 2025, this is where things get dicey. The Dodgers' bullpen isn't quite as banged up or as unreliable as they were last year, but they're not the air-tight, bulletproof coterie that their combined salaries suggest they should be. Henriquez will be coming straight off of the IL to rejoin the team in the NLDS, and Díaz, Sasaki, and Scott are all woefully unpredictable.
There is some thought that the Dodgers might carry eight relievers instead of nine, to free up a spot on the position player side for a guy like Kim. In this scenario, we'll stick with them taking nine. If not, Bubic is the most obvious cut. Last one in, first one out.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] NLDS notes: Josue De Paula, Shohei Ohtani, Freddie Freeman
item.dc:creator: Jacob Macofsky
item.description: While eight teams battle it out to see who will advance to the Division Series, the Dodgers are among four teams using this time off to prepare for October baseball. After winning an even 100 games in the regular season, the Dodgers secured a first-round bye and will await the winner of the NL Wild Card matchup between the Atlanta Braves and Philadelphia Phillies. While the Dodgers continue to add the finishing touches to their postseason roster, there are some lingering questions as to which pl
item.content:encoded:
While eight teams battle it out to see who will advance to the Division Series, the Dodgers are among four teams using this time off to prepare for October baseball.
After winning an even 100 games in the regular season, the Dodgers secured a first-round bye and will await the winner of the NL Wild Card matchup between the Atlanta Braves and Philadelphia Phillies. While the Dodgers continue to add the finishing touches to their postseason roster, there are some lingering questions as to which players will be a part of the team's depth chart.
21-year-old outfielder Josue De Paula made his presence known while filling in for the then-injured Shohei Ohtani, slashing .323/.500/.581 across 42 plate appearances before he was sent down to Triple-A Oklahoma City. Sonja Chen of MLB.com believes that both De Paula and utility man Hyeseong Kim can make an impact on the postseason roster, with the former being relegated to pinch-hit opportunities due to his lack of big-league experience in the outfield.
Of course, De Paula is capable of playing the corner outfield, but we only saw him play six innings in left as a Dodger. And given how important defense is in the postseason, I doubt we will see him in the field unless it's an emergency.
The month of September has given Shohei Ohtani plenty of time to prepare for his third consecutive postseason run with the Dodgers. The Dodgers still have another three days to prepare for the NLDS, and Ohtani is using this time to get his swing in the right place, per Chen.
"Everything is feeling great physically," general manager Brandon Gomes said on a Zoom call with the media on Tuesday. "The swings, once he came back, overall were in a good place. And using these five days to continue to get reps and feeling good into this series is really important. But feels like he's in a great spot."
Freddie Freeman had his power zapped in the second half of the regular season, hitting just one home run while posting a slugging percentage of .339. Freeman dealt with patellar tendonitis in his right knee, but entering the NLDS, he said that he's feeling a lot better, reports Jack Harris of the California Post.
"I truly feel good right now, physically," Freeman said on Tuesday, during a video conference with reporters ahead of the Dodgers' first pre-National League Division Series bye week workout. "So it's on me now to figure out the mechanics of the swing in the next five days. And I have all the confidence in myself that I will figure that out by [Game 1 on] Saturday."
