item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers beat the San Francisco Giants, 2-0, on Friday night and improved to 98-62 on the year.
Two-time Cy Young award winner Tarik Skubal unleashed another masterpiece with seven scoreless innings, 10 strikeouts, no walks and just three hits allowed. Offensively, Will Smith had a three-hit evening while two second inning solo home runs were collected by Teoscar Hernández and Andy Pages (his first home run since being activated off the injured list).
Ahead of Friday's game, the Dodgers demoted an infielder to make room on the roster to activate catcher Dalton Rushing. Manager Dave Roberts spoke on the kind of role fans can expect from Rushing down the stretch.
“At the most it would be three pinch-hit at-bats, so just conduct at-bats and see what you got,” Roberts said. “Just the circumstances of his situation, it’s just tough to just be hurt, come back, then be hurt again, and then take three pinch-hit at-bats to potentially then say, ‘Hey, you’re on the roster.’"
Additionally, Roberts had a message for rookie Josue De Paula after he was optioned to Triple-A following a productive first 11 games at the major league level. The reasoning, he revealed, was that De Paula could act as a spark plug while superstar Shohei Ohtani was on the injured list — and during his time on the shelf, it's exactly what the 21-year-old provided.
“This was the original thought, that once Shohei gets back, we’re going to send him out,” Roberts said. “We had a runway to give him, which we gave him and he performed more than admirably. This also, as far as the timing, just gives us an opportunity to potentially have him back for the postseason. He’s a part of the conversation, and he’s earned that, and that’s what I told him last night.”
Finally, there is an update on southpaw Blake Snell after he lasted just one inning due to groin discomfort during his most recent start. Luckily for Dodgers fans, the team announced that Snell will make his next scheduled start on Saturday during the penultimate regular season game.

Tom Verducci at Sports Illustrated wrote about Skubal being the latest ace to join
item.content:encoded:
Tarik Skubal's final regular season tuneup went about as well as he and the Dodgers could have hoped, with 10 strikeouts in seven scoreless innings on only 75 pitches, with no walks against the San Francisco Giants on Friday night. On the season the left-hander had a 2.72 ERA and 3.06 xERA in 158 2/3 innings, including a 2.61 ERA, 3.15 xERA, and 23.2-percent strikeout-minus-walk rate in 10 starts for the Dodgers.
Tom Verducci at Sports Illustrated wrote about Skubal being the latest ace to join the Dodgers starting rotation, looking forward to an October run. Skubal on the Dodgers:
"It's awesome to be a part of something where the standard is winning a World Series. That's the way everybody goes about their business, from ownership to president to GM to manager to players, and then you talk about support staff and the chefs in the kitchen, the flight attendants … They all go out of their way to make sure you have everything you need to go out there and perform. I feel like everyone in this organization is rowing in the same direction and everybody wants a World Series just as bad as the players do."
Jarrett Seidler at Baseball Prospectus ranked all 30 MLB front offices and wrote many words about his hierarchy over the last few weeks. After writing about Nos. 21-30 and Nos. 11-20, Seidler on Thursday wrote about his top 10 front offices, with the Dodgers No. 2 overall, one of three teams in his top tier along with the top-spot Brewers and No. 3 Rays. From Seidler:
The Dodgers remain the best team around at trades, both buying and selling. They remain at or near the top in draft acquisition, player development, and research. They are going to be one of the best teams in baseball deep into the 2030s on an annual basis. They got Shohei Ohtani to sign with them. So there's a lot going for them.
But I just don't know how one can call the guys who signed the Kyle Tucker deal seven months ago—a deal that is currently trending towards being the literal worst contract in the history of the sport—the best front office in baseball, ultimately.
Baseball America named its players of the year at every level. Josue De Paula, who won Texas League MVP, was named Double-A player of the year by BA, and California League MVP Easton Shelton was named Class-A player of the year. Eduardo Quintero lost out to Great Lakes outfield mate Charles Davalan for Midwest League MVP, but Quintero was tabbed by BA as High-A player of the year.
Other Dodgers minor leaguers named All-Stars at their level were James Tibbs III as designated hitter in Triple-A, third baseman Jake Gelof in Double-A, Davalan and pitcher Zach Root in High-A, plus third baseman Chase Harlan and outfielder Jaron Elkins in Class-A.
Triple-A end-of-season awards should be announced on Saturday, with the Triple-A title game coming at 7:05 p.m. PT in Las Vegas between PCL title-winning Oklahoma City and Rochester, the International League champs.

item.source: ABC News - Breaking News, Latest News and Videos

item.description: Teoscar Hernández, Andy Pages hit home runs, Skubal strikes out 10 as Dodgers beat Giants 2-0 Teoscar Hernández and Andy Pages hit home runs in the second inning, leading the Los Angeles Dodgers to a 2-0 win over the San Francisco Giants SAN FRANCISCO -- Teoscar Hernández and Andy Pages hit home runs in the second inning to back Tarik Skubal's three-hit, seven-inning performance, and the Los Angeles Dodgers beat the San Francisco Giants 2-0 on Friday night. Shohei Ohtani went 0 for 4 with three
item.content:encoded:
Teoscar Hernández, Andy Pages hit home runs, Skubal strikes out 10 as Dodgers beat Giants 2-0
Teoscar Hernández and Andy Pages hit home runs in the second inning, leading the Los Angeles Dodgers to a 2-0 win over the San Francisco Giants
SAN FRANCISCO -- Teoscar Hernández and Andy Pages hit home runs in the second inning to back Tarik Skubal's three-hit, seven-inning performance, and the Los Angeles Dodgers beat the San Francisco Giants 2-0 on Friday night.
Shohei Ohtani went 0 for 4 with three strikeouts in his third game back after a 13-game stint on the injured list because of right biceps discomfort.
Skubal (12-7) struck out 10, including four straight during one stretch, and didn't walk a batter in his 10th start for the two-time defending World Series champions since being acquired from Detroit on Aug. 2. The Dodgers had won each of his previous six outings as he went 4-0 over his last four decisions spanning six starts since a loss to Milwaukee on Aug. 16.
It was the two-time reigning AL Cy Young Award winner's fourth double-digit strikeout game of the season, second with Los Angeles.
Roki Sasaki pitched a perfect eighth with a pair of strikeouts before Tanner Scott finished the one hour, 53 minute game for his 24th save. It was the second-fastest game in the ballpark's 27-year history and the fastest Giants-Dodgers game since a 1:50 contest on Aug. 30, 1958, in the second game of a doubleheader, according to MLB.
Giants starter Yunior Marte (0-2) surrendered the two home runs among his six hits in five innings. Earlier in the day, San Francisco welcomed back former closer Camilo Doval, claimed off waivers after they dealt him to the Yankees ahead of the 2025 trade deadline.
Manager Dave Roberts gave utility man Tommy Edman a day off to rest and planned to sit some regulars or give them shorter stints in Sunday's regular-season finale.
Los Angeles has won six straight against the Giants and is 7-4 this year to capture the season series for a fifth straight season, going 47-22 during that time.
The Dodgers have held opponents to four or fewer runs in 108 games, going 82-26 in those contests.
LHP Blake Snell (4-1, 1.86 ERA) pitches Saturday against his former Giants team, which counters with LHP Matt Wilkinson (1-3, 3.65).
___

item.title: [Los Angeles Times] Commentary: Dodgers' three-peat hopes rest on their four aces — and bottom-of-order production
item.dc:creator: Bill Shaikin
item.description: - Click here to listen to this article - - The Dodgers’ path to a third straight World Series title will depend on four frontline starters, but manager Dave Roberts hopes his offense won’t leave them carrying the load. - In a 2-0 win over San Francisco, Teoscar Hernández and Andy Pages offered a timely reminder that the Dodgers will need consistent production from the bottom half of the lineup in the playoffs. - Hernández is a proven October hitter, while Pages is finding his swing after c
item.content:encoded:
- Click here to listen to this article
-
- The Dodgers’ path to a third straight World Series title will depend on four frontline starters, but manager Dave Roberts hopes his offense won’t leave them carrying the load.
- In a 2-0 win over San Francisco, Teoscar Hernández and Andy Pages offered a timely reminder that the Dodgers will need consistent production from the bottom half of the lineup in the playoffs.
- Hernández is a proven October hitter, while Pages is finding his swing after coming back from a broken hand.
SAN FRANCISCO — This is the 60th anniversary of the 1966 World Series, in which the losing team did not score for the final 33 innings of the series.
That losing team was the Dodgers. Over the final three games of the series, Jim Palmer, Wally Bunker and Dave McNally of the Baltimore Orioles each pitched a complete-game shutout.
That art of pitching is not in style today. Yoshinobu Yamamoto pitched two complete games last October, but he cannot pitch every game, even if he left that impression upon the Toronto Blue Jays.
The Dodgers’ clearest and cleanest route to a three-peat nonetheless rests upon the four shoulders of Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow. If the four aces can do to October opponents what the 1966 Orioles did to the Dodgers, or some reasonable 21st century facsimile, we’ll see you at the parade.
Does Dodgers manager Dave Roberts believe his starting pitchers will have to carry the load in October?
“I hope not,” Roberts said.
Tarik Skubal gives up just three hits and strikes out 10 in his final start before the postseason to help carry the Dodgers to a 2-0 win over the Giants.
Friday’s 2-0 victory over the San Francisco Giants offered two encouraging swings. Teoscar Hernández and Andy Pages each hit home runs, a reminder that a properly tuned Dodgers offense runs on more than Shohei Ohtani, Mookie Betts, Freddie Freeman and Will Smith.
Skubal scattered three hits and struck out 10 in seven scoreless innings, which would have gone for naught without the Hernández and Pages home runs. Given that the Dodgers were playing the Giants and the remains of their depleted roster, it was something of a warning sign: this could happen against a postseason team.
No team can plan to score a lot of runs against the Dodgers’ starters. The opposing game plan would be to neutralize them and keep the game close enough to where one or two big swings can make the difference. The Giants, who have the National League’s second-worst record, almost pulled it off.
“When you get to the postseason, they’re going to try to eliminate Shohei and try to make other guys beat you,” Roberts said. “So it always sort of comes to the middle to the bottom of the order, where you’ve either got to get guys on base or get hits, get big hits.”
In October, Hernández is who you want at bat. He has homered in six of the seven postseason series he has played for the Dodgers, including each of the last five. In 33 postseason games for the Dodgers, he has driven in 25 runs.
For most players, offensive production drops in October, when batters face the best pitchers from the best teams. For Hernández, his career OPS is .796 in the regular season and .792 in the postseason.
And, for all his summer struggles, he is batting .354 this month, with an OPS just shy of 1.000. He’ll be, as the league-issued hoodies used to say, October ready.
For Pages, however, last October was cruel.
This October was not looking particularly promising, either. Pages missed 27 games because of a broken hand, leaving him the final six games of the regular season to get his swing back into rhythm.
“You think that you take five weeks off,” Roberts said, “that your timing is going to be off a little bit.”
So far, so good: five hits in 12 at-bats, including the home run Friday.
Pages ended the regular season last year with four hits in his final 28 at-bats. That, Roberts said, tells him this October will be different for Pages.
“I think the one thing is the confidence, how he went into last October really scuffling, and it sort of bled into October,” Roberts said, “where I think right now he feels really confident, swinging the bat well, and the hope is that this one bleeds into October as well.
“So, I think it’s definitely a different result going into October, and then also his headspace. There’s a lot more confidence this year.”
In 2025, when the Dodgers won the World Series, they ranked second among the 30 major league clubs in runs scored, and in home runs. In 2024, when they won the World Series, they ranked third in runs scored, and in home runs.
The Dodgers rank fourth in runs scored this year, and seventh in home runs. The offense is down some, if not much. In all the national postseason hype, the Dodgers projections will boil down to one sentence: Can anyone stop those starters?
“I think at first glance that’s what you see in our ballclub,” Roberts said. “But we have a lot of talented, really good hitters and I hope they work hand in hand and not just our pitching and defense carry us.”
For the Dodgers, the postseason opens one week from Saturday. If the Dodgers roll out the 1966 playbook, their October stay will be short.

item.description: Los Dodgers blanquean a Giants 2-0 con jonrones de Teoscar Hernández y Andy Pages Tarik Skubal ponchó a 10 bateadores en siete entradas y permitió apenas tres hits para liderar la victoria de Los Ángeles sobre San Francisco. Skubal permitió apenas tres hits en siete entradas, ponchó a 10
item.content:encoded:
Los Dodgers blanquean a Giants 2-0 con jonrones de Teoscar Hernández y Andy Pages
Tarik Skubal ponchó a 10 bateadores en siete entradas y permitió apenas tres hits para liderar la victoria de Los Ángeles sobre San Francisco.
Los Angeles Dodgers vencieron 2-0 a los San Francisco Giants este viernes, impulsados por los jonrones de Teoscar Hernández y Andy Pages en la segunda entrada y una destacada actuación del lanzador Tarik Skubal.
Skubal permitió apenas tres hits en siete entradas, ponchó a 10 bateadores y no concedió boletos. El lanzador consiguió así su victoria número 12 de la temporada y mejoró su registro a 12-7.
Fue la décima apertura de Skubal con los Dodgers desde que el equipo lo adquirió de los Detroit Tigers el 2 de agosto. Los Ángeles ha ganado sus seis aperturas anteriores y el lanzador acumula un registro de 4-0 en sus últimas cuatro decisiones, que abarcan seis aperturas.
El actual ganador del premio Cy Young de la Liga Americana consiguió además su cuarto partido de la temporada con al menos 10 ponches, el segundo desde su llegada a Los Ángeles.
Hernández y Pages aportaron los únicos batazos de Los Ángeles
Los Dodgers construyeron toda su ventaja en la segunda entrada.
Teoscar Hernández conectó el primero de los dos cuadrangulares y, posteriormente, Andy Pages también envió la pelota fuera del parque para colocar el marcador 2-0.
El abridor de San Francisco, Yunior Marte, permitió los dos jonrones entre los seis imparables que concedió durante cinco entradas. Marte cargó con la derrota y dejó su récord en 0-2.
Sasaki y Scott completaron la blanqueada
Después de la salida de Skubal, Roki Sasaki lanzó una octava entrada perfecta y ponchó a dos bateadores.
Tanner Scott se encargó del noveno inning y consiguió su salvamento número 24 de la temporada.
El encuentro duró apenas una hora y 53 minutos, convirtiéndose, según MLB, en el segundo partido más rápido disputado en los 27 años de historia del estadio de San Francisco. También fue el juego entre Dodgers y Giants más rápido desde un encuentro de una hora y 50 minutos disputado el 30 de agosto de 1958.
Ohtani sigue buscando ritmo tras su regreso
Shohei Ohtani terminó de 0-4 con tres ponches en su tercer partido desde que regresó de la lista de lesionados, donde permaneció 13 juegos debido a molestias en el bíceps derecho.
Los Dodgers, por su parte, han ganado seis partidos consecutivos contra los Giants y tienen marca de 7-4 frente a San Francisco esta temporada, con lo que aseguraron la serie de temporada por quinta campaña consecutiva.
Durante ese período de cinco temporadas, Los Ángeles tiene un registro de 47-22 contra los Giants.
Snell abrirá el sábado
Los Dodgers continuarán la serie este sábado con el zurdo Blake Snell, quien tiene marca de 4-1 y una efectividad de 1.86.
Snell se enfrentará a su antiguo equipo, mientras que San Francisco enviará al montículo al zurdo Matt Wilkinson, con récord de 1-3 y efectividad de 3.65.

item.title: [New York Post] Roki Sasaki, Tanner Scott look like Dodgers’ playoff bullpen anchors
item.dc:creator: Dylan Hernandez
item.description: SAN FRANCISCO – The sequence was promising on paper. In practice on Friday night, it was spectacular. Roki Sasaki in the eighth inning. Tanner Scott in the ninth. Manager Dave Roberts emphasized they wouldn’t necessarily be deployed in that order come the playoffs, but their performances in the Dodgers’ 2-0 victory over the Giants indicated they could be the foundation of a championship-caliber bullpen for the Dodgers. “I don’t want you to pigeonhole me into using these guys in certain roles, bu
item.content:encoded:
SAN FRANCISCO – The sequence was promising on paper. In practice on Friday night, it was spectacular.
Roki Sasaki in the eighth inning.
Tanner Scott in the ninth.
Manager Dave Roberts emphasized they wouldn’t necessarily be deployed in that order come the playoffs, but their performances in the Dodgers’ 2-0 victory over the Giants indicated they could be the foundation of a championship-caliber bullpen for the Dodgers.
“I don’t want you to pigeonhole me into using these guys in certain roles, but, yeah, I think it’s just better to have as many guys that you have confidence in leverage (situations),” Roberts said.
Sasaki followed a seven-inning effort by starter Tarik Skubal by striking out two batters in a perfect eighth inning.
Scott retired the side in the ninth to record his 24th save.
On their World Series run last year, the bullpen was something the Dodgers had to work around. They were extremely dependent on their starting pitchers, whom they counted on not only to pitch deeper into games but also make relief contributions. Sasaki’s emergence as closer was as much a reflection of their lack of options as it was of the Japanese fireballer’s gifts.
The Dodgers should enter the playoffs next month with an entirely different feel.
Scott has recovered from his nightmare season last year, looking more like the Padres relief ace who shut down Shohei Ohtani in the 2024 playoffs to earn a $72-million payday with the Dodgers.
As for the 24-year-old Sasaki, he looks even better as a reliever than he did last year.
“I think the fastball’s better,” Roberts said. “I think the split’s better. It’s also nice that he’s already done it. So, just in total, he’s just a better pitcher than he was last year and a lot more confident. And certainly, the stuff was really good the last couple outings.”
Four of the six fastballs Sasaki threw were clocked at faster than 100 mph.
The other two registered readings of more than 99 mph.
“Overall, he just keeps getting better,” Scott said. “Even when he was starting, I thought he was pretty dominant. For him to get moved to the bullpen as we go into October, it’s huge for us.”
Sasaki started seven games after the All-Star break and was 2-0 with a 3.05 earned-run average. A blister on his pitching hand landed him on the injured list. When he returned earlier this week, he did so as a reliever.
He also struck out two batters in his other relief appearance, a scoreless inning on Tuesday against the San Diego Padres.
“Throughout the season, I’ve sharpened myself technically,” Sasaki said in Japanese. “Compared to last year, I feel much better in that respect.”
Sasaki will likely pitch next in the regular-season finale on Sunday, Roberts said.
He could close out games again in October, as Roberts said there could be games in which he calls on Scott to pitch against a particularly dangerous segment of the opposing lineup earlier in the game.
Scott said he was open to pitching in any situation.
“Just get outs,” Scott said. “That’s all that matters in October. Get outs.
“October is about winning every single game. It really doesn’t matter what roles you get asked to do. Just go out there and do it.”

item.content:encoded:
Los Dodgers blanquean a los Gigantes con 2 jonrones y 10 ponches de Skubal
SAN FRANCISCO — Teoscar Hernández y Andy Pagés conectaron jonrones en la segunda entrada para respaldar la actuación de Tarik Skubal, quien permitió tres hits en siete innings, y los Dodgers de Los Ángeles vencieron 2-0 a los Gigantes de San Francisco la noche del viernes.
Shohei Ohtani se fue de 4-0 con tres ponches en su tercer juego de regreso tras una estadía de 13 partidos en la lista de lesionados debido a molestias en el bíceps derecho.
Skubal (12-7) ponchó a 10, incluidos cuatro consecutivos durante un tramo, y no otorgó bases por bolas en su décima apertura con los bicampeones defensores de la Serie Mundial desde que fue adquirido de Detroit el 2 de agosto. Los Dodgers habían ganado cada una de sus seis salidas anteriores, mientras él tuvo marca de 4-0 en sus últimas cuatro decisiones a lo largo de seis aperturas desde una derrota ante Milwaukee el 16 de agosto.
Fue el cuarto juego de la temporada del ganador vigente en dos ocasiones del premio Cy Young de la Liga Americana con ponches de doble dígito, el segundo con Los Ángeles.
Roki Sasaki lanzó un octavo inning perfecto con un par de ponches antes de que Tanner Scott cerrara el juego, que duró una hora y 53 minutos, para su 24to salvamento. Fue el segundo juego más rápido en los 27 años de historia del estadio.
El abridor de los Gigantes, el dominicano Yunior Marte (0-2), permitió los dos jonrones entre los seis hits que concedió en cinco innings. Más temprano en el día, San Francisco dio la bienvenida de regreso al ex cerrador Camilo Doval, reclamado en waivers después de que lo traspasaran a los Yankees antes de la fecha límite de cambios de 2025. ___

item.description: El campocorto de los Dodgers de Los Ángeles, Mookie Betts, está teniendo un septiembre demente en el plato y parece alguno que puede sobrellevar la ataque en la postemporada. item.content:encoded:
El campocorto de los Dodgers de Los Ángeles, Mookie Betts, está teniendo un septiembre demente en el plato y parece alguno que puede sobrellevar la ataque en la postemporada.
El demente septiembre de Betts
Betts está bateando .367 en septiembre hasta el viernes, con 21 carreras impulsadas, seis jonrones y nueve dobles.
Tiene un OPS de 1.117 y un wRC+ de 219, ambas métricas resaltan cuán elitista ha sido. Ha sido, con diferencia, su mejor mes de la temporada y es similar a sus mejores marcas como MVP.
Anuncio
Da boletos el 16% de sus apariciones en el plato y se poncha sólo el 8,5% de las veces.
Su enfoque en el plato luce excelente, con buenas decisiones de swing y un esforzado dominio de la zona de strike que empuja a los lanzadores a realizar lanzamientos más desafiantes de los que desearían.
Cuando hace swing, tiene 32 bolas aceptablemente golpeadas este mes y la velocidad de salida promedio es de 92.6 mph, la más entrada del año hasta el momento.
Por qué los Dodgers necesitaban esta producción de Betts
Para sorpresa de nadie, Betts fue el mejor bateador del equipo en septiembre. Su wRC+ solo rivaliza con Josue De Paula, aunque el tamaño de su muestra fue mucho más pequeño que el de Betts.
Anuncio
Shohei Ohtani se perdió la viejo parte del mes por una ultraje en el padrino derecho, mientras que Andy Pages asimismo se perdió la viejo parte del mes y regresó solo en los últimos días.
Por otra parte, Freddie Freeman y Tommy Edman se han vuelto prácticamente fríos, lo que solo aumenta aún más la escazes de que alguno dé un paso al frente.
Betts ha sido el hombre que ha llevado la ataque, con 25 carreras ponderadas creadas, según FanGraphs, la viejo cantidad en el equipo, superado por Teoscar Hernández, quien tiene 19.
Con su surgimiento y la caída de Edman, Betts asumió el puesto de primer bate hasta que Ohtani regresó, y su maniobra ha sido tan bueno que incluso luego del regreso de la superestrella japonesa, el manager Dave Roberts todavía mantiene a Betts como líder contra los zurdos.
Anuncio
¿Podrá Betts sustentar esto en la postemporada?
Betts tiene un historial de mejorar durante los playoffs. En su primera temporada con los Dodgers, bateó .296/.378/.493 con OPS+ de 135 hasta octubre, cuando los Dodgers ganaron la Serie Mundial.
2021 fue más de lo mismo, bateando .319/.377/.404 con 116 wRC+. 2022 y 2023 terminaron temprano para los Dodgers y Betts tuvo problemas entreambos primaveras.
En 2024, cuando los Dodgers ganaron uno de sus primeros títulos consecutivos, Betts estuvo mágico, bateando .290/.387/.585 con 151 wRC+.
Durante la viejo parte de la temporada, Betts no fue lo que los fanáticos de Mookie esperaban, con un bautizo promedio de la muérdago y una gran defensa en el campocorto.
Anuncio
A partir de mediados de agosto y hasta septiembre, cambió el estandarte y dejó al manager Dave Roberts impresionado y sorprendido.
“No podría decirte que vi esto [coming]”, dijo Roberts. “Pero se ha vuelto más esforzado. Ha trabajado duro en eso… Y el hecho de que todo salga aceptablemente ha sido increíble. Simplemente no importa dónde lo golpees, a quién se enfrenta, [what’s] la situación… está tomando buenos turnos al bate”.
Betts, mientras tanto, sabía que su antigua producción a nivel de Tahúr Más Valioso todavía estaba en él.
“Sé que todavía soy capaz de hacerlo”, dijo Betts. “Sé que estaba ahí en alguna parte”.
De cara a octubre, pocos bateadores deberían hacer apreciar mejor a los fanáticos.
Su experiencia, anejo con su nueva producción, deberían ayudarlo a encajar en la fórmula, anejo con el pitcheo abridor de calidad, que lo colocará a él y a los Dodgers de 2026 en la inmortalidad de la MLB.

item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers shortstop Mookie Betts is having a crazy September at the plate, and he looks like someone who can carry the offense in the postseason.
Betts’ Crazy September
Betts is hitting .367 in September entering Friday, with 21 RBIs, six home runs, and nine doubles.
He has a 1.117 OPS and a 219 wRC+, both metrics highlighting just how elite he has been. It has been his best month of the season by far, and it is akin to his MVP bests.
He is walking 16% of plate appearances and striking out on just 8.5% of the time.
His approach at the plate looks great, with good swing decisions and a strong command of the strike zone that pushes pitchers to throw more challenging pitches than they would want.
When he does swing, he has 32 hard-hit balls this month, and the average exit velocity is 92.6 mph, the highest of the year thus far.
Why the Dodgers needed this production from Betts
To no one’s surprise, Betts was the team’s best hitter in September. His wRC+ is only rivaled by Josue De Paula, though his sample size was much smaller than Betts’.
Shohei Ohtani missed most of the month with a right-arm injury, while Andy Pages also missed the majority of the month, returning only in the last few days.
Additionally, Freddie Freeman and Tommy Edman have gone mostly cold, only further increasing the need for someone to step up.
Betts has been the guy to carry the offense, with 25 weighted runs created, according to FanGraphs, the most on the team, second to Teoscar Hernandez, who has 19.
With his emergence and Edman’s slump, Betts took over the leadoff spot until Ohtani returned, and his play has been so good that even after the Japanese superstar returned, manager Dave Roberts still has Betts lead off against lefties.
Can Betts keep this up in the postseason?
Betts has a track record of stepping up during the playoffs. In his first season with the Dodgers, he hit .296/.378/.493 with a 135 OPS+ through October, when the Dodgers won the World Series.
2021 was more of the same, hitting .319/.377/.404 with a 116 wRC+. 2022 and 2023 ended early for the Dodgers, and Betts struggled both years.
In 2024, when the Dodgers won one of their first consecutive titles, Betts was magical, hitting .290/.387/.585 with a 151 wRC+.
For most of the season, Betts wasn’t the Mookie fans expected, with league-average hitting and great defense at shortstop.
Starting in mid-August and into September, he flipped the script and left manager Dave Roberts impressed and surprised.
“I couldn’t tell you that I saw this [coming],” Roberts said. “But he’s got stronger. He’s worked hard on that … And just for it to come together has been great. It just doesn’t matter where you hit him, who he’s facing, [what’s] the situation –– he’s taking good at-bats.”
Betts, meanwhile, knew his former MVP-level production was still in him.
“I know I’m still capable of it,” Betts said. “I know it was in there somewhere.”
Heading into October, few hitters should make fans feel better.
His experience, along with his newfound production, should help him fit into the formula, alongside the quality starting pitching, that puts him and the 2026 Dodgers into MLB immortality.

item.content:encoded:
ドジャースでワールドシリーズ3連覇を狙う大谷翔平。
32歳になったスターは、このほど故障者リストから復帰した。23日は1安打、24日には2安打を放ち、復調に向けて歩みを続けている。
そうしたなか、MLBは2026年のユニフォーム売上ランキングを発表。
大谷は2010年の集計開始以降で、4年連続売り上げ1位となった史上初のMLB選手になった。
「大谷の人気は、新たな高みに達した。2010年に集計が開始されて以来、メジャーリーグで初めて4シーズン連続で『最も人気なユニフォーム選手』になったのだ。2023年以降、アメリカ、日本、そして世界中で最も多くのユニフォームを売り上げている」とのこと。
9位には山本由伸（ロサンゼルス・ドジャース）、20位には村上宗隆（シカゴ・ホワイトソックス）も入った。
野球界最高の人気選手である大谷は、復帰後に確かな復調を見せている。
パドレス戦ではMLB屈指のクローザーであるメイソン・ミラーが投じた時速102.6マイル（約165キロ）の速球を捉えた。
水曜には384フィート（約117メートル）、木曜にも382フィート（約116メートル）の大飛球をかっ飛ばし、木曜日の平均打球初速は101.9マイル（時速164キロ）を記録した。
『LA Times』は「大谷は故障者リストから復帰後、力強い打球を放ち、ストライクゾーンの見極めも向上させるなど、好ましい兆候を見せている。もし膝と上腕二頭筋の怪我を完全に克服したのなら、ドジャースがワールドシリーズ3連覇に挑む上で重要な役割を果たすはず」と伝えている。
また、デーブ・ロバーツ監督も「今後の兆しであってほしいね」と期待を口にしていた。
筆者：井上大輔（編集部）
画像提供：Getty Images

item.title: [DodgersBeat] Dodgers Activate Dalton Rushing; Option Alex Freeland
item.dc:creator: Cody Snavely
item.description: SAN FRANCISCO, CA—As expected, before Game One of a three-game series against the San Francisco Giants, the Los Angeles Dodgers activated left-handed-hitting catcher Dalton Rushing from the 10-day injured list. In order to make room on the 28-man roster, the Dodgers optioned infielder Alex Freeland to Triple-A Oklahoma City. item.content:encoded:
SAN FRANCISCO, CA—As expected, before Game One of a three-game series against the San Francisco Giants, the Los Angeles Dodgers activated left-handed-hitting catcher Dalton Rushing from the 10-day injured list.
In order to make room on the 28-man roster, the Dodgers optioned infielder Alex Freeland to Triple-A Oklahoma City.
For Rushing, these next three games are his final chance to make his case for a spot on the Dodgers’ postseason roster. Because of his UCL injury, his role will be limited to pinch-hitting off the bench, but the second-year catcher has one last chance to show the Dodgers he can still provide an impact bat when October arrives.
This is Rushing’s second return from the injured list this month for the same injury, as the lefty lasted only eight at-bats before heading back to the IL and receiving a PRP injection to calm the pain.
In that time, while no longer on the roster due to the activation of Shohei Ohtani, the role of a left-handed hitter off the bench is also down to Josue De Paula, who posted an OPS over 1.000 and hit .323 in his short but successful stint at the major league level.
As for Alex Freeland is headed back to the Minors after joining the Dodgers when active rosters expanded on September 1st. At the time, the Dodgers opted for Freeland over an outfield prospect despite Teoscar Hernández and Kyle Tucker both struggling, with James Tibbs III appearing to be the expected choice for that extra position-player spot.
Instead, Freeland got the call and put together a solid month, hitting .250/.413/.389 with two doubles, one home run and two RBI across 17 games, including 10 starts. He last appeared Saturday against the San Francisco Giants.
It was an inconsistent season overall for the 25-year-old, who surprisingly made the Dodgers’ Opening Day roster over Hyeseong Kim. Freeland showed flashes at both the Major League level and with Oklahoma City, and with this move, he can rejoin the Comets for their Triple-A National Championship Game in Las Vegas on Saturday.
Unfortunately for Freeland, being optioned this late in the season also closes the door on a potential postseason roster spot. He cannot be added to the Dodgers’ National League Division Series roster in time for Game One on Saturday, October 3rd, unless he replaces a player who is placed on the injured list.

He has also written for multiple websites, such as Dodgers Way, Dodgers Low-Down, and Dodgers Tailgate. A Wilmington University graduate, Snavely is an avid Dodgers fan who uses his advanced baseball knowledge to keep fans updated on the latest storylines, rumors, and opinions on Dodgers baseball.

item.title: [PR TIMES] Historic Shohei Ohtani Tokyo Series Jersey to Be Featured at YouMeWe's 2026 Gala Ahead of Auction
item.description: Historic Shohei Ohtani Tokyo Series Jersey to Be Featured at YouMeWe's 2026 Gala Ahead of Auction Move With Purpose activation to connect jersey's return to Tokyo with youth empowerment programming TOKYO — September 25, 2026 — YouMeWe, a Tokyo-based nonprofit focused on teen empowerment in orphanages, today announced that the Los Angeles Dodgers jersey worn by Shohei Ohtani during his historic first MLB game in Japan will be on display at the YouMeWe Gala 2026 on October 14, ahead of its closing
item.content:encoded:
Historic Shohei Ohtani Tokyo Series Jersey to Be Featured at YouMeWe's 2026 Gala Ahead of Auction
Move With Purpose activation to connect jersey's return to Tokyo with youth empowerment programming
TOKYO — September 25, 2026 — YouMeWe, a Tokyo-based nonprofit focused on teen empowerment in orphanages, today announced that the Los Angeles Dodgers jersey worn by Shohei Ohtani during his historic first MLB game in Japan will be on display at the YouMeWe Gala 2026 on October 14, ahead of its closing bid on TheRealest.com on October 17.
The jersey is being brought to Tokyo through a collaboration with The Realest, the authentication and marketplace platform operating in partnership with the MLBPA.
Ohtani wore the jersey on March 18, 2025, at the Tokyo Dome, in the Tokyo Series opener that marked his first official MLB game played in Japan. It features the first-ever Gold MLB Logoman patch worn in a game, introduced in 2025 to honor MVP, Cy Young, and Rookie of the Year winners alongside the 2025 Tokyo Series emblem and a Fernando Valenzuela No. 34 memorial patch. The jersey is personally signed and inscribed by Ohtani and has been authenticated through MLB on-field authentication, SIA photo-matching, and Fanatics Authentic certification.
As part of the activation, YouMeWe will run a “Move With Purpose” program element for local youth — a movement challenge and up-close viewing designed to connect a milestone piece of baseball history to the organization's ongoing work with young people in Japan.
"Every child deserves someone who believes they can reach the world stage. Shohei Ohtani showed Japan, and the world, that a boy from rural Iwate could become a global inspiration. But thousands of children growing up in Japan's care homes never get the mentors, experiences, or confidence that turn potential into possibility. Baseball reminds us that a shared game can connect people across every language and border. YouMeWe builds those same bridges for teens in care, through mentorship, global exposure, and skills for life after 18. This jersey represents what's possible. Your support makes it reachable, as in our Tanomochi Circle of 50 kids supported weekly," said Michael Perry-Clemons, Founder & CEO of YouMeWe.
The jersey will remain on view through the Gala before bidding closes on TheRealest.com on Saturday, October 17, 2026.
About YouMeWe
YouMeWe is a Tokyo-based nonprofit organization dedicated to empowering teens in Japan through mentorship, education, and community programming, including its Move With Purpose initiative and the Tanomoshi Circle giving community. Learn more at youmewenpo.org.
Media Contact
Michael Perry-Clemons, Founder & CEO, YouMeWe — michael@youmewenpo.org

item.content:encoded:
土曜未明…大谷翔平の“BIGニュース”「ものが違う」 副収入196億円も納得「本当に凄い」
MLBがユニホーム売上ランキングを発表
メジャーリーグ機構（MLB）と選手会は25日（日本時間26日）、「MLBショップ」などにおける今季開幕戦以降のユニホーム売上ランキングを発表し、ドジャースの大谷翔平投手が4年連続で1位に輝いた。土曜未明に駆け巡った快挙に対し、日本のファンは「本当に凄いわ」と鼻高々だった。
MLBの発表によると、追跡調査が開始された2010年以降、4年連続で首位を守った選手は大谷が初だという。大谷はエンゼルス時代から圧倒的な人気を誇ったが、名門ドジャース移籍後にさらに加速。ポストシーズンにも進出したことで、全米での知名度も飛躍的に上昇した。
日本未明の午前2時頃の“最新発表”に対し、日本人ファンからは歓喜と称賛の声が殺到した。「さすがユニコーン」「ユニホーム売上1位は世界一の選手と言う証でしょう」「4年連続ってスゴイな」「引退しても一定数売れそう」「やっぱり大谷翔平はものが違うんだよ」「4年連続1位は凄いね」「人気も実力もNo.1」と誇らしげなコメントが並んだ。
大谷は過去4度のMVPに輝いているだけでなく、「フォーブス」によるとグラウンド外での収入1億2500万ドル（約196億円）は全アスリート1位に立っているという。
2位にヤンキースのアーロン・ジャッジ外野手、3位に「40-40」達成のカブスのピート・クロウ＝アームストロング外野手が続いた。さらに日本勢では、ドジャースの山本由伸投手が9位、今季メジャーデビューを果たしたホワイトソックスの村上宗隆内野手が20位にランクイン。トップ20に日本人選手3人が同時に入る史上初の快挙となった。
（Full-Count編集部）

item.title: [Yardbarker] Alex Freeland Optioned By Dodgers To Activate Dalton Rushing Off Injured list
item.dc:creator: Matthew Moreno
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers activated Dalton Rushing off the 10-day injured list and optioned Alex Freeland to Triple-A Oklahoma City prior to Friday’s game against the San Francisco Giants. Freeland heads back to the Minors after joining the Dodgers when active rosters expanded on Sept. 1. He was chosen over an outfield prospect despite Teoscar Hernández and Kyle Tucker both struggling at the time. James Tibbs III at one point appeared to be the expected choice for the Dodgers’ extra position playe
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers activated Dalton Rushing off the 10-day injured list and optioned Alex Freeland to Triple-A Oklahoma City prior to Friday’s game against the San Francisco Giants.
Freeland heads back to the Minors after joining the Dodgers when active rosters expanded on Sept. 1. He was chosen over an outfield prospect despite Teoscar Hernández and Kyle Tucker both struggling at the time. James Tibbs III at one point appeared to be the expected choice for the Dodgers’ extra position player.
Instead the team elected for Freeland, who hit .250/.413/.389 with two doubles, one home run and two RBI over 17 games (10 starts) this month. Freeland last played on Saturday against the San Francisco Giants.
Freeland endured an inconsistent year after making the Dodgers’ Opening Day roster over Hyeseong Kim. He had some stretches of promise not only at the Major League level, but while with the Comets as well. The 25-year-old conceivably will join Oklahoma City for their Triple-A National Championship game in Las Vegas on Saturday.
With Freeland getting optioned this late in the season, he is not a candidate to make the Dodgers’ postseason roster for the National League Division Series. He would not be eligible to get added in time for Game 1 on Saturday, Oct. 3, unless taking the spot of an injured player.
Rushing is back from a second stint on the injured list due to trouble with his right elbow. The first instance was due to a slight tear in the UCL, but the latest came because of a flexor tendon problem.
It prompted the Dodgers to halt Rushing’s throwing progression and he now has three games to seemingly make up for lost time. Rushing had been projected to be the left-handed bat off the bench for the postseason, but Josue De Paula may now have the inside track for that role.
Dodgers manager Dave Roberts indicated Rushing would receive a maximum of three at-bats as a pinch-hitter this weekend.
Like Andy Pages and Shohei Ohtani earlier this week, Rushing is back without having gone on a rehab assignment in part because of the Minor League season ending. Though, he did log at-bats against Will Klein, who likewise is hopeful to earn a role with the Dodgers come October.

item.content:encoded:
Redacción Deportes, 25 sep (EFE).- El japonés Shohei Ohtani, estrella de los Dodgers de Los Ángeles, volvió a ser el jugador con la camiseta más vendida de las Grandes Ligas, una posición que ocupa por cuarto año consecutivo, según la lista publicada este viernes por MLB y MLB Players, Inc. (Mlbpi).
Ohtani se convirtió así en el primer jugador desde que MLB comenzó a registrar las ventas en 2010, que encadena cuatro temporadas como líder en comercialización de camisetas.
PUBLICIDAD
Desde 2023, los aficionados han comprado la camiseta Nike de Ohtani más que cualquier otra en Estados Unidos, Japón y el resto del mundo, consolidando al jugador japonés como la figura con mayor demanda comercial entre los peloteros de las Grandes Ligas.
El listado, elaborado a partir de las ventas de camisetas Nike realizadas a través de Fanatics, incluido MLBShop.com, desde el Día Inaugural de la temporada 2026, sitúa al capitán de los Yankees de Nueva York, Aaron Judge, en el segundo puesto y al jardinero de los Cachorros de Chicago Pete Crow-Armstrong en el tercero.
PUBLICIDAD
Crow-Armstrong, quien esta temporada se convirtió en el séptimo jugador en la historia de las Mayores y el primero de los Cachorros en conectar al menos 40 jonrones y robar 40 bases, alcanzó el mejor puesto para un jugador de Chicago desde que el puertorriqueño Javier Báez fue tercero en 2018.
El listado también refleja la presencia de otras figuras de alcance internacional. El venezolano Ronald Acuña Jr., de los Bravos de Atlanta, ocupa el cuarto lugar, seguido por el dominicano Fernando Tatis Jr., de los Padres de San Diego.
Los Dodgers colocaron a tres jugadores entre los diez primeros, con Ohtani al frente, Freddie Freeman en el sexto puesto y Mookie Betts en el octavo. El japonés Yoshinobu Yamamoto, también de Los Ángeles, aparece noveno.
La temporada 2026 marcó además un registro inédito para los jugadores japoneses, con tres de ellos entre los 20 primeros de la clasificación, después de que el toletero Munetaka Murakami, de los Medias Blancas de Chicago, debutara en el vigésimo puesto.
PUBLICIDAD
Yamamoto, por su parte, ocupa el noveno lugar, mientras que Ohtani mantiene el liderazgo de una clasificación que vuelve a poner de manifiesto su dimensión dentro y fuera del terreno de juego.
La lista se conoce antes del inicio de las Series de Comodines de ambas ligas, que comenzarán el próximo martes 29 de septiembre, con Ohtani, Judge y Crow-Armstrong entre las principales figuras de unos equipos que ya tienen asegurado su boleto a la Postemporada. EFE
PUBLICIDAD

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Dodgers' Dave Roberts Reveals Message He Gave Josue De Paula After Being Optioned
item.dc:creator: Ricardo Sandoval; Unknown
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers are finally getting healthy just in time for the postseason as they activated superstar Shohei Ohtani off the injured list this week. As a corresponding move, the team decided to option top prospect Josue De Paula. De Paula made a name for himself in 11 contests for Los Angeles, and many fans hoped the Dodgers would go another route when they activated Ohtani. However, the Dodgers optioning De Paula was always going to be the move, as they wanted him to continue getting o
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are finally getting healthy just in time for the postseason as they activated superstar Shohei Ohtani off the injured list this week.
As a corresponding move, the team decided to option top prospect Josue De Paula.
De Paula made a name for himself in 11 contests for Los Angeles, and many fans hoped the Dodgers would go another route when they activated Ohtani.
However, the Dodgers optioning De Paula was always going to be the move, as they wanted him to continue getting opportunities to play at Triple-A before potentially being an option in the postseason.
Manager Dave Roberts loved what he saw from the 21-year-old, and revealed the message he gave De Paula when informing him about his demotion to Triple-A.
“This was the original thought, that once Shohei gets back, we’re going to send him out,” Roberts said. “We had a runway to give him, which we gave him and he performed more than admirably. This also, as far as the timing, just gives us an opportunity to potentially have him back for the postseason. He’s a part of the conversation, and he’searned that, and that’s what I told him last night.”
He added: "It was actually an easier conversation than you guys probably would expect, given how well he’s performed."
Josue De Paula Has Made a Strong Case for the Postseason
De Paula was fantastic in his first 11 games in the majors. He recorded a .323 batting average with a 1.081 OPS, one home run, seven RBIs and 10 hits in 31 at-bats.
De Paula only struck out five times and drew 11 walks.
De Paula's maturity at the plate was evident before his major league debut, and he showed exactly why once he stepped into the batter's box.
His advanced plate discipline and impressive strike-zone judgment are exactly why he is a candidate to make the postseason roster.
“He's done everything he can to put himself in a position to be in the conversation for us as we're making our postseason roster,” president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman said.
One area De Paula does need to improve on is his defense. That won't come to fruition until the offseason, though.
"I just think that — just being candid — I don’t think that he’s valued it as much as he will," Roberts said recently. "And it just has to be important. Certainly, when you get to the big leagues, outs are important, converting outs are important."
The Dodgers have 12 players who appear to be locks to make the postseason roster. De Paula has certainly made his case to be the 13th position player in October, but he'll be competing with Dalton Rushing, who's set to be activated on Friday.

Ricardo Sandoval is a freelance writer with On SI. He is a graduate of California State University, Northridge, and specializes in sports writing, particularly in MLB, NBA and NFL. He previously served as an Associate Editor for Dodgers Nation and has worked with Newsweek and The Sporting News.

New York Yankees slugger Aaron Judge was second for the second straight season, MLB and the players' association affiliate MLB Players, Inc. said Friday. Judge finished third in 2023 and '24. Pete Crow-Armstrong of the Ch
item.content:encoded:
NEW YORK (AP) — Shohei Ohtani has become the first player to lead Major League Baseball jersey sales at the end of four straight seasons since the sport started tracking figures in 2010, among four players in the top 20 on the two-time World Series champion Los Angeles Dodgers.
New York Yankees slugger Aaron Judge was second for the second straight season, MLB and the players' association affiliate MLB Players, Inc. said Friday. Judge finished third in 2023 and '24.
Pete Crow-Armstrong of the Chicago Cubs was third, up from 16th at the end of last season, and Atlanta's Ronald Acuña Jr. was fourth, an increase from 11th last year.
San Diego's Fernando Tatis Jr. was fifth, followed by the Dodgers' Freddie Freeman, Philadelphia's Bryce Harper, the Dodgers' Mookie Betts and Yoshinobu Yamamoto, and the New York Mets' Juan Soto.
Munetaka Murakami of the Chicago White Sox was 20th, and he joined with Ohtani and Yamamoto to become the first trio of Japanese players in the top 20.
Texas' Corey Seager was 11th, followed by Toronto's Vladimir Guerrero Jr., Boston's Adley Rutschman, the Phillies' Kyle Schwarber, Pittsburgh's Paul Skenes, Seattle's Cal Raleigh, Cincinnati's Elly De La Cruz, San Diego's Jackson Merrill and Arizona's Nolan Arenado.
MLB's list tracked sales on Fanatics' sites, including MLBShop.com, since opening day.

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES, CA — Freddie Freeman believes he’s finally beginning to rediscover his swing, and with the Dodgers having secured a first-round bye into the NLDS, the veteran first baseman is encouraged by what he’s seeing from his teammates as October approaches.
Freeman collected two hits in Thursday night’s 4-1 loss to the Padres, both coming after he made an adjustment during his third plate appearance. He explained afterward that he’s starting to feel more comfortable using his lower half, something that had been missing from his swing during his recent struggles.
“I know the last couple of at-bats, a little better. Got more in my legs,” Freeman said. “So, trying to make adjustments pitch to pitch. Just trying to get a feel, and felt something on a foul ball in my third at-bat.”
“Took it into the next couple pitches, got a hit. Took it into the next at-bat, got a hit. So I’ll take it into tomorrow.”
Getting Hot at the Right Time
Although the Dodgers dropped the final two games of their series against San Diego, Freeman is encouraged by the individual performances he’s seeing throughout the lineup, particularly from Shohei Ohtani and Mookie Betts.
“I’m just encouraged with Shohei getting a couple of hits, Mookie staying hot,” Freeman said. “That’s really what it’s all about. Guys getting hot right now.”
“We got the first-round bye, so play some good baseball this weekend and take it into next week.”
Freeman also praised Ohtani’s return to the lineup, including the hard contact he made against Padres closer Mason Miller during Wednesday’s game.
“It’s nice for Shohei to come out there and get some hits. That ball off Mason Miller was special, so I know that would feel good for him,” Freeman said.
“Mookie’s been hot. Teo’s been swinging the bat great. Will’s been really good lately, too. So a couple of us can add on to it, and Kyle, obviously, he’s been really good the last month, too. So we’ve got a good stretch going.”
The first baseman also provided a reassuring update about his own health. Asked about the condition of his knee, Freeman offered a simple response.
“Knee’s good. I feel nothing.”
When asked whether the issue was now yesterday’s news, he confirmed that it was.
“Yeah. Yeah. All good.”
Freeman Isn’t Concerned About the Dodgers’ Record Against Playoff Teams
One of the more interesting exchanges came when Freeman was asked about the Dodgers’ struggles against quality opponents during the second half of the season.
Since their series victories over the Yankees and Phillies, the Dodgers have struggled to win series against teams with winning records, including the Padres, who took two of three at Dodger Stadium this week.
Freeman, however, isn’t particularly interested in revisiting those results.
“I wouldn’t have even known unless you guys asked,” he said. “All we care about is playing good this weekend, these three games, and take that in.”
“It doesn’t matter who we’re playing on Saturday or what we’ve done against those teams. It’s all out the window from Saturday. It’s game on there, but playing good baseball is a good option. Positive things going into the off week.”
It’s an understandable perspective from a veteran who knows that regular-season results offer little comfort once the postseason begins. The Dodgers will certainly have to start producing more runs against elite pitching staffs, but Freeman’s focus is on getting the entire lineup clicking when the games matter most.
A Well-Earned Opportunity to Rest
Freeman also emphasized the importance of the first-round bye, particularly for a team that has endured the physical demands of another long season.
“I think rest for all of us is always nice,” he said. “We’ve been grinding since February, getting ready for the season. Then you go through a 162-game schedule. It’s a lot.”
“So we played really good baseball for six or eight months, and we get rewarded for that. So we’ll take it in and rest up and get ourselves ready to go for Saturday.”
With several key players having returned from injuries in recent weeks, the opportunity to rest and prepare rather than immediately enter a Wild Card series could be especially valuable.
Four Number One Starters
Perhaps Freeman’s most emphatic response came when a reporter referred to another member of the Dodgers’ rotation as the team’s number four starter.
Freeman wasn’t having any of that.
“We have four number one starters. That’s what we have,” he said. “I don’t think anybody is going to be one, two, three or four. They’re all ready to go, and whatever role they’re going to be deployed in the NLDS, we got four starters.”
“So I think our guys, we got four number ones. If you want to call him a number four, you can call him a number four, but they’re all number ones.”
It’s a sentiment that should resonate with Dodger fans after watching the recent performances of Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Tyler Glasnow. The starting rotation appears to be coming together at an ideal time, and Freeman clearly has confidence in the arms that will be taking the mound in October.
For now, Freeman’s priorities are straightforward: carry his recent improvements into the final weekend, get the rest he’s earned, and prepare for the NLDS.
And if a few more Dodgers can find their swings along the way, all the better.
More Dodgers Coverage:
Have you subscribed to the Bleed Los Podcast YouTube channel? Be sure to ring the notification bell to watch player interviews, participate in shows & promotions, and stay up to date on all Dodgers news and rumors!
A lifelong baseball fan, Webb has been going to Dodger games since he moved to Los Angeles in 1987. His favorite memory was attending the insane Game 3 of the World Series in 2025 and hugging random Dodgers fans after Freddie’s walkoff homer. He has been writing for Dodgersbeat since 2020.

item.content:encoded:
The AL and NL Wild Card Series presented by AbbVie begins Tuesday, Sept. 29 with many of MLB’s most popular players preparing to take center stage. Shohei Ohtani of the Los Angeles Dodgers, Aaron Judge of the New York Yankees and Pete Crow-Armstrong of the Chicago Cubs are leading the league in most popular player jerseys as their respective Clubs enter the final weekend of the regular season with Postseason berths secured.
Ohtani’s popularity reached new heights as he became the first player to finish four straight seasons with the most popular player jersey in the Majors since tracking began in 2010. Since 2023, fans have purchased Ohtani’s Nike jersey more than any other in the U.S., Japan and worldwide. With Dodgers teammate and reigning Willie Mays World Series Most Valuable Player Yoshinobu Yamamoto’s jersey ranking no. 9 and Chicago White Sox All-Star slugger Munetaka Murakami debuting on the list at no. 20, this is also the first season that three MLB Players from Japan have their jerseys in the top 20.
After becoming only the seventh player in MLB history and first Cubs player to hit at least 40 home runs and steal at least 40 bases in a single season, Crow-Armstrong’s jersey finished as the third most popular of the season – the highest ranking for a Cubs star since Javier Báez finished third in 2018.
This list, released jointly today by MLB and MLB Players, Inc. (MLBPI), accounts for sales of Nike jerseys from the Fanatics network of sites, including MLBShop.com, since Opening Day of the 2026 Championship Season.

item.title: [Dodgers Nation] Dodgers Fans Demand Josue De Paula Return After Slump
item.dc:creator: Nelson Espinal
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers fans have spoken, and they want rookie Josue De Paula back with the team to provide a spark. item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers fans have spoken, and they want rookie Josue De Paula back with the team to provide a spark.
Why the Dodgers Demoted De Paula
After 11 stellar games, in which De Paula looked amazing at the plate, the Dodgers demoted him on Wednesday, September 23rd, sending him back to the minors.
With Shohei Ohtani returning from the injured list, he would assume the designated hitter role from De Paula. Additionally, Dalton Rushing is returning to get some at-bats and make his case for a postseason roster spot.
De Paula was hitting .323/.500/.545 with a 1.081 OPS, making pitchers work and bringing a youthful edge to an older roster.
After his demotion, manager Dave Roberts and president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman both praised De Paula and made it clear he will be considered for a spot on the postseason roster.
Since he was demoted on Wednesday and players must wait 10 days to be promoted back to the major leagues, he would be in line to return in time for Game 1 of the NLDS.
While the decision-makers are giving Rushing a chance to make his case and weigh their options, Dodgers Nation has already decided.
Dodgers Fans Demand De Paula
Following his demotion, the Dodgers have scored just two runs over the last 18 innings, losing both games to the San Diego Padres.
In his last game on Tuesday, September 22nd, De Paula went 2-for-3 with a triple, a walk, and a stolen base.
With the two-game cold stretch since his absence, fans want him back in the mix.
“Hmm, maybe sending JDP down wasn’t the right move after all,” a fan said after the Dodgers lost on Thursday.
“Miss you JDP,” another commented.
“Damn JDP and will smith really carry that much weight huh,” a third added.
“Josue was only gonna get better BRING HIM BACK,” a fourth wrote.
As for the postseason, fans don’t even think it’s a question of whether De Paula should be on the team.
“Dude was on fire!! And confident!! Don’t understand at all!! And he was starting and succeeding,” a fan said.
“JDP needs to be there. He proved it!!” another chimed in.
“Cmon guys, we all know JDP will make that playoff roster, if he doesn’t I’m going to the front office myself,” a third fan said.
Safe to say, the outrage if De Paula is not on the postseason roster will be palpable.

item.title: [FanSided] Why MLB fans should root for Roki Sasaki in the playoffs, not revel in Dodgers downfall
item.dc:creator: Jake Elman
item.description: Crossing the Pacific Ocean and signing with the Los Angeles Dodgers meant cultural and personal transitions for prized Japanese import Roki Sasaki. item.content:encoded:
Crossing the Pacific Ocean and signing with the Los Angeles Dodgers meant cultural and personal transitions for prized Japanese import Roki Sasaki.
But when Sasaki officially met the U.S. media in early 2025, he made it clear he and his newest fanbase had two things in common: baseball and grief.
Sasaki returned from the injured list this week just as a March 2025 story by the Dodgers’ official website resurfaced on social media. At the time, California was still recovering from the January 2025 wildfires that ravaged the Los Angeles area, an unfortunately familiar sight for their newest pitcher.
Nearly 15 years earlier, Sasaki lost his father, grandparents, and his family’s home in the March 2011 tsunami. He turned to baseball as an escape, just as so many others affected by tragedy often do.
"Los Angeles is facing challenging and difficult times right now,” Sasaki said in January 2025, “and as a member of the Dodgers, starting today, I am dedicated to give my best and strive forward together with the people of the city."
Baseball fans can support Roki Sasaki without rooting for the Los Angeles Dodgers
This might sound contradictory, but hear us out.
We just saw Mets fans overwhelmingly cheer for Pete Alonso, even after he smashed a game-tying home run. Citi Field cared far more about Alonso the player than it did the Orioles as a team. Had the Orioles somehow snuck into the postseason, we imagine there’d be plenty of Mets fans with even the slightest rooting interest.
The same principle — or, at least, an extremely similar one — easily applies to Sasaki. Forget the fact he signed with the reigning World Series champions and played a pivotal role during last year’s title run. He’s still a human being with emotions who went through a horrifically traumatic experience; nearly 20,000 people are believed to have died in the Great East Japan Earthquake, and over 2,550 people remained missing as of 2021.
And above all else, Sasaki hasn’t done anything wrong beyond struggling to hit the strike zone. But compare that to some of the other notable names we’ll see this postseason. San Diego’s Fernando Tatis Jr. and Ramón Laureano each served PED-related suspensions. Boston’s Jarren Duran has feuded with fans and media in a way Red Sox Nation eventually stopped defending.
We’ve long been critical of both Sasaki and how the Dodgers have refused to make him a full-time reliever. Dave Roberts confirmed earlier this week the 24-year-old will pitch out of the bullpen during the postseason, just as he did last October, and the first impressions were positive; Sasaki threw a scoreless inning and didn’t allow a walk against the Padres on Tuesday night.
We wouldn’t blame you for hoping the Dodgers lose in the NLDS. They’re a superteam seeking their third consecutive championship and fourth in six years. At least three players on the active roster — Shohei Ohtani, Freddie Freeman, and Mookie Betts — are widely considered locks for the Hall of Fame, and Tarik Skubal is well on his way.
But when Sasaki comes in from the bullpen, try not to be overly hard on him. Save your vitriol for the umpires and broadcasters.

item.content:encoded:
Mookie Betts batted second against the San Diego Padres on Thursday. The Los Angeles Dodgers returned Shohei Ohtani to his usual leadoff spot.
He played behind Betts on Wednesday at No. 2.
But the change didn’t see success. San Diego beat the Dodgers 4-2 on Thursday night. The win clinched the Padres’ franchise-record third consecutive postseason berth, their fifth in seven seasons.
The Dodgers also secured a bye into the Division Series, avoiding the wild-card round.
Los Angeles now turns to the San Francisco Giants to close the regular season. The three-game series opens Friday at Oracle Park and runs through Sunday. The Dodgers open the postseason on Oct. 3.
Betts went 3-for-4 with a double in Thursday’s loss. He scored a run and drew a walk. He is heating up at the perfect time. In September, his average improved to .367 from .257, with an OPS of 1.177.
Keeping up with the success on the field, Betts also announced major news off the field.
Mookie Betts Announces Major Career News
Betts signed with 3 Arts Sports and Sanders Sports & Entertainment for personal representation.
“We’re excited to announce that 3 Arts Sports and Sanders Sports & Entertainment are joining forces to represent Los Angeles Dodgers star Mookie Betts across brand partnerships, business opportunities and off-field ventures,” the two firms wrote. “Proud to be on Mookie’s team and excited for what’s ahead.”
Betts reshared the post on his own Instagram account.
The two firms will co-manage his personal endorsements, brand partnerships and business development.
3 Arts Sports also represents Travis Kelce, WNBA star Sophie Cunningham and NFL stars Jayden Daniels and Myles Garrett.
Kelce recently signed on as Tommy Hilfiger’s global brand ambassador, a multi-season deal that includes a co-designed menswear collection as a partner of 3 Arts Sports.
Betts face value sits alongside the biggest in the industry.
Shohei Ohtani is Looking Great Ahead of Postseason
Manager Dave Roberts assessed Ohtani after Wednesday’s return. He called Ohtani considerably better than before the injured list stint, roughly an 8 or 9 out of 10 compared with a 5 beforehand.
“The last 2 nights, he’s looked great,” Roberts said. “Really exciting, just missed a homer.”
Ohtani will not pitch in the postseason. The Dodgers shut him down from pitching for the rest of 2026 earlier this month. Roberts said the move lets Ohtani focus fully on hitting.

item.title: [Beehiiv] The Josue De Paula Predicament
item.dc:creator: Mark Chiarelli
item.description: The Josue De Paula Predicament Plus: Astros rookie homers three times amid pursuit for AL West crown Josue De Paula, OF, Dodgers: De Paula already has a major league hit, but in a weird quirk, he hadn’t recorded one in Triple-A entering Thursday’s deciding game of the Pacific Coast League Championship Series. De Paula checked that off early, lining a single to right field in the third inning. He followed with an RBI double later in the game to extend Oklahoma City’s lead to 5-0. Overall, he fini
item.content:encoded:
The Josue De Paula Predicament
Plus: Astros rookie homers three times amid pursuit for AL West crown
Josue De Paula, OF, Dodgers: De Paula already has a major league hit, but in a weird quirk, he hadn’t recorded one in Triple-A entering Thursday’s deciding game of the Pacific Coast League Championship Series. De Paula checked that off early, lining a single to right field in the third inning. He followed with an RBI double later in the game to extend Oklahoma City’s lead to 5-0. Overall, he finished 2-for-5 with a run and an RBI as Oklahoma City won the Pacific Coast League championship.
De Paula started the season in Double-A, hitting .303/.401/.547 with 27 home runs in 124 games. He jumped straight to the majors after Shohei Ohtani got hurt and hit .323/.500/.581 with five extra-base hits, 11 walks and only five strikeouts in 42 plate appearances. Even after that dominant start, De Paula was optioned to Triple-A when Ohtani returned.
In 11 major league games, De Paula played only six innings in the field, spending most of his time at designated hitter. His defense is a major question mark right now, to the extent that the Dodgers don’t seem to trust him in the field. He still could make the Dodgers’ playoff roster because of his upside at the plate in a pinch-hitting role, but it will be difficult for him to carve out a major role this season as long as Ohtani is healthy.
Lucas Spence, OF, Astros: One of the heroes of the Astros’ victory on Thursday that kept them deadlocked with the Rangers atop the American League West was their 23-year-old outfielder. Spence, the No. 9 prospect in the Astros’ system, hit his first three career home runs, powering the Astros to a 7-5 victory.
Spence gave the Astros their first lead with a three-run home run in the second. He then hit the go-ahead home run in the seventh before homering again in the ninth to extend the Astros’ lead to two, which proved to be the final margin.
Spence is now hitting .205/.286/.432 in his first 16 major league games. He was identified as a potential breakout player in the preseason and has seen his stock rise slightly in the Astros’ system after hitting .238/.348/.426 with 13 home runs in 99 games across three levels.
Mike Sirota, OF, Dodgers: Sirota continued his impressive season, reaching base four times in Oklahoma City’s victory to clinch the Pacific Coast League championship. Sirota finished 1-for-2 with three walks, an RBI and a stolen base. He grounded out in the second inning before driving in a run with a single to left in the third to extend Oklahoma City’s lead to 2-0. He then walked in the fifth, seventh and ninth innings.
Sirota finished the series 3-for-11 with three singles and four walks. He hit .307/.461/.526 in 108 games during the regular season and established himself as one of the top outfield prospects in the Dodgers’ system and all of minor league baseball.
Luis Peña, SS, Brewers: Peña, the No. 21 prospect in baseball, underwent surgery on Thursday to repair a fractured left fibula, according to MLB.com's Adam McCalvy. Peña injured his ankle while stealing a base in a game on Sept. 5 and was carted off the field. The 19-year-old was limited to just 70 games in 2026 and spent the bulk of the year with High-A Wisconsin. He hit .296/.380/.415 with 35 stolen bases across three stops.
Peña also missed nearly a month early in the season after passing out in the dugout during a game against Fort Wayne on April 22. He was hospitalized and underwent a slew of medical tests before returning to the field. McCalvy noted that Peña's recovery timeline from ankle surgery remains unclear, though it is typically six to nine months.

item.title: [True Blue LA] Dodgers notes: Shohei Ohtani, Tyler Glasnow, first-round bye
item.dc:creator: Jacob Macofsky

So far, the team has gone 2-18 with runners in scoring position while scoring just three runs over their two consecutive losses to the San Diego Padres. item.content:encoded:
Shohei Ohtani is back in the lineup and the Dodgers saved their best starting lineup for the final five games of the regular season. So far, the team has gone 2-18 with runners in scoring position while scoring just three runs over their two consecutive losses to the San Diego Padres.
Ohtani was one of three Dodgers with an extra-base hit over their last two games, as the two-way superstar is 3-9 with a double, an RBI and a walk since returning. Thursday’s game in particular saw connect for two hits while smacking two deep fly balls that died on the center field warning track in their 4-2 loss, and the three weeks off have evidently helped him mitigate the unease he felt at the plate at the start of the month.
Andrew Friedman admitted the obvious, that the injuries to both his biceps and knee hampered his production at the plate, reports Jack Harris of the California Post, and he noted that he isn’t the most transparent when it comes to his physical health.
“There’s no question [the injuries] affected him,” Friedman said. “I think the fact that he feels as good as he does right now is certainly encouraging. Now it’s about making sure that holds.”
“He’s not always the best reporter of how he feels,” Friedman said. “Freddie [Freeman is] the same way. Clayton Kershaw. I’ve been around a lot of these guys that feel like their job is to be out there to help the team however they can, and sometimes will downplay some things that are bothering them.”
Despite Tyler Glasnow being dealt the loss in his final tune-up on Thursday, he impressed early on by flirting with a no-hitter through his first five innings while also racking up a season-high 11 strikeouts over 6 1/3 innings.
As the Dodgers begin to construct their ideal postseason pitching staff, Glasnow’s name is all but certain to be fixed into the rotation, and the right-hander stated that he’s in a good rhythm entering October while speaking to with the media postgame.
Last postseason, the Dodgers weren’t as fortunate to obtain a first-round bye, having to embark on a four-series gauntlet in their eventual success of becoming baseball’s first repeat champions in a quarter century.
With a much stronger regular season this time around, the Dodgers for the first time since 2024 will have that extra period of rest to prepare for their quest for a three-peat. The most significant factor for their first-round bye will be allowing players dealing with nagging issues to become as healthy as can be come October 3, per Sonja Chen of MLB.com.
“I think we all know why it’s important,” Freeman said earlier this week. “There’s a lot of us kind of limping toward the end here, a lot of aches and pains this year. It’s good to get those guys back on the field, get some ABs in them and then rest up and get some more ABs during the lives and whatever we do here in that week to get us ready for [NLDS Game 1].”

item.title: [sanantoniopost.com] MLB roundup: White Sox, Guardians, Cubs, Padres wrap up playoff berths

Chicago is back in the postseason for the first time since 2021 after enduring three straight 100-loss seasons. Fueled by an early barrage against Royals right-hand
item.content:encoded:
Field Level Media

25 Sep 2026, 12:10 GMT+10

(Photo credit: William Purnell)
Miguel Vargas had two hits and two RBIs, Kyle Teel homered and David Sandlin delivered six strong innings as the visiting Chicago White Sox routed the Kansas City Royals 9-1 on Thursday to clinch an American League playoff berth.
Chicago is back in the postseason for the first time since 2021 after enduring three straight 100-loss seasons.
Fueled by an early barrage against Royals right-hander Randy Dobnak, the White Sox remained a game behind the AL Central-leading Cleveland Guardians. Chicago holds the head-to-head tiebreaker over Cleveland. Whichever one of those two teams fails to win the division will wind up as the third AL wild-card team.
Sandlin (3-2) yielded one run and five hits. Dobnak (3-5) allowed six runs (four earned) and six hits in 1 1/3 innings.
Guardians 1, Red Sox 0
Angel Martinez's second-inning home run was all visiting Cleveland needed for a win over Boston to clinch its third consecutive playoff berth.
Joey Cantillo (11-9) dominated for five shutout innings as the Guardians' bulk reliever, yielding one hit. Hunter Gaddis, Erik Sabrowski and Cade Smith allowed a combined one hit over the final three innings to help Cleveland win its seventh game in the last eight.
The playoff-bound Red Sox fell for the fourth time in five games despite getting five innings of one-run ball from Ranger Suarez (8-5).
Cubs 2, Marlins 1
Nico Hoerner ripped a go-ahead RBI single in the sixth and Matthew Boyd tossed seven strong innings, helping host Chicago clinch a playoff berth with a victory over Miami.
Chicago's Pete Crow-Armstrong walked to lead off the first inning and promptly stole second base to become the seventh player in major league history to record at least 40 homers and 40 stolen bases in a single season.
Seiya Suzuki belted a solo homer in the fifth inning to highlight his two-hit performance for the Cubs, who salvaged the finale of their three-game series with Miami. Chicago sits in the second NL wild-card spot, one game behind San Diego.
Padres 4, Dodgers 2
Dustin Harris drove in the go-ahead run in the sixth inning as visiting San Diego beat Los Angeles to clinch a playoff spot for a franchise-record third consecutive season.
Yuki Matsui (4-1) earned the win with a scoreless inning, and Mason Miller gave up a run with two outs in the ninth before securing his 38th save. Ethan Salas and Fernando Tatis Jr. each had two hits and an RBI for the Padres.
Tyler Glasnow (5-2) fanned a season-high 11 but allowed three runs in 6 1/3 innings for the Dodgers, who secured a first-round playoff bye thanks to the Atlanta Braves' loss on Thursday. Shohei Ohtani went 2-for-5 with an RBI double.
Brewers 5, Phillies 1
Jake Bauers' RBI single in the eighth inning plated the go-ahead run for Milwaukee, which reached the 100-win mark for the first time in franchise history with a win at Philadelphia. When the Dodgers fell to the Padres later, the Brewers clinched the top record in the major leagues.
Bauers, who went 2-for-5, singled up the middle, allowing Jackson Chourio to score from second, giving the Brewers (100-59) a 2-1 lead and starting a three-run frame.
Philadelphia remains in an NL wild-card spot, but the Phillies could not drop their magic number to clinch from two. Phillies starter Andrew Painter threw six innings of one-run ball, fanning eight. Bryce Harper went 2-for-4 with an RBI.
Diamondbacks 12, Rockies 8
Gabriel Moreno and Nolan Arenado homered in a six-run first inning and surging Arizona beat Colorado in Denver to continue its drive for a wild-card berth.
James McCann also went deep for Arizona, which moved within two games of Philadelphia for the third and final NL playoff berth. Arizona finishes the regular season in San Diego while the Phillies host Tampa Bay this weekend.
Cole Carrigg homered among his four hits, Kyle Karros and Zac Veen also went deep and had two hits for Colorado, which finished with 17 hits.
Rangers 3, Mets 1
Kumar Rocker pitched five solid innings for Texas, which salvaged the finale of a three-game series against New York in Arlington, Texas.
Josh Jung (3-for-3) hit a two-run homer in the first and Corey Seager went deep in the sixth for the Rangers, who remain tied with Houston for first place in the American League West. Rocker (6-11) allowed one run on three hits. Jordan Montgomery recorded his first save of the season.
Mets starter Zac Thornton (5-6) yielded two runs on four hits over five innings. Brett Baty extended his on-base streak to 17 games.
Astros 7, Athletics 5
Rookie Lucas Spence hit his first three career homers and drove in five runs as Houston smacked five homers while defeating the Athletics in West Sacramento, Calif.
Isaac Paredes and Christian Walker added solo blasts for the Astros who remained tied for first in the AL West with the Rangers. Houston holds the tiebreaker, having gone 9-4 vs. Texas this year.
Houston reliever Miguel Ullola (2-0) fired three scoreless innings and Brayan Abreu worked 1 1/3 shutout innings for his ninth save. Zack Gelof hit two homers and Jeff McNeil drilled a three-run shot for the Athletics, who lost for the seventh time in nine games.
Yankees 6, Rays 4
Rookie George Lombard Jr. hit a tiebreaking two-run homer with two outs in the eighth inning as New York overcame a four-run deficit and earned a victory over visiting Tampa Bay.
New York ace Cam Schlittler allowed two runs (one earned) in three innings in a playoff tuneup, ending the season with a 1.95 ERA. Bradley Hanner (1-0) threw two scoreless innings for his first career victory.
Junior Caminero had a pair of RBI singles for the Rays. Ian Seymour allowed one hit in five scoreless innings. Steven Matz (5-6) served up Lombard's decisive homer.
Pirates 2, Cardinals 1
Spencer Horwitz's sacrifice fly in the eighth drove in the go-ahead run, and Paul Skenes concluded his season with a quality start as Pittsburgh wrapped up its home schedule with a victory over St. Louis.
Skenes tossed 6 1/3 innings, struck out eight, walked two and allowed one run on three hits. His final pitch completed a strikeout of Leo Bernal, giving him 200-plus for the second straight season. Luke Weaver (4-1) escaped an inherited eighth-inning jam before Mason Montgomery recorded his 17th save.
Alec Burleson homered for the Cardinals. St. Louis (77-82) is guaranteed to finish with back-to-back losing seasons for the first time since 1994-95.
Reds 7, Braves 6
A two-run homer by Hector Rodriguez, one of three long balls by Cincinnati, helped the visiting Reds beat Atlanta in the rubber game of a three-game series.
Rodriguez clubbed a 423-foot homer to right field against AJ Smith-Shawver (0-3) in the sixth inning to give the Reds the lead for good. Elly De La Cruz added his 30th homer and Carlos Jorge hit his first career homer. Cincinnati reliever Connor Phillips (2-0) pitched 1 1/3 scoreless innings.
Atlanta right-hander Tyler Mahle threw five innings and gave up five runs on six hits in his worst outing since being acquired from San Francisco at the trade deadline.
Angels 6, Mariners 4
Christian Moore doubled, singled and drove in three runs as Los Angeles won at Seattle.
Josh Lowe also had a single and a double and scored three times for the Angels. Los Angeles starter Grayson Rodriguez (5-8) gave up four runs on five hits over five innings. Ryan Watson pitched the ninth for his fourth save.
Julio Rodriguez homered for the Mariners, whose postseason hopes were dashed when the Rangers defeated the Mets earlier in the day. Bryan Woo (12-10) allowed five runs, four earned, on seven hits in 5 1/3 innings.
