item.title: [Yahoo] Shohei Ohtani tiene previsto regresar el miércoles, pero los Dodgers aún tienen dudas por resolver
item.dc:creator: Maddie Lee
item.description: A los Dodgers les queda menos de una semana de la temporada regular para ponerse en forma para los playoffs. Y los movimientos en su plantilla para esta serie reflejan esa prisa por el tiempo. El mánager Dave Roberts confirmó el martes que Shohei Ohtani (bíceps derecho, rodilla izquierda) iba a ser reincorporado el miércoles tras su estancia de 15 días en la lista de lesionados. Según Roberts, Ohtani se siente "considerablemente" mejor que antes de estar en la lista de lesionados. "Diría que si
item.content:encoded:
A los Dodgers les queda menos de una semana de la temporada regular para ponerse en forma para los playoffs. Y los movimientos en su plantilla para esta serie reflejan esa prisa por el tiempo.
El mánager Dave Roberts confirmó el martes que Shohei Ohtani (bíceps derecho, rodilla izquierda) iba a ser reincorporado el miércoles tras su estancia de 15 días en la lista de lesionados. Según Roberts, Ohtani se siente "considerablemente" mejor que antes de estar en la lista de lesionados.
"Diría que si antes estaba en un nivel de cinco, ahora probablemente esté en un ocho o un nueve", dijo Roberts antes de que ocho lanzadores lideraran la victoria de los Dodgers por 7-0 contra los Padres de San Diego en el primer partido de la serie.
El martes, los Dodgers redujeron a uno su número mágico para asegurar una exención en la primera ronda. Y antes del partido, recuperaron a otros dos jugadores importantes para la postemporada, al reincorporar del lista de lesionados al jardinero central Andy Pages (fractura en la mano izquierda) y al lanzador derecho Roki Sasaki (ampolla en el dedo medio derecho).
En movimientos correspondientes, los Dodgers enviaron al equipo de Triple A de Oklahoma City al lanzador derecho Emmet Sheehan y al receptor Eliézer Alfonzo.
Sasaki se hizo cargo de la cuarta entrada del partido con relevos y lanzó sin permitir carreras. Permitió un par de sencillos, pero su bola rápida tuvo un poco más de vida en esa breve participación, con un promedio de 98.7 mph y una velocidad máxima de 101.7.
"Pude adaptarme porque ya tenía la experiencia [desde el bullpen] del año pasado", dijo Sasaki a través del intérprete Kensuke Okubo. "Probablemente voy a lanzar en un par de partidos más, así que solo voy a hacer ajustes y seguir avanzando".
Pages se fue de 0 de 2, pero llegó a base dos veces, gracias a un golpeado por lanzamiento y una base por bolas.
"Obviamente, al haber estado fuera un mes, no me siento del todo bien ni tan cómodo al bate", dijo Pages a través del intérprete del equipo, Juan Dorado. "Pero hay cosas [de batear con la máquina Trajekt] que me ayudaron a poder regresar".
Sin embargo, incluso con el regreso de los jugadores, aún hay preguntas que los Dodgers deben responder en la última semana de la temporada:
¿En qué posición bateará Ohtani?
Al menos al principio, Roberts planea colocar a Ohtani al inicio del orden de bateo, como de costumbre. Pero el campocorto Mookie Betts ha entrado en la discusión.
"Sin duda, contra lanzadores diestros [Ohtani] estará ahí", dijo Roberts. "Creo que debería analizar la situación de Mookie contra lanzadores zurdos, pero tengo que pensar en la estructura completa de la alineación".
Ohtani ha sido el primer bateador en todos los partidos que ha sido titular este año. Pero bateó en el segundo lugar en 79 partidos entre las dos temporadas anteriores combinadas.
Incluso sin Ohtani, la alineación de los Dodgers ha estado funcionando bien. El martes, Tommy Edman conectó su segundo jonrón en otros tantos partidos, y Will Smith conectó un jonrón por tercera vez en cuatro días.
¿Está sana la rotación?
El lanzador zurdo de los Dodgers, Blake Snell, quien salió de su apertura la semana pasada por una contractura en la ingle izquierda, realizó una sesión de bullpen el martes. Está programado para una última apertura en la temporada regular el sábado, dijo Roberts.
Eso significa que los cuatro abridores proyectados de los Dodgers para los playoffs están programados para lanzar de este miércoles a sábado, con Yoshinobu Yamamoto y Tyler Glasnow en el montículo para los dos últimos partidos contra los Padres, y Tarik Skubal y Snell en los dos primeros partidos en San Francisco.
¿Quién es el cerrador?
En resumen, podría cambiar de un día para otro.
"En un mundo perfecto —aunque todos sabemos que el mundo no es perfecto—, me encantaría tener [un cerrador fijo]", dijo Roberts. "Creo que si surge la oportunidad, por ejemplo, de que Tanner [Scott] lance una entrada decisiva en la séptima u octava entrada, es difícil dejar pasar esa oportunidad si él es la mejor opción en ese momento. Porque simplemente no sabes cómo se desarrollará la novena entrada.
"Esas son cosas con las que hay que lidiar, y siempre es bueno que la gente las discuta. En este momento no veo a un cerrador que sea solo una persona".
Sasaki asumió ese papel el año pasado. No está claro exactamente cómo lo utilizará Roberts esta vez, pero Roberts dijo que podría ser una opción, dependiendo de cómo lance al regresar de la lista de lesionados.
"El año pasado fue una de esas situaciones de necesidad, dada nuestra situación en cuanto al rendimiento, la salud y la plantilla", dijo Roberts. "Desempeñó ese papel de manera admirable".
El martes, fue uno de los ocho lanzadores de los Dodgers que, en conjunto, lograron una blanqueada en un día de bullpen.
"Hemos tenido mucho talento a lo largo de los años", dijo Roberts. "Pero al sentarnos aquí hoy, al final de la temporada, el bullpen está en la mejor forma en la que ha estado. Eso podría cambiar en un día, en un partido, como todos sabemos. Pero en este momento, me siento muy bien con todos los que están ahí afuera".
El lanzador derecho Edwin Díaz, quien perdió el puesto de cerrador debido a una combinación de lesiones y bajo rendimiento, está en camino de volver a ser considerado para la novena entrada. El martes, retiró a los primeros bateadores de la alineación en orden para una quinta entrada limpia, lo que marcó su tercera salida consecutiva sin permitir carreras desde que regresó de la lista de lesionados.
"Si eres uno de los 12 o 13 lanzadores en una posible lista para la postemporada, estás en la lista de los que gozan de confianza", dijo Roberts. "Y él se ha colocado justo en medio de esa conversación. Y considerando todo lo que ha tenido que pasar este año para enderezar el rumbo, es un gran mérito para él".
¿Quién se queda con el último lugar en la banca?
La contienda por ser el bateador zurdo de la banca en la postemporada se ha reducido al novato Josué De Paula y al receptor lesionado Dalton Rushing (distensión en el flexor derecho). Pero con Rushing aún en la lista de lesionados, De Paula parece tener ventaja.
No le des demasiada importancia al movimiento correspondiente de los Dodgers con respecto a Ohtani el miércoles. Si envían a De Paula a las ligas menores a 10 días del primer partido de la Serie Divisional de la Liga Nacional, aún puede ser incluido en la plantilla.
Los Dodgers tendrán que hacer otro movimiento en la plantilla más adelante en la semana, cuando planean activar a Rushing. Si envían a un jugador a las ligas menores para hacerle espacio a Rushing, ese jugador solo sería elegible para el inicio de la Serie Divisional de la Liga Nacional como transacción correspondiente a un movimiento a la lista de lesionados.

item.content:encoded:
La recta final de la Temporada 2026 está al rojo vivo en las Grandes Ligas de Béisbol (MLB) y este miércoles 26 de septiembre los Dodgers se enfrentan a los Padres en el Dodger Stadium, desafío que representa el regreso de Shohei Ohtani a la alineación de los campeones defensores. Aquí te decimos dónde ver el juego de hoy EN VIVO.
Dave Roberts y los Dodgers viven una jornada especial ya que, finalmente, podrían asegurar ser uno de los dos mejores campeones divisionales en la Liga Nacional y evitar jugar la Serie de Comodines; todo esto ante unos Padres que, pese a una buena racha, necesitan ganar urgentemente para no rezagarse en la carrera por los puestos de playoffs.
¿Cómo llegan al juego Dodgers y Padres HOY?
Los Angeles Dodgers están teniendo un gran cierre de temporada llegando a esta jornada con 5 juegos ganados en fila, el más reciente blanqueando a los Padres por 7-0 durante un juego de bullpen. El de hoy representa un día especial para los Dodgers por el regreso de Shohei Ohtani de la lista de lesionados; el manager aseguró que está “significativamente mejor” tras presentar molestias en la rodilla izquierda y el bíceps derecho.
A shutdown performance from the 'pen. ???? pic.twitter.com/JPJbMfqkWO
— Los Angeles Dodgers (@Dodgers) September 23, 2026
Los San Diego Padres tuvieron que guardar la champaña ya que, al sufrir su segunda derrota en los últimos 15 juegos, se les negó su clasificación oficial a los playoffs, boleto que buscarán reclamar esta noche. Para ello, necesitan ganar esta noche ante los Dodgers y que los Diamondbacks caigan ante los Rockies.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Impact of Shohei Ohtani's Return on Dodgers, Playoff Picture
item.dc:creator: Curt Bishop; Unknown
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers are still battling it out with the Milwaukee Brewers for the top seed in the National League. item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are still battling it out with the Milwaukee Brewers for the top seed in the National League. Likely, whichever team captures the top seed will also have home-field advantage throughout the World Series.
Los Angeles is just one game behind Milwaukee for the top spot with five games left on the schedule. Though not surprising given the depth of their roster, the Dodgers have still been able to do this with Shohei Ohtani on the shelf with a knee injury. However, the two-way star is likely to return from the injured list on Wednesday, which should impact the Dodgers and the playoff race.
How Ohtani's return impacts Dodgers, playoff race
With the Dodgers just one game back of the Brewers for the top seed, this could give them a major advantage. Now, they have the best player in all of Major League Baseball healthy again, and with an upcoming weekend series with the 65-93 San Francisco Giants, they could have the advantage as they look to take the top seed.
Meanwhile, the Brewers, while facing a fellow non-contender in the St. Louis Cardinals, have the tougher scene facing up and coming pitchers Michael McGreevy and Quinn Mathews. Both the Brewers and Dodgers have already punched their tickets to the postseason, but if these two teams meet again in the NLCS, the Dodgers will almost certainly have the advantage with Ohtani back in action.
That gives their lineup a completely different look, and though Ohtani is likely done pitching for the year, the Dodgers lineup looks much better with him in it. As long as he can stay healthy in the playoffs, the Dodgers should be in good shape as they look to secure a three-peat.
Ohtani has been out a while too, so he should be quite well rested as he returns to action. The Dodgers are still a solid team without him, but they may now have the advantage as far as gaining the top seed in the playoffs, and this only further cements them as the favorite to win a World Series title
The two-way superstar is hitting .277/.380/.522 with 30 home runs, 80 RBI, a 6.5 WAR and a .902 OPS. Despite the injuries, he still has put together a solid season, and though he may not win the MVP this year, he still is among the most impactful players in the sport, and the Dodgers should have a big advantage with him healthy again.
Curt Bishop is a freelance sports writer who graduated from Maryville University of St. Louis with a Bachelor of Arts degree in the field of Communication and currently writes as a contributor for various platforms covering Major League Baseball. Curt’s work includes covering trade and free agency predictions, as well as rumors and news. item.content:encoded:
La superestrella japonesa se espera que regrese este miércoles a la alineación de Los Ángeles después de permanecer en la lista de lesionados desde el 9 de septiembre por una inflamación en el bíceps derecho y dolor persistente en la rodilla izquierda.
El manager Dave Roberts aseguró que Ohtani se siente considerablemente mejor, justo cuando los Dodgers se preparan para enfrentar nuevamente a los Padres de San Diego.
Los Dodgers ya aseguraron su 13er título del Oeste de la Liga Nacional en 14 años, y ahora Ohtani tendrá cinco juegos restantes para recuperar ritmo y tomar turnos al bate antes de la postemporada.
Todo apunta a que retomará su lugar como primer bate, especialmente ante lanzadores derechos, aunque Roberts todavía analiza la estructura de la alineación y el papel de Mookie Betts, quien ha tenido un gran rendimiento durante septiembre

item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers' leadoff spot could be a toss-up between Mookie Betts and Shohei Ohtani come postseason. item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers' leadoff spot could be a toss-up between Mookie Betts and Shohei Ohtani come postseason. While Ohtani has done an exceptional job at the top for most of the season, his latest injury concerns and a drop in performance lately have made an MLB analyst wonder if the Dodgers should consider giving the job to Betts in October.
Betts is having a great month in September, batting .373/.468/.746 with six home runs, and posting a 1.215 OPS, 227 wRC+, and 1.6 fWAR. Betts' stellar hitting and previous success at the leadoff spot have former MLB player Xavier Scruggs convinced the Dodgers need to make the move and take the pressure off Ohtani.
"It takes pressure off Ohtani, putting him in the two-spot," Scruggs said of Betts. "And I think it's a real decision for Dave Roberts because, look, before Ohtani went on the IL, and it's almost like you don't know exactly what to expect once he comes back. So maybe that's a situation where, since his numbers have dropped, we ease it on him."
Ohtani's numbers were really off in the last 13 games before he hit the injured list. The Dodgers star batted just .122/.295/.184 with just one extra-base hit and struck out 21 times.
The contrast in performance could give Dodgers manager Dave Roberts a small headache before finalizing his postseason lineup.
When Can Dodgers Expect Shohei Ohtani to Return?
Shohei Ohtani will return to the Dodgers lineup on Wednesday against the San Diego Padres. Manager Dave Roberts confirmed he is ready to be reinstated from the 15-day injured list.
Ohtani will return as designated hitter, as he has already been shut down as a pitcher for the remainder of the season. The Dodgers superstar was suffering from right biceps inflammation and lingering left knee soreness, prompting his move to the injured list.
Ohtani is expected to resume hitting at the top of the lineup, though there are discussions about whether he could play behind Mookie Betts against left-handed pitching.
"That's probably the way it's going to fall out, but I haven't totally decided yet," Roberts said. "I have to think about the entire lineup structure."
The Dodgers have already clinched the NL West title and are strongly putting their foot forward to complete a World Series three-peat. Ohtani's return just before the postseason is to ensure the Japanese star gets some game time and finds his form at the plate.

item.title: [newsonjapan.com] Asian Games Day 5 Brings Swimming Gold and Gymnastics Drama
item.description: NAGOYA - Japan's Asian Games campaign produced another day of records and medals on September 23, with Shoon Mitsunaga setting a national record to win the men's 100-meter butterfly, both Japanese gymnastics teams taking silver behind China, and Toshikazu Yamanishi adding to the host nation's athletics medal haul. item.content:encoded:
NAGOYA - Japan's Asian Games campaign produced another day of records and medals on September 23, with Shoon Mitsunaga setting a national record to win the men's 100-meter butterfly, both Japanese gymnastics teams taking silver behind China, and Toshikazu Yamanishi adding to the host nation's athletics medal haul.
Away from the Games, the professional baseball pennant races entered their final stages, with Hanshin fighting to retain its Central League lead and SoftBank approaching the Pacific League championship.
The fifth day of the Asian Games brought a particularly intense contest between Japan and China, whose athletes met in swimming, gymnastics and athletics. China's 13-year-old swimming sensation Yu Zidi completed a remarkable hat trick of individual gold medals, while its men's and women's gymnastics teams narrowly defeated Japan in front of home spectators.
Japan's September 23 sporting program extended well beyond the principal medal events, with competition across rowing, fencing, table tennis, shooting, cycling, combat sports and a wide range of other disciplines. The Asian Games will continue through October 4, with athletics beginning its seven-day program in Nagoya.
Japan's swimming successes were led by 21-year-old Mitsunaga, who won the men's 100-meter butterfly at Tokyo Aquatics Centre in 50.56 seconds, lowering the Japanese record from 50.81. Defending champion Katsuo Matsumoto also reached the podium, taking bronze and giving Japan two medals in the event.
The result was particularly striking given Mitsunaga's performance in the morning heats, when he qualified seventh in 52.54 seconds. His improvement in the final brought Japan its second successive Asian Games gold in the event.
Japan added three silver medals and another bronze in the pool. Rio Shirai finished second in the women's 100-meter backstroke, while 35-year-old Satomi Suzuki collected silver in the women's 100-meter breaststroke in a Games-record time of 1:05.83. Komi Kato took bronze in the same event, and Japan's mixed 4x100-meter medley relay team finished second. Suzuki's result was her 11th career Asian Games medal.
China's Yu Zidi provided the day's other major swimming story. The 13-year-old won the women's 400-meter individual medley in 4:28.56, setting a Games record and completing three victories in three individual events after earlier winning the 200-meter butterfly and 200-meter individual medley.
China also won the men's 200-meter freestyle through Zhang Zhanshuo and the women's 100-meter backstroke through Peng Xuwei.
Japan's gymnastics teams experienced remarkably similar outcomes in their two team finals, finishing second to China in both competitions.
In the men's final, China scored 259.095 points, finishing just over one point ahead of the Japanese team. Zhang Boheng secured the title with a strong horizontal bar routine after Japan had entered the final rotation with a chance to overturn China's lead.
Olympic champion Shinnosuke Oka, competing with a back injury, fell during his horizontal bar routine and received 12.966. Teammate Daiki Hashimoto produced strong performances on pommel horse and vault, but China retained the Asian Games team title for a third consecutive edition.
Japan also took silver in the women's competition, scoring 165.362 points against China's 166.462. The Japanese team comprised Aiko Sugihara, Rina Kishi, Misa Nishiyama, Mana Okamura and Haruka Nakamura. It was Japan's ninth successive Asian Games medal in the women's team event.
The results followed Sugihara's individual all-around gold on September 22, the first by a Japanese woman at the Asian Games. The women's team will now turn its attention to the world championships in the Netherlands in October.
Soft tennis supplied two more gold medals for Japan. Toshiki Uematsu won the men's singles title, with fellow Japanese player Takuya Kurosaka taking silver, while Reina Tenma captured the women's singles championship.
Japan also secured medals across several less-publicized sports. Nanoka Kida took silver in the women's jianshu and qiangshu combined event in wushu. The equestrian eventing team earned silver, with Olympic veteran Yoshiaki Oiwa adding an individual bronze, while cyclist Yudai Todome finished third in the men's road race.
Athletics opened its program with the men's and women's half-marathon race walks. Japan's two-time world champion Toshikazu Yamanishi finished second in the men's competition behind China's Shi Shengji, who broke away after the 10-kilometer mark. China also won the women's race through Yang Liujing.
The athletics program, running through September 29 at Mizuho Park in Nagoya, will bring further Japanese contenders into action as track and field joins swimming, gymnastics and other established medal-producing sports.
Japan's team-sport campaigns also advanced significantly on September 23. The men's under-21 soccer team defeated Thailand 3-0 at Toyota Stadium to complete the group stage with three victories and no goals conceded. Yotaro Nakajima opened the scoring in the 31st minute before Keita Kosugi and Hisatsugu Ishii added two goals in quick succession early in the second half.
Japan had previously beaten Hong Kong 2-0 and Kyrgyzstan 7-0. The victory over Thailand secured first place in Group A and set up a September 26 quarterfinal against North Korea, which qualified from Group B after defeating Iran 4-1. Japan is seeking its first men's Asian Games soccer title since 2010.
The women's table tennis team also reached the final, defeating South Korea 3-0 in its semifinal at Sky Hall Toyota. Hina Hayata and Miwa Harimoto were among the players who helped Japan advance to a second consecutive Asian Games team final. Japan will face defending champion China on September 24, seeking its first women's team gold since the 1966 Bangkok Games.
Asian Games baseball produced another emphatic Japanese result as the corporate-league national team defeated the Philippines 7-0 at Toyohashi Municipal Stadium.
Japan scored twice in the second inning and three times in the third before adding another two runs in the sixth. Koya Yano and Masami Soeda each hit a two-run home run, while starting pitcher Kenta Nagano and reliever Kato combined to hold the Philippines to three hits. Japan completed its opening-round campaign unbeaten after earlier defeating China 11-3 and Palestine 15-0.
The three victories gave Japan first place in Group A and a place in the Super Round on September 25 and 26. The medal games are scheduled for September 27. Japan is attempting to win its first Asian Games baseball gold since 1994.
Japan's rowing team also reached an important milestone, with all 10 of its entered boats qualifying for their respective A finals despite heavy rain forcing changes to the competition schedule at the Nagaragawa International Regatta Course in Gifu Prefecture. The medal races are scheduled for September 24.
Outside the Asian Games, Hanshin strengthened its position at the top of the Central League with an 8-4 victory over Yakult at Jingu Stadium, extending its winning streak to four games.
Haruto Takahashi pitched six innings, allowing one run on five hits to record his league-leading 15th victory. Thirteen of those wins have come away from home, making him the first Hanshin pitcher to achieve that mark since Minoru Murayama in 1965.
The result was particularly important after the Tigers entered the day with a 1.5-game advantage over Yomiuri and a championship magic number of eight. The Giants remained in contention with a 2-1 victory over Hiroshima at Mazda Stadium.
SoftBank also moved closer to the Pacific League title, defeating Seibu 10-3 at Mizuho PayPay Dome in Fukuoka. The Hawks' latest victory came as Nippon-Ham lost 5-3 to Rakuten at Es Con Field Hokkaido. Orix defeated Lotte 1-0 at ZOZO Marine Stadium, with Ryoma Ikeda hitting his first career home run to provide the game's only run.
The day's other Central League result was a 4-3 victory for DeNA over Chunichi at Yokohama Stadium.
Soccer's domestic cup competition added another dimension to the day's schedule, with the Emperor's Cup continuing on September 23. All six J1 clubs facing J2 opposition advanced, including Kashima Antlers, for whom 18-year-old Minato Yoshida scored his first goal. Kashiwa Reysol also progressed with a victory over FC Imabari.
Grand sumo's September tournament reached its 11th day at Ryogoku Kokugikan, where yokozuna Onosato strengthened his position at the top of the championship race with a victory over sekiwake Fujinokawa. Onosato improved to 10 wins and one defeat, opening a two-victory advantage after all three wrestlers who had entered the day with two losses were beaten.
Ozeki Aonishiki defeated Takanosho to secure his eighth victory and a winning record. Sekiwake Atamifuji suffered his third defeat against ozeki Kirishima, while former ozeki Asanoyama improved to 8-3 with a victory over Kinbozan. With four days remaining, Onosato led a group of six wrestlers on three losses.
In Major League Baseball, attention surrounding Shohei Ohtani shifted toward his expected return to the Los Angeles Dodgers lineup after a spell on the injured list. Manager Dave Roberts confirmed on September 22 that Ohtani was scheduled to be reinstated on September 23 following treatment for knee and biceps problems. The Dodgers had already secured the National League West title and were preparing for the postseason.
Japan's September 23 sports program illustrated the breadth of the country's increasingly crowded autumn calendar, from national-record swimming performances and Asian Games medals to domestic baseball pennant races, international soccer, professional sumo and Japanese athletes competing overseas.
The next day of Asian Games competition will bring Japan's women's table tennis team into its final against China, rowing's medal races and the opening apparatus finals in artistic gymnastics, with further opportunities for the host nation to add to its medal total.

item.title: [mlb.com] The teams no one wants to play in October
item.dc:creator: Travis Sawchik
item.description: The best teams over 162 games and the clubs nobody wants to see in October are not necessarily the same. The regular season and the postseason reward different things. Over six months, baseball is a test of skill and depth. The weakest links eventually get exposed. A team can survive a thin rotation, a shaky middle-relief corps or a few light-hitting positions for a while – but it's much harder to hide those weaknesses over six months. October is different. The games are fewer, off-days greater.
item.content:encoded:
The best teams over 162 games and the clubs nobody wants to see in October are not necessarily the same.
The regular season and the postseason reward different things.
Over six months, baseball is a test of skill and depth. The weakest links eventually get exposed. A team can survive a thin rotation, a shaky middle-relief corps or a few light-hitting positions for a while – but it's much harder to hide those weaknesses over six months.
October is different.
The games are fewer, off-days greater. The urgency is heightened. Teams concentrate work among their best pitchers and lineups. Managers can shorten games with their best relievers. And one superstar hitter or ace can have an outsized influence on a short series.
Variance matters, too. A cleanup hitter can go 2-for-20 in April and the season keeps moving. Go 2-for-20 in October and the season might be over.
“Scary” is not necessarily the same as “best.” It is about concentration of talent, the ability to hide weaknesses, who is peaking at the right time, and the number of ways a team can make a short series tilt quickly.
I started with a simple framework: Which teams can shorten a series with two or three dominant starters? Which have a bullpen capable of essentially ending a game after five or six innings? Which lineups have enough power to avoid having to string together three or four hits against elite pitching? Which teams have deeper lineups to grind down opponents?
Who are the teams nobody wants to see in October?
The concentrated dynamo: the Dodgers
The Dodgers are the obvious answer.
Yes, they have some health question marks with Blake Snell and Shohei Ohtani. Yes, Edwin Díaz has not been the end-game piece they were hoping for in the bullpen. And, yes, their overall team slugging is down double-digit points from each of the last two years as well. But they are still a heavy World Series favorite no one wants to play.
A rotation led by Snell, Tarik Skubal, Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Tyler Glasnow is as good as it gets, and they are backed by a lineup that, while aging, still ranks as one of the best in the game. The market and models still believe they are the team to beat; FanGraphs gives them a 29.3% chance to win the title.
The team without a weakness: Brewers
While the Dodgers are the favorites, there's a case to be made that the Brewers are the scarier October opponent.
And after struggling out of the gate, Milwaukee is 82-44 since May 1 – five games better than the Rays, the next-ranking team. They've been above average in every month since April.
The terrifying thing about the Brewers is that there isn't an obvious way to attack them.
They have the most dominant pitcher in the game this year in Jacob Misiorowski, who unlike in his rookie year has shown no signs of slowing down. Misiorowski remains dominant in the second half with a 29% K-BB mark. His elevated velocity has held steady. And nearly as unhittable in the second half is Logan Henderson, who sports a 2.22 ERA, is holding opponents to a .171 average, and enjoys a 26.9 K-BB% mark since the All-Star break.
Getting the starter out doesn't make life easier either. The Brewers' reliever corps ranks fourth in ERA (3.41) and third in fWAR (6.6) out of all 30 teams.
Supporting those arms is an excellent defense.
And while the Brewers lack elite power, they string together quality at-bats with seven qualified Brewers hitters having an OPS+ of 100 or better, trailing only the Dodgers (eight) in the projected postseason field. The Phillies, by contrast, have two.
They are also trending the right way. The Brewers are 17-9 over the 30 days, tied for the second-best mark in baseball.
FanGraphs gives the Brewers the second-best title chances after the Dodgers (13.9%). They are a team built for the regular season and October.
OK, those are obvious contenders. What about other clubs?
The middling (potential) division winner: Guardians
The Guardians were one of the teams that actually won the Trade Deadline. Those added reinforcements, along with some positive regression from first-half slumpers like Steven Kwan, picked up a sluggish offense. They rank eighth in the Majors in runs since Aug. 1 (216 entering Tuesday).
A less obvious October advantage? Cleveland leads baseball in the percentage of plate appearances in which it enjoys the platoon advantage, at 77%, compared with a league average of 58.3%. In a five-game or seven-game series against a manager trying to optimize every matchup, that can become consequential.
And what really makes this team dangerous is the pitching staff.
The Guardians are one of three teams projected to be in the field that roster two pitchers that rank in the top 10 of fWAR in the second half of the season (the Dodgers are another, along with the Phillies).
Gavin Williams and Parker Messick have emerged as front-line starters this year. Tanner Bibee is a strong No. 3. While middle relief has hurt the club all season, being able to move a starter to the relief group should build a better bridge to closer Cade Smith.
Most teams that spend much of a season hovering around .500 don't have this kind of top-end pitching.
The Guardians are also hot, tied for the second-best record (17-9) in the Majors over the last month – tied with the Dodgers, Brewers, Braves and Padres – entering play Tuesday. Only the Rays (19-8) are better – but the Rays don't quite have the Guardians’ top-end starting pitching depth.
As the playoff picture stands entering Tuesday, the Guardians would face the winner of the White Sox (+42 run differential) or Rangers (-34 run differential) in the ALDS, with AL East clubs competing on the other side of the bracket. That's an extremely favorable path for a team with sneaky upside.
The unusual build: Cubs 
The Cubs are perhaps the strangest team on this list because their postseason case is built around the idea that an elite lineup and defense can overwhelm the quality and concentration of October pitching.
In the second half they've posted a 125 wRC+, 25% better than league average, and they've combined for a 134 wRC+ over the last month. That's an incredible number.
The 2018 Dodgers are an interesting comp. They led the NL with a 111 wRC+, including a 134 mark over the last 30 days of the season – just like these surging Cubs. They were also an elite defensive team lacking an elite rotation.
Those Dodgers won a relatively modest 92 games in the regular season but advanced to the World Series. Perhaps the Cubs can, too. While an ace makes life easier, there are different paths through October.
The wild card among wild cards: Padres
If you believe in timing and momentum, believe in the Padres.
For much of the season they have been a confounding team, much like their face of the franchise, Fernando Tatis Jr.
Over the last month, the Padres are third in baseball with a 118 wRC+.
Moreover, the pitching has become more interesting – deeper and healthier – at exactly the right time.
Nick Pivetta returned from his long absence to post a 1.93 ERA over three September starts.
Michael King has outperformed peripherals to become a 12-game winner with a 3.03 ERA. Robbie Ray, acquired at the Trade Deadline, gives them another veteran option.
They also have one great postseason advantage: If they can hand a lead over to the bullpen it's lights out with Adrian Morejon and Mason Miller closing out games.
The Padres own the end game, and at no time does that matter more than in October.

item.title: [Dodger Blue] Dodgers manager discusses intriguing postseason roster battle
item.dc:creator: Matt Borelli
item.description: Since being called up from Double-A Tulsa earlier this month as the corresponding move for Shohei Ohtani going on the 15-day injured list, Josue De Paula has done nothing but impress his Los Angeles Dodgers teammates and coaching staff. The top prospect has flashed his elite offensive potential, showing remarkable plate discipline and power while drawing comparisons to New York Mets slugger Juan Soto. With Ohtani returning from the IL on Wednesday, questions remain about De Paula’s role with the
item.content:encoded:
Since being called up from Double-A Tulsa earlier this month as the corresponding move for Shohei Ohtani going on the 15-day injured list, Josue De Paula has done nothing but impress his Los Angeles Dodgers teammates and coaching staff.
The top prospect has flashed his elite offensive potential, showing remarkable plate discipline and power while drawing comparisons to New York Mets slugger Juan Soto.
With Ohtani returning from the IL on Wednesday, questions remain about De Paula’s role with the Dodgers moving forward. But the expectation is that he will compete with Dalton Rushing for the final spot on the team’s postseason roster.
“He’s done a great job,” manager Dave Roberts said of De Paula. “We made the move with Eliezer Alfonzo out on option with Andy (Pages) coming back. With Shohei coming back, I’m just not sure what the counter is going to be. But to your question, Josue has done a fantastic job.”
Rushing has been on the 10-day injured list since Sept. 6 after re-aggravating his right elbow while playing catch. However, he took live batting practice against Will Klein on Tuesday and should be activated in the coming days.
That would give Rushing only a few games to show the Dodgers he is back up to game speed and deserving of a spot on their postseason roster.
“Dalton, taking his at-bats. The thought is to give him an opportunity at some point in time to get activated and see how it looks coming off the bench,” Roberts said. “So I’m not sure if that’s tomorrow, Thursday, Friday, something like that.”
Rushing was in the midst of a breakout season before the right elbow injury threw him off course, so it will be interesting to see which direction the Dodgers decide to take.
Dodgers postseason roster battle
The Dodgers will consider several factors when choosing between De Paula and Rushing for the final spot on their postseason roster, including the ability to put together a good at-bat, not chasing pitches out of the strike zone and power.
“Quality of at-bat, conducting an at-bat, the ability to swing at strikes, take balls, get on base, get a hit,” Roberts explained. “There’s potential slug with both those guys. It’s going to be a good debate.
“I think hitting off the bench is very difficult, and you’re just trying to figure out who gives us the best chance. To be quite frank, it’s going to be tougher for Dalton given the time that he’s missed. To kind of think that you have three games to get back into playoff form, it’s tough to do. It’s not a knock on him. He’s been great for us, but it’s still tough.
“And also when you’re talking about having the consistency of at-bats recently from Josue. But again, we have to have those conversations and make a decision.”

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] How Can Dodgers Legally Get Josue De Paula On Postseason Roster?
item.dc:creator: Aaliyan Mohammed
item.description: In an unprecedented move in the Andrew Friedman era, the Los Angeles Dodgers called up a position player directly from Double-A earlier this month: Josue De Paula. item.content:encoded:
In an unprecedented move in the Andrew Friedman era, the Los Angeles Dodgers called up a position player directly from Double-A earlier this month: Josue De Paula.
De Paula is not a good defender, but his bat is off the charts. He has a great eye at the plate and dominated in Double-A. Still, the big leagues are a whole different thing. That has not seemed to bother De Paula, who has a 1.081 OPS in 11 games with 11 walks and just five strikeouts.
De Paula has gotten to serve as the designated hitter with Shohei Ohtani out, but that's about to change. His defense is not good enough to start in left field, and the Dodgers are not going to start him over Andy Pages, Teoscar Hernández or Kyle Tucker right now. However, he would still be a very valuable bat for the postseason, with the ability to get on base at a high clip.
There's one big problem, however. He was not on the 40-man roster on Sept. 1, which is the eligibility cutoff for the postseason. The Dodgers can still legally get De Paula on a postseason roster, but will need to petition the commissioner's office.
"A player who doesn't meet said criteria for postseason eligibility can still be added to a team's roster in the postseason via petition to the Commissioner's Office if the player was in the organization on Aug. 31 and is replacing someone who is on the injured list and has served the minimum amount of time required for activation," read Major League Baseball's rules for postseason eligibility. "(For example, a player on the 10-day injured list who has been on it for at least 10 days, or a player who has been on the 60-day injured list for at least 60 days.) Players who are acquired in September or after are ineligible."
De Paula is good on the first need, but the Dodgers would have to say he's replacing Dalton Rushing, who is the only current Dodger who has exceeded a minimum stay on the injured list. This would make sense, as Rushing may not be able to catch anyway and would be used as a pinch hitter. De Paula can fill that role.
More MLB: Dodgers' Freddie Freeman Explains Why Dodgers Need Bye This Year

item.description:

item.content:encoded:
Field Level Media

23 Sep 2026, 19:49 GMT+10

(Photo credit: Jayne Kamin)
Shohei Ohtani is expected to be back in the starting lineup Wednesday, Yoshinobu Yamamoto will be on the mound and the Los Angeles Dodgers will accelerate their playoff preparations in a home game against the San Diego Padres.
Ohtani last played Sept. 7, one day after he struck out a season-high four times, and has been on the injured list with right biceps discomfort ever since.
With five regular-season games remaining, Ohtani will get a chance to build some momentum for the postseason.
'Unless I hear otherwise, he'll be in the lineup,' said Dodgers manager Dave Roberts, who admitted that the team's leading home-run hitter with 30 is about an '8 or 9' on a health scale of 1-10.
Where to put Ohtani in the lineup is another question. Normally the Dodgers' leadoff hitter, Mookie Betts has made the top spot his own lately.
With the Padres set to start left-hander Robbie Ray, the right-handed Betts likely is to hit leadoff Wednesday, while Ohtani could be in his former No. 2 spot. Betts went 1-for-4 with an RBI and a run scored in Tuesday's 7-0 victory over the Padres and is batting .366 since the start of September.
Yamamoto (14-8, 2.51 ERA) has looked like an ace all season and has been at his best of late by going 3-1 with a 1.79 ERA over his last seven starts. The right-hander is 3-3 with a 3.76 ERA in seven career starts against San Diego.
The Dodgers (97-60) increased their home winning streak to 11 games and reduced their magic number to two for clinching a bye through the wild-card round. They also pulled within a game of the National League-leading Milwaukee Brewers (98-59).
Los Angeles center fielder Andy Pages returned from a broken hand on Tuesday and reached base twice.
'Obviously being out for a month, I'm not feeling all that great or familiar at the plate but there are things from the Trajekt (pitching machine) that helped me come back,' Pages said through a team interpreter.
The Padres' magic number for clinching a wild-card spot remained at two after Tuesday's loss.
Ray (13-8, 3.60) pitched well immediately after he was acquired from the San Francisco Giants at the trade deadline but has an 8.78 ERA over his past three starts. He is 3-2 with a 5.22 ERA in eight starts for San Diego.
In 26 career starts against the Dodgers, tied for his most against any club, Ray is 9-9 with a 3.81 ERA.
The Padres (87-70) entered Tuesday's series opener against the Dodgers with 13 victories in their previous 14 games but failed to find much offense as Los Angeles went to a bullpen game and used eight pitchers.
It was the second time since the All-Star break the Padres were held without a run.
San Diego also is expected to activate right-hander Jason Adam following a shoulder injury as he rejoins one of the major league's best bullpens. Adam is 2-2 with a 2.51 ERA in 36 relief appearances but has not pitched in a big-league game since June 29.
'Yeah, more than ready,' Adam said, according to the San Diego Union-Tribune. 'I feel 100% ready.'
Padres manager Craig Stammen was guarded with the team's plans.
'It's good to see him back pitching in his normal way,' Stammen said. 'Hopefully we'll have him activated before the season ends.'
--Field Level Media

item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers star Shohei Ohtani will make his return to the lineup tonight (Wednesday, September 23) against the San Diego Padres. The Dodgers have activated the two-way standout from the 15-day injured list after he took time to rest his nagging knee and biceps injuries. Ohtani will serve as the designated hitter for the remainder of the regular season and playoffs, as he is currently unable to pitch.
Ohtani's return comes at a crucial time for the Dodgers, who are looking to solidify their position in the National League West. According to MLB.com, Dodgers manager Dave Roberts confirmed that Ohtani is now in a better physical state, rating him an "eight or a nine" on a scale of one to ten. Ohtani has been progressing well in his hitting, having taken 30-40 swings off a Trajekt machine, which simulates real pitchers.
Despite his recent struggles at the plate, Ohtani remains a key player for the Dodgers. Before his injuries, he recorded a .902 OPS and hit a team-leading 30 home runs. In his last 24 games before going on the injured list, Ohtani hit .198 with 34 strikeouts. ABC7 reported that Roberts plans to play Ohtani in every remaining game to help him reacclimate to major league pitching.
The Dodgers have managed to maintain a strong record in Ohtani's absence, going 13-3 in the last 16 games. As they prepare for the playoffs, Ohtani's return as a designated hitter is expected to bolster their lineup. The Dodgers are also considering roster adjustments, with outfield prospect Josue De Paula potentially being sent down to make room for Ohtani.
For tonight's game, the Dodgers will face the Padres with right-handed pitcher Yoshinobu Yamamoto on the mound. The game will be broadcast on SportsNet LA and available on the MLB app.

I’m just happy I got hits w
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES, CA — Freddie Freeman delivered three RBI in the Dodgers’ 7-0 win over the Padres on Tuesday night, continuing his recent rebound at the plate. After struggling through much of September, the veteran first baseman appears to be finding his stroke just as the postseason approaches. Following the game, Freeman talked about his recent improvement, the Dodgers’ increasingly healthy lineup and the importance of securing a first-round bye.
“It’s a little better. I’m just happy I got hits when I needed to get hits. Today and the last couple of games have been a lot better, so hopefully we’re trending in the right direction when we need to.”
Freeman is also encouraged by what he’s seeing from the rest of the lineup, particularly with Andy Pages back from his hand injury and Shohei Ohtani expected to return Wednesday.
“It’s been really good. You’ve got guys swinging the bat who got off to tough starts. Kyle’s been great. Teo’s been hot. Guys are starting to come back that we’ve been missing over the last couple of weeks, too. It’s good to see Andy back, and Sho coming back tomorrow. A lot of good things happening for the offense lately.”
With the Dodgers’ magic number for clinching the National League’s second seed down to one, Freeman has his sights set on getting that job done.
“I feel like we’ve just been playing really good baseball as a group lately as well. We had to step up when guys went down, and that’s a credit to the guys that have been going. You want to be playing well going into the playoffs. We need one more win for that bye. That’s what we need. We need that, get some rest, and then have a great week of practicing going into the playoffs. Guys are swinging the bats at the right time, and hopefully we can carry that.”
Asked why the first-round bye is particularly important for this year’s club, Freeman laughed.
“I think we all know why it’s important. There’s a lot of us kind of limping toward the end here. A lot of aches and pains this year. It’s good to get those guys back on the field and get some at-bats in them, then rest up and get some more at-bats during the live sessions and whatever we do during that week to get us ready for Saturday.”

item.dc:creator: Matt Larter
item.description: One of the MLB's top teams, the Los Angeles Dodgers face an interesting lineup decision with Shohei Ohtani set to return from the injured list Wednesday. Ohtani has missed a little more than a week after being placed on the 15-day IL with a biceps issue, but Dodgers manager Dave Roberts announced Tuesday that the superstar will be activated. Ohtani has been the Dodgers' regular leadoff hitter throughout the season. However, his absence has given Mookie Betts an opportunity to bat first, and the
item.content:encoded:
One of the MLB's top teams, the Los Angeles Dodgers face an interesting lineup decision with Shohei Ohtani set to return from the injured list Wednesday.
Ohtani has missed a little more than a week after being placed on the 15-day IL with a biceps issue, but Dodgers manager Dave Roberts announced Tuesday that the superstar will be activated.
Ohtani has been the Dodgers' regular leadoff hitter throughout the season. However, his absence has given Mookie Betts an opportunity to bat first, and the veteran has taken full advantage.
Betts finding his stride
Jul 25, 2026; New York City, New York, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers shortstop Mookie Betts (50) throws out New York Mets third baseman Bo Bichette (not pictured) on a ground ball during the ninth inning at Citi Field. Mandatory Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images
Roberts said Tuesday that, "as of now," Ohtani will return to the leadoff spot. However, he also acknowledged that the Dodgers are considering a platoon at the top of the batting order.
Under that scenario, Ohtani would lead off against right-handed pitchers, while Betts would move into the top spot against left-handers.
There is a case for keeping Betts in the role, at least against certain matchups. Ohtani has struggled recently, batting .139/.262/.222 with two extra-base hits and no RBIs over his last nine games.
Betts, meanwhile, has been outstanding since moving to the top of the order. During Ohtani's absence, the 33-year-old went 9-for-16 with four doubles, two home runs and six RBIs across four games.
Dodgers face a tough choice
Betts has only batted leadoff in six games this season, but his recent production has made the decision more complicated for Roberts and the Dodgers.
His September numbers have been particularly impressive. Betts is hitting .373/.468/.746 with 13 extra-base hits and 20 RBIs over 17 games this month, showing the type of production the Dodgers were hoping to get from him after a difficult season.
The Dodgers have plenty of flexibility because of the depth throughout their lineup, and their record gives them some breathing room. Los Angeles enters Wednesday at 97-60, comfortably leading the National League West and sitting just one game behind the Milwaukee Brewers for the best record in the National League.
The Dodgers will face the San Diego Padres in the second game of their three-game series Wednesday, with five games remaining in the regular season. The return of Ohtani could give Los Angeles another major boost, but it also leaves Roberts with an intriguing decision at the top of his lineup.

item.dc:creator: Aaliyan Mohammed

They've shown they can win both ways, but a bye this year is a little more important. The Dodgers stars are only getting older, and with age comes wear and tear. The team has been pretty banged up, and it's no secret that they want the extra rest. "I think we all know why it's important," first baseman Freddie Freeman said, per Sporting Tribu
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers won the World Series in 2024 with a first-round bye, and won it last year as the Nol. 3 seed, having to play in a Wild Card Series.
They've shown they can win both ways, but a bye this year is a little more important. The Dodgers stars are only getting older, and with age comes wear and tear. The team has been pretty banged up, and it's no secret that they want the extra rest.
"I think we all know why it's important," first baseman Freddie Freeman said, per Sporting Tribune's Fredo Cervantes. "There's a lot of us kind of limping toward the end here. A lot of aches and pains this year."
Freeman is not kidding when he talks about the Dodgers "limping" to the finish line, even though he said it while chuckling. Shohei Ohtani is currently on the injured list, Freeman is playing through some knee issues, Andy Pages just got back in the lineup after a fractured hand and Blake Snell exited his last start after just one inning.
Not to mention the normal wear and tear a 162-game season takes on players. The Dodgers have the oldest lineup in baseball, and they could use a bye more than anyone. Not getting the bye would mean a date with either San Diego, Chicago, Philadelphia or Arizona in a best-of-three series.
Any of those matchups would be much tougher than the matchup the Dodgers had against the Cincinnati Reds in the Wild Card last year. Any one of those teams could upset the Dodgers in a Wild Card Series. However, it's hard to imagine a team coming out of a tough Wild Card Series and beating a rested Dodgers squad with its pitching lined up.

item.title: [Just Baseball] The Dodgers' Max Muncy Continues To Be Underrated | Just Baseball
item.dc:creator: Clay Snowden
item.description: Los Angeles, California. The city of movie stars, names and big personalities. Oh yeah, and championships, with the two most recent going to the Dodgers. When you think about the Los Angeles Dodgers, the names that come to mind are Shohei, Tarik, Yoshinobu, and Mookie. Not Max. No, he’s not the typical profile to win an MVP; he doesn’t have the flair that matches the city, and maybe consiste
item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles, California. The city of movie stars, names and big personalities. Oh yeah, and championships, with the two most recent going to the Dodgers. When you think about the Los Angeles Dodgers, the names that come to mind are Shohei, Tarik, Yoshinobu, and Mookie.
Not Max.
For one reason or another, Max Muncy has been an underappreciated player in this league for far too long. No, he’s not the typical profile to win an MVP; he doesn’t have the flair that matches the city, and maybe consistency just isn’t sexy.
But, remove Max Muncy from the Los Angeles Dodgers, and this season, along with their recent history, looks different.
Stats from prior to games on Sept. 20, 2026.
Muncy’s Importance in 2026
Although the Dodgers easily clinched another NL West title, I think it’s fair to say their season has not gone quite as planned. Crazy, right? When you have their amount of star power and top prospects, and you acquire Tarik Skubal at the deadline, anything less than the best record in baseball isn’t good enough.
Part of the reason why the Dodgers have not reached the extremely high expectations many placed on them is injuries. Shohei Ohtani, Will Smith, Roki Sasaki, Andy Pages, Dalton Rushing, Edwin Díaz, Tyler Glasnow, Blake Snell, and others all missed significant time on the IL.
Combine that IL time with Kyle Tucker’s ho-hum season and Mookie Betts not being quite the player he once was at the plate, and you can see why the Dodgers don’t quite look like an unstoppable force.
With so many injuries and inconsistencies in the lineup, the Dodgers needed Max Muncy more than ever. Even at 36 years old, Muncy is having an amazing season. He is slashing .254/.351/.500 with 29 home runs and a 132 wRC+, second on the team only to Ohtani’s 142 wRC+. Muncy’s 4.3 fWAR is first amongst Dodgers position players. Yes, that includes Ohtani.
He’s currently on pace to either match or surpass his career high of 4.5 fWAR from the 2021 season when he hit 36 home runs. If he doesn’t quite get to 4.5, 4.4 would tie his second-best season, which came in 2019 in the juiced-ball era. Yeah, I’d say Muncy’s doing pretty well.
After being such a consistent and healthy player throughout the beginning part of his career, Muncy missed parts of the last two seasons due to injury. Returning from injury to play over 140 games, and at this high of a level, goes to show what type of talent he is.
On the current roster, Muncy is one of three players with more than 20 home runs. Keep in mind, Ohtani also has more than 20, but he is on the IL. Muncy’s 29 home runs place him in the top 20 in all of baseball. We still saw his power in his injury-riddled seasons in 2024 and 2025, but seeing it return to this level has been a massive boost for the Dodgers.
Kyle Tucker was seen as a middle-of-the-order bat who could push Muncy down a spot, but as it has turned out, Muncy is more important than ever. Sure, this team would still have topped 90 wins without Muncy, but the lineup would feel much different. The hole created at third base would be filled by Miguel Rojas or Enrique Hernández, which is far from ideal. The drop-off from Muncy to whoever the replacement was would have been massive.
As you look ahead to the postseason, there are still questions around the Dodgers’ lineup. Pages recently returned from the IL, and Ohtani will soon, giving the Dodgers a much-needed boost. Pages adds another righty bat into the lineup and allows Tommy Edman to move back to the infield. Ohtani fills DH, which is currently held down by rookie Josue De Paula.
Muncy adds another veteran back with postseason experience. A .817 OPS and 16 career postseason home runs give the Dodgers another threat once the weather cools and the games become more important.
Yes, Muncy has been crucial to the Dodgers’ success this season. But you could really say that about his entire career.
Muncy’s Consistent Excellence
Let’s start back at the beginning. Max Muncy started with the Oakland Athletics before being released in 2017 and signing a minor league contract with the Dodgers. He debuted in LA in 2018, immediately finding success, slashing .263/.391/.582 with 35 home runs. From an Oakland castoff to hitting 35 home runs a year later was impressive, but it was just the beginning.
Muncy followed in 2019, repeating his 35-home run season, a mark he has posted four times since joining the Dodgers. Power has been an important part of his game, and so has consistency. From 2018 through 2023, Muncy logged at least 135 games each year, excluding the COVID season.
Of those six seasons, three were at 130 wRC+ or better, and five were over 100. Really, the only subpar season of his career came in 2020, when he had a 98 wRC+ and 12 home runs in 58 games.
His 2024 and 2025 shortened seasons were still, statistically, some of the best of his career. If we look at it just from a wRC+ standpoint, his 133 wRC+ in 2024 and 137 in 2025 rank in the top four in his career, while 2026 (132 wRC+) lands in the same discussion.
By now, you know what you’re getting with Muncy. Consistent power and one of the best walk rates in the league. His batting average isn’t going to wow anyone, and neither is his defense, although both are adequate in this day and age.
Max Muncy is one of the best Dodgers of all time, and you might not even realize it. His 238 career home runs rank fifth in Dodger history. He ranks seventh in walks, roughly 100 behind Jackie Robinson. Only 14 Dodgers have driven in more runs, and by the time Muncy hangs up the cleats, he could be near the top 10.
Year in and year out, Muncy gives the Dodgers exactly what they expect of him. Early in his career, he provided versatility around the diamond. If the team needed a second baseman, he’d play there. When they needed a first baseman in 2021, Muncy was the answer. Now, he’s settled into third base.
Three All-Star appearances and three World Series rings. I’d argue that he deserves more recognition. Not too bad for a guy that they got for next to nothing.
Final Thoughts
I know that the Dodgers have the type of star power that drives jersey sales. Who wouldn’t want to wear an Ohtani jersey? He’s the best player to ever play the game.
However, I wish we would see more Muncy jerseys at Dodger Stadium. In some ways, this might be a “you don’t know what you’ve got till it’s gone” situation. Luckily, I think Muncy still has several more productive seasons left. He’s not showing signs of slowing down.
If you placed Max Muncy into a number of other cities, he would be their star. I guess it’s easy to get lost in Hollywood, which has over 2,800 of them.

Freddie Freeman led the charge, going 2-for-4 with three RBIs in an offense that produced nine hits and four walks against one of the best pitching staffs in the National League. item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers dismantled the San Diego Padres 7-0 on Tuesday night at Dodger Stadium. Freddie Freeman led the charge, going 2-for-4 with three RBIs in an offense that produced nine hits and four walks against one of the best pitching staffs in the National League.
The Dodgers are 97-60. Their magic number to clinch a first-round playoff bye is one. A win over the Padres on Wednesday or an Atlanta Braves loss to the Reds gets them there.
For most teams, a bye is a nice bonus. For these Dodgers, Freeman made clear it is something far more necessary than that.
Freeman’s Candid Assessment
Freeman was asked after Tuesday’s win why securing the bye matters so much to this team.
“I think we all know why it’s important,” Freeman said. “There’s a lot of us kind of limping toward the end here. A lot of aches and pains this year.”
The Dodgers have dealt with injuries at nearly every position this season. Shohei Ohtani just spent two weeks on the injured list with knee, biceps, and neck issues. Andy Pages missed a month with a fractured hand. Blake Snell has been building back from his own absence. Tyler Glasnow has never made it through a full regular season without an injury since joining the organization.
What the Bye Provides
The Dodgers have won the World Series in each of the last two seasons. They know how October works. They also know what happens when a team enters the postseason at less than full strength.
A first-round bye would give the Dodgers nearly a week off before the Division Series. It allows pitchers to reset their arms. It allows hitters coming off the injured list, Ohtani and Pages, to get additional at-bats in intrasquad games rather than jumping straight into a high-leverage series.
Freeman’s three-RBI performance on Tuesday was a reminder that the lineup is dangerous when everyone is healthy and clicking. Will Smith and Tommy Edman each homered. Mookie Betts added an RBI double. Kyle Tucker picked up a hit. The pieces are there. The question is whether they can stay on the field long enough to use them.
“We’re playing good baseball,” Freeman said. “We need to carry it on for the next five games.”
Final Word for the Dodgers
The Dodgers are built to win another championship. The talent is there. The pitching is there. The experience is there. What they need now is time. Time to heal. Time to reset. And time to arrive at the postseason as close to full strength as possible.
One more win and the bye is theirs. Freeman made the case for why nothing matters more right now.

item.content:encoded:
The Dodgers received two key reinforcements making their returns from injury on Tuesday, as both Andy Pages and Roki Sasaki played a factor into the team’s 7-0 shutout win over the San Diego Padres.
The Dodgers are preparing to get the final Infinity Stone added to their gauntlet, as two-way superstar Shohei Ohtani is expected to return from the injured list for Wednesday’s game against San Diego. Whether Ohtani will remain in the leadoff spot in the starting lineup is still up in the air, as Mookie Betts has been swinging a red-hot bat at the leadoff spot in his absence, per Sonja Chen of MLB.com.
“I do think I should think through the Mookie vs. left situation, but I have to think about the entire lineup structure,” Roberts said. “That’s probably the way it’s going to fall out, but I haven’t totally decided yet.”
Roki Sasaki made his first bullpen appearance since the 2025 World Series on Tuesday, as he logged a scoreless top of the fourth inning while allowing just one hit and striking out two.
Although Sasaki has vastly improved in the second half this season before suffering a blister to his pitching hand— 5.33 ERA in first half, 2.97 ERA in second half— the plan is to once again have him out of the bullpen for the postseason for a second consecutive year, per Chen.
“It’s just showing that whatever it takes to help us win, knowing that any inning he throws in the postseason is going to be huge,” manager Dave Roberts said. “He clearly understands that.”
Josue De Paula is making a strong case for making the postseason roster, as the 21-year-old rookie is slashing .323/.500/.581 while becoming the first Dodger rookie with at least a .500 on-base percentage over his first 11 games since Corey Seager in 2015.
De Paula has spent the bulk of his time in the big leagues serving as the designated hitter, filling the void Ohtani left behind. With Ohtani expected to return from the injured list on Wednesday, the next test for De Paula is to see how he can handle himself in the outfield defensively, per Maddie Lee of the Los Angeles Times.
“All the reports that we’ve gotten from our minor-league staff are right on cue,” Ebel said. “He’s been working, he’s bringing it right here to the major leagues. And it’s a pleasure for me, with some energy, coming out early every day — hasn’t missed. We’re working on game situations, ground balls, left, right, right at him, fly balls, shags during BP. So we’re on the right track.”

【MLB】ドジャース 7ー0 パドレス（日本時間23日・ロサンゼルス） ドジャース・大谷翔平投手が、復帰を翌日に控えるなか、思わぬ形で登場した。MLB公式X（旧ツイッター）が22日（日本時間23日）に公開した1枚に“参戦”。チームを代表して現れた大谷に、ファンからは「めちゃかっこいい」と興奮の声があがった。 【実際の投稿】突如登場した大谷翔平…MLBが公開した「球界を代表する6つの顔」 MLB公式が突如公開したのは、すでにポストシーズン進出を決めた6球団を取り上げた特別画像。「究極の栄冠を目指して、あと6チームがその輪に加わる。10月（ポストシーズン）のような時期は他にない。もうすぐやってくる」とコメントが添えられた。進出が決まっているレイズ、ヤンキース、レッドソックス、ドジャース、ブルワーズ、ブレーブスから1人ずつが登場。ドジャースからは大谷が選ばれた。 大谷は15日間の負傷者リスト（IL）入りしているが、23日（同24日）にメジャー復帰が見込まれている。デーブ・ロバーツ監督は22日（同23日）のパドレス戦前、「明日になることを想定している。（異常を知らせる）何か聞かない限り、彼は明日スタメンで出場する」と、23日（同24日）の同戦でスタメン復帰する見通しだと言及。ポストシーズンを見据える中で、いよいよ戦列に戻ってくる。

item.content:encoded:
What Shohei Ohtani's impending return means for Dodgers' lineup
Shohei Ohtani is expected to be activated from the injured list on Wednesday, Sept. 23, manager Dave Roberts told reporters on Tuesday, Sept. 22. If that holds true, it would mean the Los Angeles Dodgers' franchise cornerstone would have five games to ramp up before the start of the postseason.
Ohtani, who has been on the 15-day IL retroactively since Sept. 8 due to lingering issues with his right bicep and left knee, took coach pitch batting practice and went through his normal workout routine on Tuesday ahead of a 7-0 win over the San Diego Padres and according to the Dodgers skipper, he continues to check all the boxes necessary for a return.
"The thought is tomorrow," Roberts told reporters. "Unless I hear otherwise, he'll be in the lineup tomorrow."
The Dodgers have gotten hot in Ohtani's absence, posting an 8-3 record since Sept. 11 – the day he was placed on the IL – and outscoring their opponents 59-28 in that timeframe. They enter Wednesday on a five-game winning streak, have already won the NL West and their magic number to clinch a first-round bye is down to 1. Ohtani will have the opportunity to find his footing in low-stakes games to finish out the regular season. That's huge considering he did not face live pitching in his hitting progression. But what does his impending return mean for the rest of the Dodgers lineup?
Catcher Eliezer Alfonzo was optioned on Tuesday as center fielder Andy Pages made his return. Alex Freeland could be a candidate to get optioned with rookie Josue De Paula, who is in the middle of an impressive "trial run" in his first shot at the big leagues and making a serious push at making the playoff roster. If he does play in October, it would likely be as a lefty bat off the bench.
Dalton Rushing, who has been on the IL since Sept. 6 with right elbow discomfort, is also expected to be activated soon and will battle with De Paula for that spot over the final five games, though Roberts acknowledged that Rushing is at a disadvantage with a small window to show what he can do.
"It’s not a knock on him," Roberts told reporters. "He’s been great for us. but it’s still tough given that also you’re talking about the consistency of at-bats recently from Josue. We have to have those conversations and make a decision."
Whatever the decision ends up being, a red-hot Dodgers offense with Ohtani at the top of it – though Roberts has said he'd consider keeping Mookie Betts batting leadoff against lefties – suddenly makes them one of the toughest matchups this October just when they were looking like they were in their most vulnerable state just weeks ago.

item.content:encoded:
Dodgers extend home winning streak to 11 with shutout of Padres
(Photo credit: William Liang)
Freddie Freeman drove in three runs, Will Smith and Tommy Edman hit home runs and the Los Angeles Dodgers inched closer to the best record in the National League with a 7-0 victory over the visiting San Diego Padres in the opener of a three-game series Tuesday.
Eight Dodgers pitchers held down the red-hot Padres offense in a bullpen game, with Justin Wrobleski (12-5) earning the win. Roki Sasaki struck out two in one inning in his return from a blister issue. The Dodgers extended their home winning streak to 11 games.
Los Angeles fell one game behind the NL-best Milwaukee Brewers and reduced its magic number for a top-two NL spot and a bye into the NL Division Series to one.
Rookie designated hitter Josue De Paula had two hits with a run scored for the Dodgers, with Shohei Ohtani expected to return from a biceps injury as a hitter Wednesday.
Luis Campusano had two hits for the Padres, whose magic number to clinch a playoff spot remained at two. Right-hander Michael King (12-10) gave up five runs on six hits over four innings, his most runs allowed in a start since May 30.
It was just the second loss in 15 games for San Diego, which is close to locking up a third consecutive playoff berth for the first time in franchise history.
The Dodgers took advantage of King's loss of command to start a four-run outburst in the second inning, all with two outs. The Dodgers loaded the bases on two singles and a hit batter, while Edman and Mookie Betts both walked to force in runs.
Freeman followed Betts with a two-run single for a 4-0 lead.
Freeman added a run-scoring single in the fourth inning, while Edman hit a home run in the sixth and Smith hit his in the seventh. Edman homered for the second straight game, while Smith went deep in his third consecutive start.
'The Dodgers welcomed back Andy Pages from a broken left hand, and he was hit by a pitch and drew a walk in four plate appearances.
--Field Level Media

item.content:encoded:
Shohei Ohtani to return from IL Wednesday, but Dodgers still have unanswered questions in final week
- Click here to listen to this article
-
The Dodgers have less than a week left of the regular season to round into playoff form. And their roster moves this series reflect that time crunch.
Manager Dave Roberts confirmed Tuesday afternoon that Shohei Ohtani (right biceps, left knee) was on track to be reinstated from the 15-day injured list on Wednesday. Ohtani is feeling “considerably” better than he was before the IL stint, according to Roberts.
“I would say if he was a five, he’s probably an eight or a nine right now,” Roberts said before eight pitchers led the Dodgers’ 7-0 win against the San Diego Padres.
On Tuesday, they returned two other important postseason pieces, reinstating center fielder Andy Pages (fractured left hand) and right-hander Roki Sasaki (right middle finger blister) from the injured list.
In corresponding moves, the Dodgers optioned right-hander Emmet Sheehan and catcher Eliézer Alfonzo to triple-A Oklahoma City.
Sasaki took the fourth inning of the bullpen game and threw scoreless ball. He gave up a pair of singles, but his fastball had a little extra life in the short stint, averaging 98.7 mph and topping out at 101.7.
Pages went 0 for 2 but reached base twice, on a hit by pitch and a walk.
Even as players return, however, there are still questions the Dodgers have to answer in the last week of the season:
Where will Ohtani hit?
At least at first, Roberts plans to write Ohtani in at the top of the order, per usual. But shortstop Mookie Betts has entered the conversation.
“Certainly versus right-handed pitching [Ohtani] will be there,” Roberts said. “I do think I should think through the Mookie versus left situation, but I have to think about the entire lineup structure.”
Ohtani has hit leadoff in every game he’s started this year. But he hit No. 2 in 79 games the two previous seasons combined.
Even without Ohtani, the Dodgers lineup has been clicking. On Tuesday, Tommy Edman hit his second home run in as many games, and Will Smith homered for the third time in four days.
Is the rotation healthy?
Dodgers left-hander Blake Snell, who exited his start last week with left groin tightness, threw a bullpen on Tuesday. He’s scheduled for one final regular-season start Saturday, Roberts said.
That means all four of the Dodgers’ projected playoff starters are lined up to pitch this Wednesday through Saturday, with Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Tyler Glasnow on the mound for the last two games against the Padres, and Tarik Skubal and Snell in the first two games in San Francisco.
Who is the closer?
In short, it could change by the day.
“In a perfect world, as we all know the world’s not perfect, I would love [a set closer],” Roberts said. “I think if there’s an opportunity, for example, for Tanner [Scott] to pitch a high-leverage inning in the seventh or the eighth inning, it’s just hard to pass that up if he’s the best option right there. Because you just don’t know where the ninth inning is going to be.
“Those are things that you have to kind of toil with, and those are always good things for people to debate. Right now I don’t see a one-person closer.”
Sasaki stepped into that role last year. It’s unclear exactly how Roberts will use him this time around, but Roberts said he could be an option, depending on how he pitches coming off the IL.
“Last year it was one of those things where it was a situation of need, as far as where we were at with performance and health and guys,” Roberts said. “He filled that role admirably.”
Who gets the last bench spot?
The battle to serve as the left-handed bat off the bench in the postseason has come down to rookie Josue De Paula and injured catcher Dalton Rushing (right flexor strain). But with Rushing still on the IL, De Paula appears to have an edge.
Don’t read too much into the Dodgers’ corresponding move for Ohtani on Wednesday. If they option De Paula 10 days out from the first game of the National League Division Series, he can still be included on the roster.
The Dodgers will have to make another roster move later in the week, when they plan to activate Rushing. If they option a player to make room for Rushing, that player would only be eligible for the start of the NLDS as the corresponding transaction for an IL move.

item.title: [New York Post] Dodgers shutout of Padres reveals potential (and unexpected) playoff strength
item.dc:creator: Jack Harris
item.description: Last year, the Dodgers hardly used their bullpen in the playoffs. This year, they would like that to once again be the blueprint. item.content:encoded:
Last year, the Dodgers hardly used their bullpen in the playoffs.
This year, they would like that to once again be the blueprint.
In their bid to three-peat as World Series champions, of course, the Dodgers are expected to be led by their star-studded rotation. Shohei Ohtani isn’t pitching, but Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow are.
And if all goes according to plan, they will handle the bulk of the innings.
However, replicating the starting pitching excellence of last October won’t be easy. A season ago, the Dodgers’ four-man rotation of Ohtani, Yamamoto, Snell and Glasnow accounted for 113 of the team’s 165 postseason innings (including relief appearances from Glasnow and Yamamoto). Together, they posted a 2.55 ERA.
It was historic production.
Which also means, it’s fair to assume some regression will be possible –– both in workload and effectiveness.
Thus, having more reliable bullpen options this time around could be equally important for the Dodgers. And while that might have felt like a daunting reality earlier this year, when the unit was banged up and struggling through the middle portion of the campaign, Tuesday night was a reminder that the relief corps could be a strength in this fall’s title pursuit.
“Obviously we’ve had a lot of talent over the years,” manager Dave Roberts said. “But as far as sitting here today at the end of the season, it’s as good of shape as we’ve ever been in with the bullpen.”
In a 7-0 win over the San Diego Padres, the Dodgers were not supposed to have the pitching matchup –– countering Padres ace Michael King with a makeshift bullpen game in a rivalry series opener at Dodger Stadium.
Instead, eight different Dodgers relievers held the previous red-hot Padres to a five-hit shutout. Along the way, several arms who once seemed like question marks continued to round into increasingly promising form.
“It was fantastic,” Roberts said. “This is as good as our bullpen has been, has thrown.”
It started with opener Brock Stewart, a key right-handed weapon in the Dodgers’ bullpen who began the game with a scoreless first inning, continuing his late-season resurgence after another injury-plagued year.
From there, the baton was passed on down.
Justin Wrobleski, who is in the midst of a late-season conversion to the bullpen for the second-straight year, escaped a jam in the second. Blake Treinen, who might be on the postseason roster bubble given the Dodgers’ relief depth, offered one of his best outings of late by issuing only a two-out walk in a scoreless third.
